verses.text:
He said to them, “You set aside God’s commandment very well indeed, so that you may establish your tradition!
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Let whoever speaks evil of father or mother surely die.’
But you say, ‘If a person says to his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban”—that is, a gift—’
you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother,
making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. You do many similar things.”

He answered them, “Why do you also transgress God’s commandment because of your tradition?
For God said, ‘Honor father and mother,’ and ‘Whoever reviles father or mother must surely die.’
But you say, ‘Whoever tells his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is a gift,”
will certainly not honor his father.’ You have thus nullified the word of God because of your tradition.
Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied well about you, saying,
‘This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.
In vain they worship Me, teaching human commandments as teachings.’”
He who reviles his father or his mother shall surely die.

verses.text:
Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.”
When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable.
He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.
He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.
For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”

He summoned the crowd and said to them, “Hear and understand:
what enters the mouth does not defile a person, but what comes out of the mouth—this defiles a person.”
Then the disciples came and said to Him, “Dost Thou know that the Pharisees stumbled when they heard this saying?”
He answered, “Every plant that My heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
Leave them; they are blind guides of the blind. If a blind person guides a blind person, both will fall into a pit.”
Peter answered Him, “Explain this parable to us.”
He said, “Are you also still without understanding?
Do you not understand that everything entering the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled into the latrine?
But the things coming out of the mouth come from the heart, and those defile a person.
For out of the heart come evil reasonings, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, and blasphemies.
These are the things that defile a person, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person.”

verses.text:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Whosoever vows a vow for the valuation of his soul unto the Lord,
the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty didrachmas of silver, by the sacred weight.
For a female the assessed value shall be thirty didrachmas.
From five to twenty years old, the valuation shall be twenty didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
From one month to five years old, the valuation shall be five didrachmas of silver for a male and three didrachmas for a female.
From sixty years old and upward, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; the priest shall value him according to the strength of the hand of the one who vowed.

For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.text:
If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her, and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions which she imposed upon her soul shall stand against her.
But if her husband utterly annuls them on the day he hears, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions upon herself shall not remain against her. Her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will cleanse her.
Every vow and every oath imposing a restriction to afflict her soul—her husband may establish it, or her husband may annul it.
But if he remains utterly silent toward her from day to day, he shall establish all her vows, and he shall establish the restrictions upon her, because he kept silence toward her on the day when he heard.
But if he annuls them after the day on which he heard, he shall bear his sin.

But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.
If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her, and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions which she imposed upon her soul shall stand against her.

But if her husband utterly annuls them on the day he hears, then whatever came from her lips concerning her vows and the restrictions upon herself shall not remain against her. Her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will cleanse her.
Every vow and every oath imposing a restriction to afflict her soul—her husband may establish it, or her husband may annul it.

But if he remains utterly silent toward her from day to day, he shall establish all her vows, and he shall establish the restrictions upon her, because he kept silence toward her on the day when he heard.
But if he annuls them after the day on which he heard, he shall bear his sin.

paragraphs: Study 12: Circumcision in Abraham’s covenant
Related indexed requirements: C0036. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — covenant belonging and circumcision
Connection to Christ: Acts and Galatians explicitly reject requiring circumcision for Gentile salvation.

Christian response today: Belong to Christ in faith, receive his call to baptism and live in love; do not require physical circumcision for salvation or condemn someone for their existing circumcised or uncircumcised status.
Saints Translation — Law: Genesis 17:10–14 Christ and the apostles: Acts 15:1–11 · Galatians 5:2–6 · 1 Corinthians 7:18–19
Ancient covenant practice: Circumcision marks Abraham’s male descendants and household within the covenant.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Acts rejects circumcision as a requirement for Gentile salvation. Paul describes circumcision of the heart, a circumcision not made by hands, and burial and resurrection with Christ in baptism. Faith working through love is decisive.
Saints Translation support: Acts 15:1–11 · Romans 2:28–29 · Colossians 2:11–12 · Galatians 5:6 · 1 Corinthians 7:18–19
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament treatment; the connection with baptism is explicit, while sacramental applications differ.

Read carefully: This does not make Jews or Jewish covenant practice inferior. Colossians connects circumcision and baptism without settling every Christian disagreement about baptism or covenant membership.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Circumcision on the eighth day is the covenant sign commanded for Abraham’s male descendants and household. The New Testament explicitly addresses its application to Gentiles: it must not be required for salvation or treated as the basis of righteousness. The historical command remains Scripture without becoming a compulsory Christian initiation rite.

And you shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

And every male child among you, eight days old, shall be circumcised throughout your generations, the slave born in your house, and the slave bought with silver from any foreigner who is not of your seed.
The slave born in your house, and the slave bought with silver, shall surely be circumcised; and My covenant shall be upon your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be destroyed from his kindred; for he has broken My covenant.”
Some men came down from Judea and taught the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.”

When Paul and Barnabas had a serious disagreement and debate with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some others from among them to go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem about this question.
Sent on their way by the Church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.
When they arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the Church, the apostles, and the elders, and reported all that God had done with them.
But some believers from the party of the Pharisees rose and said, “It is necessary to circumcise them and command them to keep the law of Moses.”
The apostles and the elders gathered to consider this matter.

After much debate, Peter rose and said to them, “Men, brothers, you know that in earlier days God made a choice among you, that through my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the good news and believe.
God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them by giving them the Holy Spirit just as He did to us.
He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
Now, therefore, why are you testing God by placing upon the disciples’ neck a yoke that neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
Rather, we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in the same way as they are.”
Look, I, Paul, tell you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
And I testify again to every man who receives circumcision that he is obligated to do the whole law.
You who seek to be justified by law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen from grace.
For we, by the Spirit, through faith, eagerly await the hope of righteousness.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any strength, but faith working through love.
Was anyone called when already circumcised? Let him not undo his circumcision. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping God’s commandments matters.
For the Jew is not the one outwardly so, nor is circumcision what is outward in flesh;
but the Jew is the one inwardly so, and circumcision is of the heart, in Spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.
in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ,

paragraphs: Study 59: Responsibility for rash oaths
Related indexed requirements: C0410, C0411. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Hebrews’ account of Christ’s once-for-all offering is applied here to the sacrificial element; the responsibility for truthful speech remains.
Christian response today: Confess wrongdoing and speak dependably; do not carry out a harmful promise merely because you made it.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 5:4–6 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12 · Hebrews 10:1–18
Text and setting: Oath and offering law
Torah: Leviticus 5:4–6

Leviticus addresses a rashly spoken oath, recognition of guilt, confession and the prescribed offering. It does not teach that a harmful promise must be carried out merely because it was spoken. Jesus and James call for dependable, truthful speech; repentance must not become an excuse to fulfill an evil intention.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12

Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall fulfil your oaths to the Lord.’
But I tell you: do not swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God,
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of His feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let your word be ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever is beyond these is of evil.
But above all, my brothers, do not swear, either by heaven or by earth or by any other oath. Let your yes be yes, and your no be no, so that you may not fall under judgment.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man or woman solemnly vows a vow of consecration unto the Lord, to be set apart
from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins.
All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
All the days of the vow of purification no razor shall come upon his head. Until the days which he vowed unto the Lord are fulfilled, he shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
All the days of his vow unto the Lord he shall not enter where any dead person is.
For his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister, he shall not defile himself when they die; for the vow of his God is upon him, upon his head.
All the days of his vow he shall be holy unto the Lord.
But if anyone dies suddenly beside him, the head of his vow shall be defiled forthwith. He shall shave his head on the day when he is cleansed; on the seventh day it shall be shaved.
And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons unto the priest, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin in connection with the dead person, and shall consecrate his head on that day,
whereon he was consecrated unto the Lord for the days of the vow. And he shall bring a year-old lamb for a guilt offering; and the former days shall not be reckoned, for the head of his vow was defiled.
And this is the law of him who has vowed: on the day when he fulfils the days of his vow, he shall present his offering at the doors of the Tent of Testimony,
and he shall bring his gift unto the Lord: one unblemished year-old male lamb for whole burning, and one unblemished year-old ewe lamb for sin, and one unblemished ram for deliverance,
and a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, loaves prepared with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and their sacrifice and their drink offering.
And the priest shall present them before the Lord, and prepare his offering for sin and his whole burnt offering.
And he shall prepare the ram as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest shall prepare its sacrifice and its drink offering.
And he who has vowed shall shave the head of his vow at the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and put the hair upon the fire which is under the sacrifice of deliverance.
And the priest shall take the boiled foreleg from the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them upon the hands of him who has vowed, after he has shaved the hair of his vow.
And the priest shall bring them as a presentation before the Lord. It shall be holy unto the priest, with the breast of presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart; and afterward he who has vowed shall drink wine.
This is the law of him who vows unto the Lord, his gift unto the Lord concerning the vow, apart from whatever his hand may find, according to the extent of his vow which he vows under the law of consecration.

Torah: Numbers 6:1–21

The passage governs a special vow undertaken by a man or woman, with restrictions concerning vine products, hair and contact with the dead, followed by offerings. It does not command every believer to become a Nazirite. Acts records Jewish vow practice; Jesus’ teaching on truthful speech remains necessary when considering vows.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Acts 21:23–26 · Matthew 5:33–37
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Acts records Jewish vow practice; the Nazirite institution is voluntary, and the New Testament does not require it of all Christians.

Where interpretations differ: Vows and their relationship to Jesus’ teaching about swearing. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

verses.text:
And Moses spoke to the rulers of the tribes of Israel, saying: This is the word that the Lord has commanded:
Any person who vows a vow unto the Lord, or swears an oath, or imposes a restriction upon himself, shall not profane his word. He shall do everything that comes from his mouth.
If a woman vows a vow unto the Lord or imposes a restriction while in her father’s house in her youth,
and her father hears her vows and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself, but her father remains silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her father refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall stand. The Lord will cleanse her, because her father refused her.
If she becomes a man’s wife while her vows are upon her, according to the specific statement of her lips by which she imposed a restriction upon herself,
and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain.
But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.
And the vow of a widow or a divorced woman—whatever she vowed concerning herself—shall remain against her.
If her vow was made in her husband’s house, or her restriction was imposed upon herself with an oath,

research.title: Vows, responsibility and household rules
paragraphs: Study 107: Vows, responsibility and household rules
Related indexed requirements: C0826, C0930, C0931, C0932, C0933. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus and James address oath-taking and dependable speech; their teaching must accompany the ancient household rules.
Christian response today: Be truthful and responsible without treating the ancient annulment procedures as blanket control over another adult’s decisions.
Saints Translation — Law: Numbers 30:2–17 (KJV 30:1–16) Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12
Text and setting: Vow law
Torah: Numbers 30:2–17 (KJV 30:1–16)

Numbers treats vows as serious commitments and describes circumstances of household confirmation or annulment in ancient Israel. Those provisions should not be silently transferred into a claim that every modern woman’s decisions require male permission. Christian application must include Jesus’ and James’ insistence on truthful, dependable speech.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 5:33–37 · James 5:12
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Jesus and James address oath-taking and dependable speech; their teaching must accompany the ancient household rules.

Where interpretations differ: Solemn vows and oaths in relation to Jesus’ teaching. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

Leviticus 27:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Leviticus 27:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Whosoever vows a vow for the valuation of his soul unto the Lord,
Leviticus 27:3 — the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty didrachmas of silver, by the sacred weight.
Leviticus 27:4 — For a female the assessed value shall be thirty didrachmas.
Leviticus 27:5 — From five to twenty years old, the valuation shall be twenty didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.
Leviticus 27:6 — From one month to five years old, the valuation shall be five didrachmas of silver for a male and three didrachmas for a female.
Leviticus 27:7 — From sixty years old and upward, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver for a male and ten didrachmas for a female.

Leviticus 27:8 — But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; the priest shall value him according to the strength of the hand of the one who vowed.
Leviticus 27:9 — If it concerns livestock of a kind presented as a gift unto the Lord, whatever one gives from these unto the Lord shall be holy.
Leviticus 27:10 — He shall not exchange it, good for bad or bad for good. If he does exchange it, animal for animal, both it and its substitute shall be holy.
Leviticus 27:11 — If it concerns any unclean livestock of a kind not presented as a gift unto the Lord, he shall set the animal before the priest.
Leviticus 27:12 — And the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
Leviticus 27:13 — If he does redeem it, he shall add a fifth to its valuation.
Leviticus 27:14 — And if a man consecrates his house as holy unto the Lord, the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
Leviticus 27:15 — If the one who consecrated it redeems his house, he shall add a fifth of the silver of the valuation to it, and it shall be his.
Leviticus 27:16 — If a man consecrates unto the Lord part of the field of his possession, the valuation shall be according to its seed: fifty didrachmas of silver for a kor of barley.
Leviticus 27:17 — If he consecrates his field from the year of release, it shall stand according to its valuation.

Leviticus 27:18 — If he consecrates his field later, after the release, the priest shall calculate the silver for him according to the years remaining until the year of release, and a deduction shall be made from its assessment.
Leviticus 27:19 — If the one who consecrated the field redeems it, he shall add a fifth of the silver to its valuation, and it shall be his.
Leviticus 27:20 — If he does not redeem the field and sells the field to another man, he shall no longer redeem it.
Leviticus 27:21 — When the release has passed, the field shall be holy unto the Lord like land set apart. It shall become the priest’s possession.
Leviticus 27:22 — If he consecrates unto the Lord part of a field he acquired, which is not part of the field of his inherited possession,
Leviticus 27:23 — the priest shall calculate for him the total valuation from the year of release, and he shall repay the valuation on that day as holy unto the Lord.
Leviticus 27:24 — And in the year of release the field shall be returned to the man from whom he acquired it, whose possession the land was.
Leviticus 27:25 — And every valuation shall be by sacred weights; the didrachma shall be twenty obols.
Leviticus 27:26 — And every firstborn which is born among your livestock shall belong unto the Lord, and none shall consecrate it; whether calf or sheep, it is the Lord’s.

Leviticus 27:27 — If it is one of the unclean four-footed animals, he shall exchange it according to its valuation and add a fifth to it, and it shall be his. If he does not redeem it, it shall be sold according to its assessed value.

Leviticus 27:28 — But every devoted thing which a man dedicates unto the Lord, of all that he has, from man unto livestock, and from the field of his possession, he shall neither sell nor redeem; every devoted thing shall be most holy unto the Lord.
Leviticus 27:29 — And whatsoever is devoted from among men shall not be redeemed, but shall surely be put to death.
Leviticus 27:30 — Every tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of trees, belongs unto the Lord; it is holy unto the Lord.

This is the covenant that you shall keep between Me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations: every male among you shall be circumcised.
You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.
At eight days old every male child among you shall be circumcised throughout your generations, whether born in your household or bought with money from any foreigner who is not of your offspring.
Both the one born in your household and the one bought with money must surely be circumcised. My covenant shall be upon your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
An uncircumcised male whose foreskin flesh is not circumcised on the eighth day—that person shall be destroyed from his kin; he has scattered My covenant.”

The apostles and the elders gathered to consider this matter.

God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them by giving them the Holy Spirit just as He did to us.
He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
Now, therefore, why are you testing God by placing upon the disciples’ neck a yoke that neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
Rather, we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in the same way as they are.”

verses.text: Cursed is he who takes a bribe to slay an innocent life. And all the people shall say: So be it.
You have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not murder’; and ‘whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.’

But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
If therefore you offer your gift upon the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

Cursed is the man who makes a graven and molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of a craftsman, and sets it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say: So be it.

Cursed is he who perverts the judgment of the sojourner, and of the orphan, and of the widow. And all the people shall say: So be it.

Cursed is he who takes a bribe to slay an innocent life. And all the people shall say: So be it.

Deuteronomy 27:16 — Cursed is he who dishonours his father or his mother. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Deuteronomy 27:17 — Cursed is he who removes his neighbour’s boundaries. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Deuteronomy 27:18 — Cursed is he who leads the blind astray in the way. And all the people shall say: So be it.

Deuteronomy 27:21 — Cursed is he who lies with any beast. And all the people shall say: So be it.

verses.text: And Moses finished speaking all these words unto all the sons of Israel.
And he said unto them, I am a hundred and twenty years old this day; I shall no longer be able to go in and come out. And the Lord said unto me, You shall not cross this Jordan.

The Lord your God, who goes before your face, shall Himself destroy these nations from before your face, and you shall take possession of them; and Joshua shall go before your face, as the Lord has spoken.
And the Lord shall do unto them as He did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, and unto their land, when He destroyed them.
And the Lord delivered them unto you, and you shall do unto them as I commanded you.

Be courageous and strong; fear not, neither be fainthearted, neither be terrified before their face; for the Lord your God, who goes before you, is with you and among you. He will in no wise fail you, neither will He forsake you.

And Moses called Joshua, and said unto him before all Israel, Be courageous and strong; for you shall go before the face of this people into the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers to give unto them, and you shall give it unto them for an inheritance.
And the Lord who goes with you will not fail you, neither will He forsake you; fear not, neither be fainthearted.
And Moses wrote the words of this law in a book, and gave it unto the priests, the sons of Levi, who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and unto the elders of the sons of Israel.
And Moses commanded them in that day, saying, After seven years, at the appointed time of the year of release, at the Feast of the Pitching of Tents,
when all Israel comes together to appear before the Lord your God in the place which the Lord shall choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in their hearing.

Gather the people, the men, and the women, and the children, and the sojourner who is in your cities, that they may hear, and that they may learn to fear the Lord your God; and they shall hearken to do all the words of this law.
And their sons, who do not know, shall hear and learn to fear the Lord your God all the days that they live upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, the days of your death draw near; call Joshua, and stand beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and I will command him. And Moses and Joshua went unto the Tent of Testimony, and stood beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord descended in a cloud, and stood beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony; and the pillar of the cloud stood beside the doors of the Tent.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers; and this people shall arise and go a-whoring after the foreign gods of the land into which it goes; and they shall forsake Me, and break My covenant which I made with them.

And I will be kindled in wrath against them in that day, and will forsake them, and turn My face from them; and the people shall be devoured, and many evils and afflictions shall find it. And it shall say in that day, Because the Lord my God is not within me, these evils have found me.
But I will surely turn My face from them in that day, because of all the wickedness which they have done, for they have turned unto foreign gods.
And now write the words of this song, and teach it unto the sons of Israel, and put it in their mouth, that this song may be a witness for Me among the sons of Israel.

For I will bring them into the good land which I sware unto their fathers to give unto them, a land flowing with milk and honey; and they shall eat, and be filled, and be sated; and they shall turn unto foreign gods, and serve them, and provoke Me, and break My covenant.

And this song shall stand against them, bearing witness before their face; for it shall in no wise be forgotten from their mouth, nor from the mouth of their seed. For I know their wickedness, all that they do here this day, before I bring them into the good land which I sware unto their fathers.
And Moses wrote this song in that day, and taught it unto the sons of Israel.
And Moses commanded Joshua, and said unto him, Be courageous and strong; for you shall bring the sons of Israel into the land which the Lord sware unto them, and He shall be with you.
And when Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book, even unto the end,
he commanded the Levites who bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying,
Take this book of the law, and lay it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God; and it shall be there for a witness against you.
For I know your provocation and your stiff neck; for while I yet live with you this day, you have been provoking God: how much more after my death!
Gather unto me your tribal chiefs, and your elders, and your judges, and your recording officers, that I may speak all these words in their hearing, and call heaven and earth to witness unto them.

For I know that after my death you shall deal utterly lawlessly, and turn aside from the way which I commanded you; and evils shall meet you in the latter days, because you shall do that which is evil before the Lord, to provoke Him to anger by the works of your hands.

And the Lord was kindled with anger against Moses, and said, “Behold, is Aaron the Levite not your brother? I know that he will surely speak to you; and behold, he shall come forth to meet you, and when he sees you, he shall rejoice within himself.
And you shall speak to him, and put My words in his mouth; and I will open your mouth and his mouth, and teach you what you shall do.
And he shall speak for you to the people, and he shall be your mouth; but you shall be for him in matters pertaining to God.
And you shall take in your hand this staff which was turned into a serpent, with which you shall perform the signs.”

verses.text: After the next day Moses sat to judge the people, and all the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.
And when Jethro saw all that he did to the people, he said, “What is this that you do to the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand before you from morning until evening?”
Moses said to his father-in-law, “The people come to me to seek judgment from God.
When they have a dispute and come to me, I judge each case and instruct them in God’s ordinances and His law.”
And Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “You are not doing this rightly.
You shall be worn out with unbearable exhaustion, both you and all this people who are with you; this matter is heavy for you, and you cannot do it alone.
Now therefore listen to me, and I will counsel you, and God shall be with you. Represent the people in matters pertaining to God, and bring their words to God.
And you shall solemnly instruct them in the ordinances of God and His law, and show them the ways in which they shall walk, and the works which they shall do.

And choose for yourself from all the people able men who fear God, righteous men who hate arrogance; and you shall set them over the people as rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, and rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

And they shall judge the people at all times; the weighty matter they shall bring to you, but the lesser judgments they shall judge themselves; and they shall lighten your burden, and bear it with you.
If you do this thing, God shall strengthen you, and you shall be able to stand; and all this people shall come to their own place in peace.”
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did all that he said.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people at all times. They brought every weighty matter to Moses, but judged every light matter themselves.

You shall be worn out with unbearable exhaustion, both you and all this people who are with you; this matter is heavy for you, and you cannot do it alone.
Now therefore listen to me, and I will counsel you, and God shall be with you. Represent the people in matters pertaining to God, and bring their words to God.
And you shall solemnly instruct them in the ordinances of God and His law, and show them the ways in which they shall walk, and the works which they shall do.

And choose for yourself from all the people able men who fear God, righteous men who hate arrogance; and you shall set them over the people as rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, and rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

And they shall judge the people at all times; the weighty matter they shall bring to you, but the lesser judgments they shall judge themselves; and they shall lighten your burden, and bear it with you.
If you do this thing, God shall strengthen you, and you shall be able to stand; and all this people shall come to their own place in peace.”
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did all that he said.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
They judged the people at all times. They brought every weighty matter to Moses, but judged every light matter themselves.

verses.text: Bezalel made the ark.
He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside.
He cast four gold rings for it, two on one side and two on the other.
The rings were wide enough for the carrying poles, so that the ark could be carried with them.
He made the propitiatory cover above the ark of gold.
He made the two gold cherubim,
one cherub at one end of the propitiatory cover and one cherub at its other end,
sheltering the propitiatory cover with their wings.
He made the table of presentation of pure gold.
He cast four rings for it, two on one side and two on the other, wide enough for the poles with which it would be carried.
He made the carrying poles of the ark and of the table, and overlaid them with gold.
He made the table’s utensils of gold: its dishes, incense vessels, ladles, and libation vessels with which to pour drink offerings.
He made the gold lampstand that gives light, with a solid shaft,
and its branches on both sides.
Shoots extended from its branches, three on this side and three on that side, corresponding to one another.

The lamp supports at their ends were nut-shaped and formed from them, as were the fittings on which the lamps would stand. The seventh fitting was at the end of the lamp support, at the top above; it was wholly solid gold.
He made seven gold lamps on it, its gold tongs, and its gold trays.
He overlaid the pillars with silver, cast gold rings for the pillar, and overlaid the bars with gold. He overlaid the pillars of the veil with gold and made gold hooks.
He also made the rings of the tent of gold, and the rings of the court and the rings for stretching the covering overhead of bronze.
He cast the silver capitals of the tent and the bronze capitals of the tent doorway and the gate of the court. He made silver hooks for the pillars; he silvered them.
He made the pegs of the tent and the pegs of the court of bronze.
He made the bronze altar from the bronze censers belonging to the men who had rebelled with the assembly of Korah.
He made all the altar’s utensils: its firepan, its base, its bowls, and its bronze meat forks.

He made a grating for the altar, a work of network beneath its firepan, below it as far as its middle. He put four bronze rings on the four sides of the altar’s grating, wide enough for the bars with which the altar would be carried.
He made the holy anointing oil and the compounded incense, the pure work of a perfumer.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze base from the mirrors of the women who fasted, who fasted at the doors of the Tent of Testimony on the day he set it up.

one drachma per head, half a shekel by the holy shekel, for everyone passing into the enrolment from twenty years old upward: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.

They used the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels for the pillars’ hooks; he gilded their capitals and adorned them.
The bronze of the contribution was seventy talents and one thousand five hundred shekels.

the bases of the court all around, the bases of the court’s gate, the pegs of the tent, and the pegs of the surrounding court,
and the bronze grating of the altar, all the altar’s utensils, and all the equipment of the Tent of Testimony.

Numbers 13:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Numbers 13:2 — Send men for yourself, and let them search out the land of the Canaanites, which I give unto the sons of Israel for a possession. You shall send one man from each tribe, according to the groups of their ancestral families, each a leader among them.
Numbers 13:3 — And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran through the Lord’s voice. All these men were leaders of the sons of Israel.
Numbers 13:4 — And these were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Salamiel son of Zaccur;
Numbers 13:5 — from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Souri;
Numbers 13:6 — from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
Numbers 13:7 — from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
Numbers 13:8 — from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
Numbers 13:9 — from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
Numbers 13:10 — from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
Numbers 13:11 — from the tribe of Joseph, of the sons of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
Numbers 13:12 — from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
Numbers 13:13 — from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
Numbers 13:14 — from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Iabi;
Numbers 13:15 — from the tribe of Gad, Gaddiel son of Machi.
Numbers 13:16 — These were the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses named Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.
Numbers 13:17 — And Moses sent them to search out the land of Canaan, and said unto them: Go up by this wilderness, and you shall go up into the hill country;
Numbers 13:18 — and you shall see the land, what it is, and the people settled upon it, whether they are stronger or weak, whether they are few or many;
Numbers 13:19 — And is the land on which they are settled good or bad? What are the towns in which they live—walled or unwalled?

Numbers 13:20 — And what is the land like—rich or neglected? Are there trees therein or not? And persevere, and you shall take of the fruits of the land. And the days were days of spring, forerunners of the grape harvest.

And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the congregation, saying: Withdraw all around from Korah’s congregation.
And Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and all the elders of Israel went with him.
And he said to the congregation: Separate yourselves from the tents of these stubborn men. Touch none of their possessions, lest you perish with them in all their sin.
And they withdrew from around Korah’s tent. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood beside the entrances of their tents, with their wives, their children, and their baggage.
And Moses said: By this you shall know that the Lord sent me to do all these deeds, and that they did not come from myself.
If these men die the death of all people, and a visitation comes upon them according to the visitation of all people, then the Lord has not sent me.

verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses
and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest: Take up the bronze fire pans from among those burned up, and scatter this strange fire there, for they have consecrated

the fire pans of these sinners at the cost of their lives. Make them into hammered plates as a covering for the altar, because they were presented before the Lord and were made holy, and became a sign to the sons of Israel.
And Eleazar son of Aaron the priest took the bronze fire pans presented by those who had been burned, and they applied them as a covering for the altar,

as a reminder to the sons of Israel that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to place incense before the Lord, so that he will not become like Korah and his faction, as the Lord had spoken through Moses.
And the next day the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the Lord’s people!
And when the congregation banded together against Moses and Aaron, they rushed toward the Tent of Testimony. The cloud covered it, and the Lord’s glory appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came into the area before the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Withdraw from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them all at once. They fell on their faces.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Take the fire pan, put fire from the altar on it, and place incense on it. Carry it quickly into the camp and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from before the Lord; it has begun to strike the people.
And Aaron took it just as Moses had told him and ran into the congregation. The outbreak had already begun among the people. He placed the incense and made atonement for the people,
and stood between the dead and the living, and the outbreak subsided.
And those who died in the outbreak numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, apart from those who died because of Korah.
And Aaron returned unto Moses at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, and the outbreak subsided.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel and take from them one staff for each ancestral house, from all their leaders according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff.
And write Aaron’s name on Levi’s staff, for they shall give one staff for each tribe of their ancestral houses.
And you shall place them in the Tent of Testimony, opposite the testimony, where I will make Myself known unto you.
And the staff of the man I choose shall sprout. I will remove from Myself the sons of Israel’s grumbling, which they direct against you.
And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all their leaders gave him staffs, one staff for each leader according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Aaron’s staff was among their staffs.
And Moses placed the staffs before the Lord in the Tent of Testimony.
And the next day Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Testimony, and there Aaron’s staff for the house of Levi had sprouted: it brought forth a shoot, flowered with blossoms, and produced nuts.
And Moses brought all the staffs out from before the Lord to all the sons of Israel. They looked, and each man took his staff.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Put Aaron’s staff before the testimonies, to be kept as a sign for the sons of the disobedient. Let their grumbling against Me cease, and they shall certainly not die.
And Moses and Aaron did so. Just as the Lord commanded Moses, so they did.
And the sons of Israel said unto Moses: Behold, we are consumed! We are lost! We are utterly spent!
Everyone who touches the Lord’s tent dies. Must we die to the very end?

thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,

and Moses took from the half belonging to the sons of Israel one out of fifty, from the men and from the livestock, and gave them unto the Levites who kept the charges of the Tent of the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.

For now I will stretch out My hand and strike you and your people with death, and you shall be blotted out from the earth.
And for this reason you were preserved, that I might show My strength in you, and that My name might be proclaimed throughout all the earth.

verses.text: When the Lord saw that he was approaching to look, the Lord called to him from the bush, “Moses, Moses!” He replied, “What is it?”
And He said, “Do not come near here. Untie the footwear from your feet; for the place where you stand is holy ground.”
And He said to him, “I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” And Moses turned his face away, for he feared to look before God.
And the Lord said to Moses, “I have surely seen the affliction of My people in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters; for I know their pain.

I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and bring them out of that land into a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
And now, behold, the cry of the sons of Israel has come to Me; and I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
Come now, and I will send you to Pharaoh king of Egypt; and you shall bring My people, the sons of Israel, out of the land of Egypt.”
Moses said to God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt?”
And God said to Moses, “I will be with you; and this shall be the sign to you that I send you: when you have brought My people out of Egypt, you shall serve God upon this mountain.”
And Moses said to God, “Behold, I shall go to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you’; and they shall ask me, ‘What is His name?’ What shall I say to them?”
And God said to Moses, “I am the One Who Is.” And He said, “This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘The One Who Is has sent me to you.’”

And God said again to Moses, “This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is My everlasting name, and My memorial from generation to generation.

Go, therefore, gather the council of elders of the sons of Israel, and say to them, ‘The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, “I have surely visited you, and seen all that has befallen you in Egypt.

And I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of the Egyptians, into the land of the Canaanites, and Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Girgashites, and Hivites, and Jebusites, into a land flowing with milk and honey.”’

And they shall listen to your voice; and you and the council of elders of Israel shall go in to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and you shall say to him, ‘The God of the Hebrews has called us. Let us therefore go a journey of three days into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to our God.’
I know that Pharaoh, king of Egypt, will not let you go unless by a strong hand.
I will stretch out My hand and strike the Egyptians with all My wonders that I will perform among them. Afterward he will send you away.
And I will give this people favour before the Egyptians; and when you depart, you shall not go empty-handed.

Every woman shall ask of her neighbour and of her fellow lodger articles of silver and gold, and clothing; and you shall put them upon your sons and upon your daughters, and you shall plunder the Egyptians.”

And at dawn, the angels urged Lot, saying, “Arise, take your wife and your two daughters whom you have, and depart, so that you do not perish with the lawless deeds of the city.”

And when they had brought them outside, they said, “Save your own life. Do not look behind you or stand anywhere in the surrounding country. Escape to the mountain, so that you are not swept away with them.”
And Lot said to them, “I beg you, lord,
for your servant has found mercy before you, and you have shown me your great righteousness by preserving my life. Yet I cannot escape to the mountain, for calamities may overtake me, and I may die.
Behold, this city is near enough for me to flee to, and it is small. There I shall be saved; is it not small? And my soul shall live.”
And he said to him, “Behold, I have regarded your face in this matter also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
So hurry and be saved there; for I can do nothing until you enter it.” Therefore he called the name of that city Zoar.

verses.text:
Now fear the Lord and serve Him with uprightness and righteousness. Remove the foreign gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.
But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods of your fathers beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But I and my house will serve the Lord, for He is holy.”
The people answered and said, “May it never be that we abandon the Lord to serve other gods.
The Lord our God—He is God. He brought us and our fathers up from Egypt and guarded us on all the way we travelled and among all the nations through whom we passed.
The Lord drove out before us the Amorites and all the nations living in the land. We too will serve the Lord, for He is our God.”
Joshua said to the people, “You cannot serve the Lord, for He is a holy God; and being jealous, He will not forgive your sins and your lawless deeds.
Whenever you forsake the Lord and serve other gods, He shall come upon you and afflict you and consume you in return for the good He has done you.”
The people said to Joshua, “No! We will serve the Lord.”
And Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord to serve Him.
Now remove the foreign gods among you and direct your heart to the Lord, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “The Lord we will serve, and His voice we will obey.”

research.title: The Law and the Prophets
paragraphs: The Lord does not loosen the Law. He gathers it into two commandments and says that everything else hangs on them. The wisdom books call the commandment a lamp, the psalmist loves it, and the prophets ask what the Lord seeks from a human being.

Do not suppose that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish but to fulfill. For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will pass from the Law until everything happens. Therefore, whoever loosens one of these least commandments and teaches people accordingly will be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens. For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of the heavens.

Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one. You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.’

Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law. For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does not work evil toward the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.
The Householder’s Treasure. Every scribe trained for the kingdom brings out of his treasure things new and old.

Son, do not forget my ordinances; let your heart keep my words, for they will add length of life, years of living, and peace to you. Do not let acts of mercy and faithfulness fail you. Fasten them around your neck, and you will find favor. And take thought for good things before the Lord and people.
because the commandment of law is a lamp and a light, and correction and discipline are life’s way,
One who turns his ear aside so as not to hear the law has himself also abhorred his own prayer.

paragraphs: Six times He says, You heard that it was said, but I tell you, and each time He carries the commandment from the hand to the heart: from murder to anger, from adultery to the look, from the oath to the plain word, from repayment to love of the enemy. Proverbs had already told Israel to feed an enemy and to leave repayment to the Lord.

You heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘You shall not murder,’ and ‘Whoever murders will be liable to judgment.’ But I tell you that everyone angry with his brother will be liable to judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ will be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

You heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you: love your enemies and pray for those persecuting you, so that you may become sons of your Father in the heavens, because He makes His sun rise upon evil and good people and sends rain upon righteous and unrighteous people. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You, therefore, shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.
Nathan: The Poor Man’s Ewe Lamb. The rich man takes the poor man’s one lamb; David condemns him, and Nathan answers, You are the man.
Anger destroys even intelligent people; but a yielding answer turns away wrath, and a painful word raises angers.
Do not let desire for beauty overcome you; do not be hunted by your own eyes, nor seized by her eyelids.
If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord will repay you good things.
Do not say, “I will punish the enemy.” But wait for the Lord, so that He may help you.
Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but one who performs faithful deeds is acceptable to Him.
Cease from anger and abandon wrath; do not be provoked to envy so as to act wickedly.
Be angry, and do not sin; speak in your hearts, and upon your beds be pierced with remorse. Diapsalma.

But exhort one another each day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin. … So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God. For the one who entered His rest also himself rested from his works, just as God did from His own. Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.

paragraphs: Nothing from outside defiles; what comes out of the heart defiles. The Law’s care for clean and unclean is carried inward, where Proverbs had already set the guard and David had asked for a clean heart.

Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand. There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.” When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable. He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him, because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods. He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person. For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders, adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness. All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”

I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean. … For God’s kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit;
With every guard keep your heart, for from these come life’s outlets.
Who will boast that he has a pure heart? Or who will speak confidently of being clean from sins?
Evil offspring judge themselves righteous, but have not washed away their discharge.
Create a clean heart in me, God, and renew an upright spirit in my inward parts.

Who will ascend the Lord’s mountain, and who will stand in His holy place? One innocent in hands and pure in heart, who did not take up his soul for emptiness and did not swear deceitfully to his neighbor.

paragraphs: What is done to be seen has its reward already. He sets the scribes’ long fringes beside a widow’s two small coins. Proverbs: let your neighbor praise you, and not your own mouth.

He called His disciples to Him and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury. For they all put in from their surplus, but she, from her need, put in everything she had—her whole livelihood.”
The Pharisee and the Tax Collector. The one who humbled himself went down to his house justified rather than the other.
The Lowest Place at the Feast. Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.
Let your neighbor praise you, and not your mouth, another, and not your lips.
Everyone high of heart is unclean before God, and one who unjustly puts hands into a hand will not be acquitted.

Do not boast before a king, and do not station yourself in the places of rulers; for it is better for you to be told, “Come up to me,” than for him to humble you before a ruler. Say what your eyes have seen.
Each spoke empty things to his neighbor; deceitful lips spoke with a heart and a heart. May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and a boastful tongue—
Lord, my heart was not exalted, nor were my eyes raised high; I did not walk among great things nor among wonders beyond me.

Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and puts them into practice will be likened to a prudent man who built his house upon the rock.
The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and fell upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.

research.title: Hear and Keep
paragraphs: To hear and not to do is to build on sand. Israel said at Sinai, We will do and obey; Ezekiel’s hearers listened as to a sweet song and did nothing. The one who keeps the word is the tree by the waters that gives its fruit in its season, the branch that remains in the vine.

Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and does them will be likened to a prudent man who built his house upon the rock. The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and fell upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock. And everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not do them will be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand. The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell; and its fall was great.”
“If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.

And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments. The one who says, “I have come to know Him,” and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person. But whoever keeps His word, in that person the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in Him. doing nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility considering one another above yourselves, each looking not to your own interests, but each also to those of others. The Unprofitable Slaves. When you have done all that was commanded, say, We have done what we ought to have done.

For the Lord is high and watches the lowly, and the lofty He knows from afar.

But you shall not be called ‘Rabbi,’ for One is your Teacher, and you are all brothers.
And call no one upon earth your father, for One is your Father, the heavenly One.

who, existing in the form of God, did not regard being equal with God as something to exploit,

He humbled Himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.
Likewise, you who are younger, submit yourselves to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
Therefore, humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that He may exalt you in due time,
I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a participant in the glory about to be revealed:
Shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion but willingly, according to God; not for shameful gain but eagerly;
not as lording it over those allotted to you, but becoming examples to the flock.
And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.

verses.text: When Jesus saw it, He was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to Me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’

But whoever has this world’s means of living and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him? Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
One who extorts from the needy provokes the One who made him, but one who honors Him has mercy on the poor.
One who has mercy on the poor lends to God, and He will repay him according to his gift.
One who blocks his ears from hearing the weak will himself also call, and there will be no one listening.
One who has mercy on the poor will himself be nourished, for he gave of his own loaves to the poor.
Open your mouth for God’s word, and judge everyone soundly. Open your mouth and judge justly, and decide the case of the poor and weak.
Blessed is the one who understands the poor and needy; in an evil day the Lord will rescue him.
From the mouth of infants and nursing children You prepared praise, because of Your enemies, to bring down the enemy and the avenger.
Judge for the fatherless and the poor; vindicate the lowly and the needy. Deliver the needy and the poor; rescue them from the hand of a sinner.”
the Father of orphans and judge of widows, God in His holy place.
When Jesus saw it, He was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to Me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in the heavens continually see the face of My Father in the heavens.

He also said to the one who had invited Him, “When you give a midday meal or a supper, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and you receive repayment.
But when you give a reception, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind.
And you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’
Salt is good; but if salt becomes saltless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
But whoever has this world’s goods and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him?
Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
Therefore let us no longer judge one another; but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or a snare for a brother.
I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean.
For if your brother is grieved because of food, you no longer walk according to love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
Religion that is pure and undefiled before God the Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
Let brotherly love remain.
Do not forget hospitality, for through it some unknowingly entertained angels.
Remember the prisoners as fellow prisoners, and those being mistreated, as you yourselves also are in a body.
For it is not that there should be relief for others and affliction for you, but on the basis of equality:
at the present time your abundance is to meet their lack, so that their abundance may also meet your lack, so that there may be equality.
As it is written, “The one with much had no excess, and the one with little had no shortage.”
One who extorts from the needy provokes the One who made him, but one who honors Him has mercy on the poor.
One who has mercy on the poor lends to God, and He will repay him according to his gift.
One who blocks his ears from hearing the weak will himself also call, and there will be no one listening.
One who has mercy on the poor will himself be nourished, for he gave of his own loaves to the poor.
Open your mouth for God’s word, and judge everyone soundly.
Open your mouth and judge justly, and decide the case of the poor and weak.
Blessed is the one who understands the poor and needy; in an evil day the Lord will rescue him.
From the mouth of infants and nursing children Thou didst prepare praise, because of Thine enemies, to bring down the enemy and the avenger.
Judge for the fatherless and the poor; vindicate the lowly and the needy.
Deliver the needy and the poor; rescue them from the hand of a sinner.”

And every gift of your sacrifice shall be seasoned with salt. You shall not let the salt of the covenant of the Lord cease from your sacrifices; with every gift of yours you shall bring salt unto the Lord your God.
And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the harvest of your field; and you shall not gather what falls from your harvest,
neither shall you glean your vineyard again, nor gather the grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the resident foreigner; I am the Lord your God.

And if there is among you one of your brethren in need, within any of your cities in the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not withhold the affection of your heart, neither shall you close your hand against your needy brother.
You shall freely open your hands unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs, according to his want.
For I rescued a poor person from a powerful man’s hand and helped an orphan who had no helper.
May the blessing of the perishing come upon me, and a widow’s mouth blessed me.
I had clothed myself with righteousness, and I wrapped myself in justice like a double cloak.
I was an eye for the blind and a foot for the lame.
I was a father to the powerless, and I traced out a case I did not know.

‘It is not such a fast that I chose,’ says the Lord. ‘Instead, loosen every bond of injustice, undo the strangling ties of coercive agreements, release the crushed, and tear up every unjust written contract.
Break your bread for the hungry and bring homeless poor people into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe him; do not overlook those belonging to your own family.

Yet this was the lawlessness of your sister Sodom: arrogance. In fullness of bread and abundance of wine she and her daughters lived luxuriously. This belonged to her and her daughters, but they did not support the hand of the poor and needy.

The Lord lives in heaven, and His authority is over all the earth. Entreat Him concerning your sins, and redeem all your injustices by almsgiving, so that gentleness may be granted you, you may have many days upon your royal throne, and He may not destroy you. Love these words, for my word is accurate and your time is full.’”

paragraphs: Stay awake. The prophets stood at their watch, and they warned of prophets who speak from their own heart and of watchmen who love to doze. Wisdom blesses the one who keeps awake at her doors day by day, and the psalmist waits for the Lord from the morning watch until night.
Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

Because if you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved; for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.
The Ten Virgins. Five were prudent and took oil; the bridegroom came, and the door was shut.
The Doorkeeper. Stay awake, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming.
The Watchful Slaves. Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds awake: he will gird himself and serve them.
The Thief in the Night. If the householder had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake.
The Faithful and the Wicked Slave. Blessed is the slave whom his master finds so doing when he comes.
The Talents. To each according to his ability; to everyone who has, more will be given.
The Minas. Do business until I come.
The Budding Fig Tree. When its branch becomes tender, you know that summer is near.
The Weeds among the Wheat. Good seed and darnel, the weed an enemy sowed, grow together until the harvest, when the Son of Man sends His angels to separate them. The Lord explains it Himself.
The Dragnet. The net gathers every kind; at the end of the age the angels separate the evil from the righteous.
The Blind Leading the Blind. Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

How long do you lie down, sluggard? When will you rise from sleep? You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, and clasp your chest with your hands a little; then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner.
Happy is the man who will listen to me, and the person who will keep my ways, staying awake at my doors day by day, guarding the posts of my entrances.
Do not boast of things for tomorrow, for you do not know what the coming day will bear.
The innocent person believes every word, but the resourceful comes to reconsideration.
Because of Your law I waited for You, Lord; my soul waited for Your word. My soul hoped in the Lord from the morning watch until night; from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.
Unless the Lord builds a house, those building it have labored in vain. Unless the Lord guards a city, the watchman has kept awake in vain.
My eyes were awake before dawn to meditate on Your sayings.
And I spoke of Your testimonies before kings, and I was not ashamed.

I proclaimed good news of righteousness in a great assembly; look, I will certainly not restrain my lips; Lord, You know. I did not hide Your righteousness in my heart; I spoke of Your truth and Your salvation. I did not hide Your mercy and Your truth from a great congregation.
