Unless the Lord builds a house, those building it have labored in vain. Unless the Lord guards a city, the watchman has kept awake in vain.
My eyes were awake before dawn to meditate on Your sayings.
And I spoke of Your testimonies before kings, and I was not ashamed.

I proclaimed good news of righteousness in a great assembly; look, I will certainly not restrain my lips; Lord, You know. I did not hide Your righteousness in my heart; I spoke of Your truth and Your salvation. I did not hide Your mercy and Your truth from a great congregation.
Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.
But watch yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the cares of life, and that day come upon you suddenly
like a trap. For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth.
But stay awake at every season, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.”
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
Jesus said to them, “Look out and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Do not give what is holy to dogs or throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them with their feet and turn and tear you apart.
Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves. So become prudent as snakes and innocent as doves.
Remember Lot’s wife.
Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses it will keep it alive.
Therefore everyone who acknowledges Me before people, I too will acknowledge before My Father in the heavens.
But whoever denies Me before people, I too will deny before My Father in the heavens.
Because if you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved;
for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.
With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings who have been made in God’s likeness.
From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen this way.
Does a spring pour out sweet and bitter water from the same opening?
My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet water.
The saying is trustworthy: for if we died with Him, we will also live with Him;
if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He also will deny us;
if we are unfaithful, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
Now concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anything to be written to you.
For you yourselves know exactly that the day of the Lord comes in this way, like a thief in the night.
When they say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction comes upon them, as labor pain upon a pregnant woman, and they will certainly not escape.
But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief.
For you are all sons of light and sons of day. We are not of night or darkness.
So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us keep watch and be sober.

But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a rushing roar, and the elements will be dissolved by burning heat, and the earth and the works in it will not be found.
Since all these things are being dissolved in this way, what sort of people ought you to be in holy acts of conduct and godliness,
waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved by fire and the elements melt in burning heat?
Be patient, therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Look, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until he receives the early and late rain.
You too be patient; strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Look, the Judge stands before the doors.
Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh is from God,
and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. And this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and is already in the world now.
I know that after my departure fierce wolves will enter among you, not sparing the flock.
Even from among you yourselves men will arise, speaking distorted things to draw the disciples away after themselves.
Therefore stay awake, remembering that for three years, night and day, I never ceased admonishing each one with tears.
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
and all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were strewn over the wilderness.
Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired.
Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, just as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose to play.”
Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
Nor let us put Christ to the test, as some of them tested Him and were being destroyed by the serpents.
Nor grumble, just as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer.
These things happened to them as examples, and were written to admonish us, upon whom the ends of the ages have arrived.
and reduced the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes, condemning them to overthrow, having made them an example for those who would live ungodly lives,
and rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the lawless people’s conduct in debauchery—
for by what he saw and heard, that righteous man, living among them, tormented his righteous soul day after day over their lawless deeds—
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment,
who were once disobedient, when the patience of God waited in the days of Noah while the ark was being prepared, in which a few—that is, eight souls—were brought safely through water.
Corresponding to this, baptism also now saves you—not a removal of dirt from the flesh, but an appeal to God for a good conscience—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
But do not let this one thing escape you, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
The Lord is not slow concerning the promise, as some consider slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing anyone to perish but all to come to repentance.

then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner.

Now the serpent was more cunning than all the wild beasts upon the earth that the Lord God had made. And the serpent said to the woman, “Why has God said, ‘You shall not eat from any tree in the garden’?”
And the Lord God said to Noah, “Enter the ark, you and all your household, for I have seen you righteous before Me in this generation.

And when they had brought them outside, they said, “Save your own life. Do not look behind you or stand anywhere in the surrounding country. Escape to the mountain, so that you are not swept away with them.”
And his wife looked behind her, and became a pillar of salt.
But the prophet who shall act ungodly, speaking in My name a word which I commanded him not to speak, or who shall speak in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.
And if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word which the Lord has not spoken?

Whatsoever the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the word does not come to pass, nor is fulfilled, that is the word which the Lord has not spoken. That prophet has spoken in ungodliness; you shall not spare him.

For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread, and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.” Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.” For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
The Great Supper. Those first invited made excuses; the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame are brought in.
The Wedding Feast. Many are called, but few are chosen.

Wisdom built herself a house, and set seven pillars beneath it. She slaughtered her own sacrificial animals, mixed her own wine in a mixing-bowl, and prepared her own table. She sent her own servants, summoning with a lofty proclamation to the mixing-bowl, saying: “Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me!” And to those lacking understanding she said: “Come, eat of my loaves, and drink wine that I mixed for you. Leave foolishness, and you will live; seek understanding, so that you may live, and set insight right in knowledge.”

Taste and see that the Lord is kind; blessed is the man who hopes in Him.

research.title: The Sending
paragraphs: He sends them as the prophets were sent: with words put in the mouth, without inheritance, in haste like Gehazi, to be mocked as the messengers were mocked. Those who sow in tears will reap with exultation.
As you go, proclaim, ‘The kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.’ Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. Freely you received; freely give.

Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say every evil thing against you because of Me. Rejoice and exult, for your reward is great in the heavens; for in this way they persecuted the prophets before you.
In everything I showed you that by working in this way we must support the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
The Sower. The seed is the word; the four soils are four ways of hearing it. The Lord explains it Himself.
The Workers in the Vineyard. The last receive as the first, for the master is generous; the last will be first and the first last.
The Grain of Wheat. Unless it falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
The Woman in Labor. Her grief turns to joy when the child is born: so your grief will become joy.
An impious person flees when no one pursues, but a righteous person is confident like a lion.
Son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline or lose heart when corrected by Him, for the Lord disciplines the one He loves and scourges every son He receives.
As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.
Those sowing in tears will reap with exultation. Going, they went and wept, carrying their seeds; but coming, they will arrive with exultation, carrying their sheaves.
For Your sake we are put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.
for on Your account I endured reproach; embarrassment covered my face.
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and He will rescue them from them all.
The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup; You are the One who restores my inheritance to me.

paragraphs: Feed My lambs. The charge to Peter answers Moses’ prayer that the congregation not be like sheep without a shepherd, and the long complaint of the prophets against shepherds who fed themselves. Proverbs gives the pastor’s rule in a line: know thoroughly the lives of your flock.

So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus says to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, You know that I love You.” He says to him, “Feed My lambs.” He says to him again a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord, You know that I love You.” He says to him, “Shepherd My sheep.” He says to him the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was grieved because He said to him the third time, “Do you love Me?” And he said to Him, “Lord, You know all things; You know that I love You.” Jesus says to him, “Feed My sheep.

Therefore, I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a participant in the glory about to be revealed: Shepherd the flock of God among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion but willingly, according to God; not for shameful gain but eagerly; not as lording it over those allotted to you, but becoming examples to the flock. And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
The Good Shepherd and the Door. The sheep hear His voice; the good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep. John calls it a figure of speech.
The Lost Sheep. There is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
The Shepherds and the Sheep. Woe to the shepherds who feed themselves; the Lord Himself will seek His sheep. The Lord’s word, I am the good Shepherd, answers this prophecy.
The Faithful and the Wicked Slave. Blessed is the slave whom his master finds so doing when he comes.
Know thoroughly the lives of your flock, and set your heart upon your herds;
Mercy and truth are a guard for a king, and they will surround his throne in righteousness.

And He chose David His servant, and took him up from the flocks of sheep; from behind the ewes giving birth He took him, to shepherd Jacob His people and Israel His inheritance. And he shepherded them in his heart’s innocence, and guided them with his hands’ understanding.
You who shepherd Israel, pay attention, You who guide Joseph like sheep; You who sit upon the cherubim, appear.
Restore to me the exultation of Your salvation, and strengthen me with a governing spirit. I will teach the lawless Your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to You.
Know that the Lord—He is God. He made us, and not we; His people and the sheep of His pasture.

who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the Lord's congregation will not be like sheep without a shepherd.
In days past, when Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them in. The Lord said to you, ‘You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over Israel.’”
Like a shepherd, He will shepherd His flock; and with His arm He will gather lambs, and comfort those that are with young.
and I will give you shepherds according to My heart, and they will shepherd you, shepherding with knowledge.
O shepherds who scatter and destroy the sheep of My pasture!
Therefore thus says the Lord to those shepherding My people: You scattered My sheep and drove them out without visiting them. Behold, I am exacting justice from you according to your evil practices.
And I will receive the remnant of My people from all the land where I drove them out, and establish them in their pasture; they will increase and multiply.
And I will raise shepherds for them who will tend them, and they will no longer fear or be frightened, says the Lord.

“Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s shepherds. Prophesy and say to the shepherds, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O shepherds of Israel, surely shepherds do not feed themselves? Do shepherds not feed the sheep?
Behold, you consume the milk, clothe yourselves with the wool and slaughter the fattened animal, but you do not feed My sheep.

verses.text:
“If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.
Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the expense, whether he has enough to finish it?
Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is unable to complete it, all who see it may begin to mock him,
saying, ‘This man began to build and was unable to finish.’
Or what king, going to meet another king in war, will not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
And if not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.
So, therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all his own possessions cannot be My disciple.

that you shall take of the firstfruits of the produce of your land which the Lord your God gives you, and put it in a basket, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

God gives seed-bearing plants and fruit for food in the creation account. This is a provision, not a command that every plant is edible or that all later believers must be vegetarian. Genesis 9:3 gives a further food permission; Christian readers should also consider thanksgiving and the teaching in 1 Timothy.

Blood is associated with life in the instruction to Noah and in Israel’s law. The Jerusalem council also includes abstention from blood in its instructions to Gentile believers. Christians differ about the continuing scope of that council’s food restrictions; the text should be stated before a denominational conclusion is drawn.

and the hare, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
and the choirogryllios, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
and the pig, because it divides the hoof and has cleft hoof-claws but does not bring up the cud; it is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
And these you may eat among all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and streams, you may eat.
And whatever has neither fins nor scales in the water, in the seas and streams, among all that the waters bring forth and every living creature in the water, is an abomination.
And they shall be abominations for you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall abhor their carcasses.
And whatever among the things in the water has no fins and scales is an abomination for you.
And these you shall abhor among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are an abomination: the eagle, the gryps, and the sea-eagle;
and the vulture, the kite, and those like it;
and the raven and those like it;
and the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like it, and the hawk and those like it;
and the night-raven, the diving bird, and the ibis;
and the purple waterbird, the pelican, and the swan;
and the owl, the heron, the plover and those like it, the hoopoe, and the bat.
And every winged creeping thing that walks on four is an abomination for you.
But among the winged creeping things that walk on four, you may eat those that have legs above their feet for leaping on the earth.
And these among them you may eat: the brouchos and those like it, the attakes and those like it, the locust and those like it, and the snake-fighter and those like it.
Every winged creeping thing that has four feet is an abomination for you.
And by these you shall become defiled: everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every animal that divides the hoof and has cleft claws but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
And these are unclean for you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile;
the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole.

And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean: any wooden utensil, garment, skin, or sack, any article used for work. It shall be dipped in water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
And if one of them falls inside any earthenware vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and the vessel shall be shattered.
And any food that may be eaten, on which water comes, shall become unclean, and any drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall become unclean.
And anything on which any of their carcasses falls shall become unclean. Ovens and pot-stands shall be demolished; these are unclean and shall be unclean for you.
But springs of water, a cistern, and a gathering of water shall remain clean; whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
If any of their carcasses falls on seed intended for sowing, it remains clean.
But if water is poured on any seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you may eat dies, whosoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever eats from these carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth shall be an abomination for you; it shall not be eaten.
And whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four continually, whatever has many feet among all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat, for it is an abomination for you.
And you shall in no wise make your souls abominable through any creeping things that creep upon the earth; neither shall you be defiled through them, nor shall you be unclean through them;
for I am the Lord your God; and you shall be sanctified and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God. And you shall not defile your souls through any creeping things that move upon the earth;
for I am the Lord who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God; and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord.
This is the law concerning animals, birds, every creature that moves in the water, and every creature that creeps upon the earth,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creatures that are eaten and the living creatures that are not eaten.

research.title: Israel’s distinctions between clean and unclean food
paragraphs: Study 61: Israel’s distinctions between clean and unclean food

Related indexed requirements: C0213, C0465, C0467, C0468, C0469, C0470, C0471, C0472, C0473, C0474, C0475, C0476, C0477, C0478, C0479. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Transformed — dietary holiness and a cleansed heart
Connection to Christ: Jesus, Acts and Romans address defilement, food and conscience; Christian interpretations of their relationship to Leviticus differ.
Christian response today: Receive food with thanksgiving, pursue purity of heart, avoid idolatry and refuse to pressure or despise another believer over food; keep Acts 15’s instructions in view.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 11:1–47 Christ and the apostles: Mark 7:14–23 · Acts 15:19–29 · Romans 14:1–3
Ancient covenant practice: Leviticus distinguishes clean and unclean animals in Israel’s covenant life.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus locates moral defilement in what comes from the heart. The current Saints reading of Mark 7:19 speaks of cleansing all foods. Paul joins freedom concerning food to love, conscience and thanksgiving. Acts 15 supplies additional apostolic instructions.
Saints Translation support: Mark 7:18–23 · Romans 14:13–23 · 1 Timothy 4:3–5 · Acts 15:28–29 · Acts 10:28
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament treatment of food and defilement; this Christian synthesis is disputed by some traditions.

Read carefully: Christians disagree about continuing clean-and-unclean distinctions and the scope of Acts 15. Peter applies his vision explicitly to receiving people in Acts 10:28; that verse must not be reduced to a standalone menu rule.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Leviticus gives Israel detailed distinctions among land animals, water creatures, birds and swarming creatures. Christian application requires reading Jesus’ teaching about defilement, the Jerusalem council and Paul on food. Traditions differ on continuing dietary observance; the study must identify that disagreement rather than claim the Torah alone settles every Christian practice.

Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.”
When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable.
He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.
He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.
For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”
Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from the Gentiles who are turning to God,
but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, sexual immorality, what is strangled, and blood.
For since ancient times, people in every city have proclaimed Moses, and he is read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”

Then the apostles and elders, with the whole Church, decided to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers.
They wrote by their hand: “The apostles and elders, your brothers, to the brothers from the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings.
Since we have heard that some who went out from among us troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, although we gave them no instruction,
we have decided with one accord to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
men who have given over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves report the same things by word of mouth.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things:
to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”

Since we have heard that some who went out from among us troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, although we gave them no instruction,
we have decided with one accord to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
men who have given over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves report the same things by word of mouth.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things:
to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”
Welcome the one who is weak in faith, but not to dispute over opinions.
One believes he may eat all things, but the weak person eats vegetables.
Do not let the one who eats despise the one who does not eat; and do not let the one who does not eat judge the one who eats, for God welcomed him.
He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.
He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.
For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”
Therefore let us no longer judge one another; but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or a snare for a brother.
I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; except that to the one who reckons something unclean, to that person it is unclean.
For if your brother is grieved because of food, you no longer walk according to love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.
Therefore do not let your good be spoken of as evil.
For God’s kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit;
for the one who serves Christ in this is pleasing to God and approved by people.
So then, let us pursue what makes for peace and what builds up one another.
Do not tear down God’s work for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean, but it is evil for a person to eat in a way that causes stumbling.
It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything by which your brother stumbles.
The faith you have, keep to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge himself in what he approves.
But the one who doubts, if he eats, has been condemned, because it is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
For everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected when received with thanksgiving,
for it is sanctified through the word of God and intercession.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things:
to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”
He said to them, “You know how forbidden it is for a Jewish man to associate with or visit someone of another people. Yet God has shown me to call no human being common or unclean.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: These are the animals you may eat among all the animals on the earth.
Every animal among the livestock that divides the hoof, and cleaves its claws into two hoofs, and brings up the cud: these you may eat.

Nevertheless, of these you shall not eat: among those that bring up the cud and those that divide the hoof and cleave the claws, the camel, because it brings up the cud, but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean unto you;
and the hare, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
and the choirogryllios, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
and the pig, because it divides the hoof and has cleft hoof-claws but does not bring up the cud; it is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
And these you may eat among all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and streams, you may eat.
And whatever has neither fins nor scales in the water, in the seas and streams, among all that the waters bring forth and every living creature in the water, is an abomination.
And they shall be abominations for you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall abhor their carcasses.
And whatever among the things in the water has no fins and scales is an abomination for you.
And these you shall abhor among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are an abomination: the eagle, the gryps, and the sea-eagle;
and the vulture, the kite, and those like it;
and the raven and those like it;
and the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like it, and the hawk and those like it;
and the night-raven, the diving bird, and the ibis;
and the purple waterbird, the pelican, and the swan;
and the owl, the heron, the plover and those like it, the hoopoe, and the bat.
And every winged creeping thing that walks on four is an abomination for you.
But among the winged creeping things that walk on four, you may eat those that have legs above their feet for leaping on the earth.
And these among them you may eat: the brouchos and those like it, the attakes and those like it, the locust and those like it, and the snake-fighter and those like it.
Every winged creeping thing that has four feet is an abomination for you.
And by these you shall become defiled: everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every animal that divides the hoof and has cleft claws but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
And these are unclean for you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile;
the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole.
These are unclean for you among all the creeping things on the earth. Whosoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean: any wooden utensil, garment, skin, or sack, any article used for work. It shall be dipped in water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
And if one of them falls inside any earthenware vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and the vessel shall be shattered.
And any food that may be eaten, on which water comes, shall become unclean, and any drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall become unclean.
And anything on which any of their carcasses falls shall become unclean. Ovens and pot-stands shall be demolished; these are unclean and shall be unclean for you.
But springs of water, a cistern, and a gathering of water shall remain clean; whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
If any of their carcasses falls on seed intended for sowing, it remains clean.
But if water is poured on any seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you may eat dies, whosoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.

And whosoever eats from these carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth shall be an abomination for you; it shall not be eaten.

And whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four continually, whatever has many feet among all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat, for it is an abomination for you.
And you shall in no wise make your souls abominable through any creeping things that creep upon the earth; neither shall you be defiled through them, nor shall you be unclean through them;

for I am the Lord your God; and you shall be sanctified and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God. And you shall not defile your souls through any creeping things that move upon the earth;
for I am the Lord who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God; and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord.
This is the law concerning animals, birds, every creature that moves in the water, and every creature that creeps upon the earth,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creatures that are eaten and the living creatures that are not eaten.

Transformed — ritual status and access to God
Connection to Christ: Jesus receives the woman with bleeding, and Hebrews distinguishes ritual regulation from cleansing of conscience; this is a contextual Christian reading.
Christian response today: Approach God through Christ and treat menstruating people with dignity; do not equate a bodily process with moral guilt or reduced spiritual worth.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 15:19–24 Christ and the apostles: Mark 5:25–34 · Hebrews 9:9–14
Ancient covenant practice: Leviticus sets temporary ritual-status and contact rules concerning menstruation within Israel’s sanctuary life.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus receives and heals the woman with prolonged bleeding. Hebrews distinguishes bodily regulations from the cleansing of conscience and invites believers to approach God through Christ.
Saints Translation support: Mark 5:25–34 · Hebrews 9:9–14 · Hebrews 10:19–22
Basis and scope: Christian interpretation of Jesus’ healing and Hebrews’ teaching; the Gospel incident is not itself a repeal formula.
Read carefully: The woman’s prolonged bleeding is not identical to ordinary menstruation. The application draws on the wider covenant teaching; churches differ in some ritual disciplines.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Leviticus describes temporary ritual uncleanness and associated contact rules. Menstruation itself is not described as a moral fault. Ritual status in Israel’s sanctuary system should not be equated with a person’s dignity, spiritual worth or modern medical diagnosis. The Gospel’s account of the woman with bleeding provides an important complementary reading.

heard about Jesus. She came behind Him in the crowd and touched His garment.

title: Discharges, skin conditions and ritual cleansing
audience_note: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
paragraphs: Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
Classification: Study context · Topical study
Topic: Food, ritual purity and cleansing

Connection to Christ: Jesus’ healing and Hebrews’ sanctuary teaching illuminate the rites without identifying every examination or washing as a separate prophecy. Christian response today: Care compassionately for people who are ill and seek holiness through Christ, keeping ritual status, moral conduct and medical care distinct.
Full research entry
wording_notes: This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
If anyone has on the skin of his body a bright scar-like mark, and it becomes a lesion of leprosy on his skin, he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.
And the priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears lower than the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.
If the bright spot on his skin is white but does not appear lower than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, but it is faint, the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.
And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the lesion remains before him, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for a second seven days.
And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day a second time; and, behold, if the lesion is faint, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, for it is a mark; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
But if the mark changes and shifts in the skin after the priest has examined him for cleansing, he shall appear before the priest a second time,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the mark has shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy.

Transformed — ritual cleansing and service with a clean conscience
Connection to Christ: Jesus’ healing and Hebrews’ sanctuary teaching illuminate the rites without identifying every examination or washing as a separate prophecy.
Christian response today: Care compassionately for people who are ill and seek holiness through Christ, keeping ritual status, moral conduct and medical care distinct.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 13:1–8 · Leviticus 14:1–9 · Leviticus 15:1–18 Christ and the apostles: Mark 1:40–44 · Hebrews 9:9–14
Ancient covenant practice: Israel’s laws prescribe examinations, separation, washings and offerings concerning skin conditions and bodily discharges.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus heals and restores people; in Mark 1 he also tells the healed man to present the Mosaic offering. Hebrews later interprets the bodily regulations through Christ’s cleansing of conscience.
Saints Translation support: Mark 1:40–44 · Hebrews 9:9–14 · Hebrews 10:19–22
Basis and scope: Christian interpretation of the wider sanctuary teaching; not a separate New Testament ruling on every washing.
Read carefully: Jesus’ healing must not be misquoted as an immediate cancellation of the priestly procedure he explicitly commands in that scene.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

These chapters prescribe examination, separation, washing and ritual procedures in Israel. Calling the whole collection “hygiene” can obscure its sanctuary purpose and the difference between ritual impurity and disease. It is not a substitute for modern medical care. Jesus’ healing and Hebrews’ account of cleansing provide the Christian context.

And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
This is the law of the person with leprosy on the day he is cleansed: he shall be brought unto the priest,
and the priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion of leprosy has healed in him that had leprosy,
then the priest shall give orders, and they shall take two living clean birds, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop for the person who has been cleansed.
And the priest shall give orders, and they shall slaughter one bird into an earthenware vessel over living water.
And he shall take the living bird, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop, and dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird slaughtered over the living water.
And he shall sprinkle the person cleansed from leprosy seven times, and he shall be clean. He shall release the living bird into the plain.

And the person who has been cleansed shall wash his garments, shave off all his hair, bathe in water, and be clean. Afterward he shall enter the camp, but he shall remain outside his house for seven days.
And on the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair: his head, his beard, and his eyebrows; he shall shave off all his hair. He shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be clean.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If any man has a flow from his body, his flow is unclean.

And this is the law of his uncleanness: discharging seed from his body through the flow by which his body has become stopped up, this is his uncleanness in him; all the days of the flow of his body, in which his body has become stopped up through the flow, are his uncleanness.
Every bed on which the man with a seminal discharge lies is unclean, and every article on which the man with a seminal discharge sits shall be unclean.
And whosoever touches his bed shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whosoever sits on an article on which the man with a seminal discharge has sat shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whosoever touches the skin of the man with a seminal discharge shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
If the man with a seminal discharge spits on someone clean, that person shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And any donkey saddle on which the man with a seminal discharge mounts shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries those things shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And anyone whom the man with a seminal discharge touches when he has not washed his hands shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
And an earthenware vessel touched by the man with a seminal discharge shall be shattered, and a wooden vessel shall be washed with water and be clean.
When the man with a seminal discharge is cleansed from his flow, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be clean.
And on the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, bring them before the Lord to the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and give them unto the priest.
And the priest shall prepare them, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord for his flow.
And if a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water and be unclean until evening.
And every garment and every skin on which there is semen shall be washed with water and be unclean until evening.
And if a man lies with a woman with an emission of semen, they shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.

And moved with compassion, He stretched out His hand and touched him, and says to him, “I will; be cleansed.”
Immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
Sternly warning him, He immediately drove him away
and said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!

by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

If anyone has on the skin of his body a bright scar-like mark, and it becomes a lesion of leprosy on his skin, he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears lower than the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.
If the bright spot on his skin is white but does not appear lower than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, but it is faint, the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the lesion remains before him, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for a second seven days.

verses.text:
Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.
Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.
And this is the law: If a person dies in a house, everyone who enters the house and everything in the house shall be unclean for seven days.
And every open vessel without a fastening tied upon it is unclean.
And anyone who touches, on the open plain, one slain, a dead person, a human bone, or a tomb shall be unclean for seven days.
And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.
And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.
And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.
And if a man is defiled, and is not purified, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord; because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean.
And this shall be an everlasting ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whosoever touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

Christian response today: Serve God through Christ with a cleansed conscience, and care reverently for the dying and dead without treating that care as moral guilt.

Ancient covenant practice: Contact with a corpse calls for the prescribed purification involving heifer ashes and water.
Development in Christ and the apostles: Hebrews explicitly compares the rite’s outward cleansing with Christ’s deeper cleansing of conscience for service to the living God.
Saints Translation support: Hebrews 9:13–14 · Hebrews 10:19–22
Basis and scope: Direct comparison made in Hebrews.
Read carefully: Fulfilled identifies the Christ-centered cleansing comparison; Transformed identifies its Christian application. Bodily care and ordinary precautions remain important.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Contact with a human corpse creates temporary ritual uncleanness under the specified purification procedure. This does not make burial or care for the dead morally wrong. Hebrews explicitly contrasts the cleansing associated with heifer ashes and the deeper cleansing of conscience through Christ.

And anyone who touches, on the open plain, one slain, a dead person, a human bone, or a tomb shall be unclean for seven days.
And for the unclean person they shall take some ashes from what was burned for purification, and they shall pour living water over them into a vessel.

And a clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it around the house, the vessels, and the people who were there, and on whoever touched the human bone, the slain person, the dead person, or the tomb.

And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

And if a man is defiled, and is not purified, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord; because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean.
And this shall be an everlasting ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whosoever touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

verses.text: You are sons of the Lord your God; you shall not perform purification rites, neither shall you make a bald place between your eyes for the dead.
For you are a holy people unto the Lord your God; and the Lord your God has chosen you to be unto Him a people for His own possession, out of all the nations upon the face of the earth.
You shall eat no abominable thing.
These are the beasts which you may eat: a calf of the cattle, and a lamb of the sheep, and a young male goat of the goats,
deer, gazelle, bubalos, goat-stag, white-rumped antelope, oryx, and giraffe.
Every beast that divides the hoof, and cleaves its hoof into two parts, and brings up the cud among the beasts, these you may eat.

And these you shall not eat of those that bring up the cud, and of those that divide the hoof and cleave its parts: the camel, and the hare, and the rock hyrax; for they bring up the cud, but do not divide the hoof; they are unclean unto you.

And these you may eat of all that are in the waters: whatsoever has fins and scales, you may eat.

You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed, the yield of your field, year by year.

And you shall eat it before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there. One born of a prostitute shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter the assembly of the Lord; even unto the tenth generation he shall not enter the assembly of the Lord, even for ever,
because they did not meet you with bread and water in the way, when you came forth out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam son of Beor, from Mesopotamia, to curse you.
And the Lord your God would not hearken unto Balaam; and the Lord your God turned the curses into a blessing, because the Lord your God loved you.
You shall not speak peace unto them, nor seek their advantage, all your days for ever.
You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian, for you were a resident alien in his land.
The sons born unto them shall enter the assembly of the Lord in the third generation.
And when you go forth to encamp against your enemies, you shall keep yourself from every evil thing.
If there is among you a man who is not clean by reason of a discharge in the night, he shall go forth outside the camp, and shall not enter the camp.
And it shall be, toward evening, that he shall wash his body with water; and when the sun is set, he shall enter the camp.
And you shall have a place outside the camp, whither you shall go forth.
And you shall have a peg upon your belt; and when you squat outside, you shall dig therewith, and turn and cover your excrement with it.

And you shall have a peg upon your belt; and when you squat outside, you shall dig therewith, and turn and cover your excrement with it.

He shall dwell with you; he shall dwell among you in any place that pleases him. You shall not afflict him.

Leviticus 11:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 11:2 — Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: These are the animals you may eat among all the animals on the earth.
Leviticus 11:3 — Every animal among the livestock that divides the hoof, and cleaves its claws into two hoofs, and brings up the cud: these you may eat.

Leviticus 11:4 — Nevertheless, of these you shall not eat: among those that bring up the cud and those that divide the hoof and cleave the claws, the camel, because it brings up the cud, but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean unto you;
Leviticus 11:5 — and the hare, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
Leviticus 11:6 — and the choirogryllios, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
Leviticus 11:7 — and the pig, because it divides the hoof and has cleft hoof-claws but does not bring up the cud; it is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:8 — You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:9 — And these you may eat among all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and streams, you may eat.
Leviticus 11:10 — And whatever has neither fins nor scales in the water, in the seas and streams, among all that the waters bring forth and every living creature in the water, is an abomination.
Leviticus 11:11 — And they shall be abominations for you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall abhor their carcasses.
Leviticus 11:12 — And whatever among the things in the water has no fins and scales is an abomination for you.
Leviticus 11:13 — And these you shall abhor among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are an abomination: the eagle, the gryps, and the sea-eagle;
Leviticus 11:14 — and the vulture, the kite, and those like it;
Leviticus 11:15 — and the raven and those like it;
Leviticus 11:16 — and the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like it, and the hawk and those like it;
Leviticus 11:17 — and the night-raven, the diving bird, and the ibis;
Leviticus 11:18 — and the purple waterbird, the pelican, and the swan;
Leviticus 11:19 — and the owl, the heron, the plover and those like it, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Leviticus 11:20 — And every winged creeping thing that walks on four is an abomination for you.
Leviticus 11:21 — But among the winged creeping things that walk on four, you may eat those that have legs above their feet for leaping on the earth.
Leviticus 11:22 — And these among them you may eat: the brouchos and those like it, the attakes and those like it, the locust and those like it, and the snake-fighter and those like it.
Leviticus 11:23 — Every winged creeping thing that has four feet is an abomination for you.
Leviticus 11:24 — And by these you shall become defiled: everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
Leviticus 11:25 — and whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:26 — Every animal that divides the hoof and has cleft claws but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:27 — And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:28 — And whosoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:29 — And these are unclean for you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile;
Leviticus 11:30 — the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole.
Leviticus 11:31 — These are unclean for you among all the creeping things on the earth. Whosoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 11:32 — And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean: any wooden utensil, garment, skin, or sack, any article used for work. It shall be dipped in water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
Leviticus 11:33 — And if one of them falls inside any earthenware vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and the vessel shall be shattered.
Leviticus 11:34 — And any food that may be eaten, on which water comes, shall become unclean, and any drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall become unclean.
Leviticus 11:35 — And anything on which any of their carcasses falls shall become unclean. Ovens and pot-stands shall be demolished; these are unclean and shall be unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:36 — But springs of water, a cistern, and a gathering of water shall remain clean; whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
Leviticus 11:37 — If any of their carcasses falls on seed intended for sowing, it remains clean.
Leviticus 11:38 — But if water is poured on any seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:39 — If an animal that you may eat dies, whosoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 11:40 — And whosoever eats from these carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:41 — And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth shall be an abomination for you; it shall not be eaten.

Leviticus 11:42 — And whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four continually, whatever has many feet among all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat, for it is an abomination for you.

Leviticus 11:43 — And you shall in no wise make your souls abominable through any creeping things that creep upon the earth; neither shall you be defiled through them, nor shall you be unclean through them;

Leviticus 11:44 — for I am the Lord your God; and you shall be sanctified and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God. And you shall not defile your souls through any creeping things that move upon the earth;
Leviticus 11:45 — for I am the Lord who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God; and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord.
Leviticus 11:46 — This is the law concerning animals, birds, every creature that moves in the water, and every creature that creeps upon the earth,
Leviticus 11:47 — to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creatures that are eaten and the living creatures that are not eaten.

and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the mark has shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy.
And when a lesion of leprosy occurs in anyone, he shall come unto the priest.
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there is a white scar in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is some sound living flesh in the scar,
it is longstanding leprosy on the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and isolate him, for he is unclean.
But if the leprosy breaks out abundantly in the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the lesion from head to foot, throughout the whole view of the priest,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the leprosy has covered all the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean as to the lesion, because it has all turned white; it is clean.
And on whatever day living skin appears on him, he shall be defiled.
And the priest shall examine the sound skin, and the sound skin shall make him unclean, because it is unclean; it is leprosy.
But if the sound skin is restored and turns white, he shall come unto the priest,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the lesion clean; he is clean.
And if an ulcer occurs on the skin of the body and heals,
and a white scar or a whitish or fiery-red bright spot appears in the place of the ulcer, he shall appear before the priest.

And the priest shall examine it; and, behold, if its appearance is lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin of the body, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy that has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the ulcer; the priest shall declare him clean.
And if the skin of the body has a burn from fire, and the healed area of the burn on his skin becomes a shining, bright, whitish-red or completely white spot,

the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the hair in the shining spot has turned white, and its appearance is lower than the skin, it is leprosy which has blossomed in the burn; and the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in the shining spot, and it is not lower than the skin, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day; but if it has indeed spread in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the shining spot stays in its place, has not spread in the skin, and is faint, it is the scar of the burn. The priest shall declare him clean, for it is the mark of the burn.
And if a man or woman has a lesion of leprosy on the head or beard,

the priest shall examine the lesion; and, behold, if its appearance is more hollow than the skin, and there is fine yellowish hair in it, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a broken patch, leprosy of the head or leprosy of the beard.

And if the priest examines the lesion of the broken patch, and, behold, its appearance is not more hollow than the skin, and there is no yellowish hair in it, the priest shall isolate the lesion of the broken patch seven days.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread, and there is no yellowish hair in it, and the appearance of the broken patch is not hollow below the skin,
then the skin shall be shaved, but the broken patch shall not be shaved. The priest shall isolate the broken patch for a second seven days.

And the priest shall examine the broken patch on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread in the skin after he was shaved, and its appearance is not hollow below the skin, the priest shall declare him clean; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
But if the broken patch has indeed spread in the skin after he has been cleansed,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the broken patch has spread in the skin, the priest shall not inspect for yellow hair, for he is unclean.
But if before him the broken patch has remained in place and black hair has grown in it, the broken patch has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
And if a man or woman has shining, whitish patches on the skin of the body,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there are shining, whitish patches on the skin of his body, it is a white eruption; he is clean. It blossoms in the skin of his body; he is clean.
If anyone loses the hair of his head, he is bald; he is clean.
If he loses the hair at the front of his head, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
But if there is a white or fiery-red lesion on his bald head or bald forehead, it is leprosy on his bald head or bald forehead.
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the appearance of the lesion on his bald head or his bald forehead is white tinged with red, like the appearance of leprosy on the skin of his body,
he is a man with leprosy; the priest shall surely declare him unclean; his lesion is upon his head.
And he that has leprosy, in whom the lesion is, shall have his garments loosened and his head uncovered, and shall put a covering about his mouth, and shall be called unclean;
all the days in which the lesion is upon him, being unclean, he shall be unclean; he shall dwell apart; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
And if a garment has a lesion of leprosy, whether a woollen garment or a garment of coarse flax,
or in warp or weft, or in linen or wool, or in leather or any worked leather,
and the lesion in the leather, garment, warp, weft, or any worked leather article is greenish or fiery red, it is a lesion of leprosy, and he shall show it unto the priest.
And the priest shall examine the lesion, and the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.

And on the seventh day the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has spread in the garment, warp, weft, or leather, in whatever use is made of leather, the lesion is persistent leprosy; it is unclean.
He shall burn up the garment, the warp or weft in wool or linen, or any leather article that has the lesion, for it is persistent leprosy; it shall be burned up with fire.
But if the priest examines it and the lesion has not spread in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article,
then the priest shall give instructions, and he shall wash the article with the lesion; the priest shall isolate the lesion for a second seven days.

And after it has been washed, the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has not changed its appearance and has not spread, it is unclean; it shall be burned up with fire. It has become established in the garment, warp, or weft.
And if the priest examines it and the lesion is faint after washing, he shall tear it out of the garment, leather, warp, or weft.
If it appears again in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article, it is blossoming leprosy; the affected article shall be burned up with fire.
And a garment, warp, weft, or any leather article that is washed, from which the lesion departs, shall be washed a second time and be clean.
This is the law of a lesion of leprosy in a garment of wool or coarse flax, or in warp or weft, or in any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.

paragraphs: Passage group: Male and female discharges, bodily contact, bedding, washing, waiting periods, offerings and sanctuary protection. Setting: Purity law.

Requirements appearing in this passage: C0533, C0534, C0535, C0536, C0537, C0538, C0539, C0540, C0541, C0542, C0543, C0544, C0545, C0546, C1239. A mixed passage can link to more than one topic or classification.
Leviticus 15:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 15:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If any man has a flow from his body, his flow is unclean.

Leviticus 15:3 — And this is the law of his uncleanness: discharging seed from his body through the flow by which his body has become stopped up, this is his uncleanness in him; all the days of the flow of his body, in which his body has become stopped up through the flow, are his uncleanness.
Leviticus 15:4 — Every bed on which the man with a seminal discharge lies is unclean, and every article on which the man with a seminal discharge sits shall be unclean.
Leviticus 15:5 — And whosoever touches his bed shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:6 — And whosoever sits on an article on which the man with a seminal discharge has sat shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:7 — And whosoever touches the skin of the man with a seminal discharge shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:8 — If the man with a seminal discharge spits on someone clean, that person shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:9 — And any donkey saddle on which the man with a seminal discharge mounts shall be unclean until evening.

Leviticus 15:10 — And whosoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries those things shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:11 — And anyone whom the man with a seminal discharge touches when he has not washed his hands shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:12 — And an earthenware vessel touched by the man with a seminal discharge shall be shattered, and a wooden vessel shall be washed with water and be clean.
Leviticus 15:13 — When the man with a seminal discharge is cleansed from his flow, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be clean.
Leviticus 15:14 — And on the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, bring them before the Lord to the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and give them unto the priest.
Leviticus 15:15 — And the priest shall prepare them, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord for his flow.
Leviticus 15:16 — And if a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:17 — And every garment and every skin on which there is semen shall be washed with water and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:18 — And if a man lies with a woman with an emission of semen, they shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:19 — And if a woman has a flow of blood, her flow shall be in her body; she shall remain in her menstrual discharge for seven days. Whosoever touches her shall be unclean until evening,
Leviticus 15:20 — and everything on which she lies during her menstrual discharge shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.
Leviticus 15:21 — And whosoever touches her bed shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:22 — And whosoever touches any article on which she sits shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:23 — If, while she is on her bed or on the article on which she sits, he touches her, he shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:24 — If anyone lies with her and her uncleanness comes upon him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

Leviticus 15:25 — And if a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual discharge, or if she also has a flow after her menstrual discharge, all the days of her unclean flow shall be like the days of her menstrual discharge; she shall be unclean.

Leviticus 15:26 — And every bed on which she lies during all the days of her flow shall be like the bed of her menstrual discharge, and every article on which she sits shall be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her menstrual discharge.
Leviticus 15:27 — Whosoever touches her shall be unclean. He shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:28 — When she is cleansed from her flow, she shall count seven days, and afterward she shall be cleansed.
Leviticus 15:29 — And on the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them unto the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
Leviticus 15:30 — And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her before the Lord for her unclean flow.
Leviticus 15:31 — And you shall make the sons of Israel wary of their uncleannesses, so that they do not die because of their uncleanness in defiling My tent which is among them.
Leviticus 15:32 — This is the law for the man with a seminal discharge and for anyone who has an emission of semen and becomes defiled through it,

Leviticus 15:33 — and for the woman bleeding in her menstrual discharge, for the one with a seminal discharge in his flow, male or female, and for the man who lies with a woman in menstrual separation.
