verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: This is the word which the Lord commanded, saying:
Any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who slaughters a calf, sheep, or goat in the camp, or slaughters it outside the camp,

and does not bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, to prepare it as a whole burnt offering or an offering of deliverance acceptable unto the Lord for a sweet savour; and whosoever slaughters outside, and does not bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, so as not to present a gift unto the Lord before the tent of the Lord: blood shall be reckoned unto that man; he has poured out blood; that soul shall be destroyed from among his people.

This is so that the sons of Israel may bring up their sacrifices, which they themselves slaughter in the plains; they shall bring them unto the Lord, to the doors of the Tent of Testimony, unto the priest, and sacrifice them as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord.
And the priest shall pour the blood all around against the altar before the Lord beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony and offer up the fat for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the vain things after which they prostitute themselves. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for you throughout your generations.
And you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who prepares a whole burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Testimony to offer it unto the Lord, that person shall be destroyed from among his people.
And any man of the sons of Israel, or of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who eats any blood: I will set My face against the soul that eats the blood, and destroy him from among his people.
For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it unto you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives; for its blood shall make atonement in place of the life.
Therefore I have said unto the sons of Israel: No soul among you shall eat blood; and the resident foreigner attached unto you shall not eat blood.
And any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who hunts a wild animal or bird that may be eaten shall pour out the blood and cover it with earth.
For the life of all flesh is its blood; and I said unto the sons of Israel: You shall eat no blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whosoever eats it shall be destroyed.

And every soul, whether among the natives or among the resident foreigners, that eats an animal which has died or has been taken by wild beasts, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening, and shall be clean.
But if he does not wash his garments and does not bathe his body in water, he shall bear his lawless deed.

And any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who hunts a wild animal or bird that may be eaten shall pour out the blood and cover it with earth.
For the life of all flesh is its blood; and I said unto the sons of Israel: You shall eat no blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whosoever eats it shall be destroyed.

And every soul, whether among the natives or among the resident foreigners, that eats an animal which has died or has been taken by wild beasts, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening, and shall be clean.
But if he does not wash his garments and does not bathe his body in water, he shall bear his lawless deed.

verses.text: You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
And the swine, for it divides the hoof and cleaves its parts, but does not chew the cud, is unclean unto you. Of their flesh you shall not eat, neither shall you touch their carcasses.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

verses.text:
And by these you shall become defiled: everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every animal that divides the hoof and has cleft claws but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
And these are unclean for you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile;
the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole.
These are unclean for you among all the creeping things on the earth. Whosoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

And whosoever eats from these carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.
He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.
For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”
Welcome the one who is weak in faith, but not to dispute over opinions.
One believes he may eat all things, but the weak person eats vegetables.
Do not let the one who eats despise the one who does not eat; and do not let the one who does not eat judge the one who eats, for God welcomed him.
Who are you to judge another’s household slave? To his own master he stands or falls; and he will be made to stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
For one judges one day above another, but another judges every day alike. Let each be fully assured in his own mind.
The one who regards the day regards it for the Lord. And the one who eats eats for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat refrains for the Lord and gives thanks to God.
who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.

verses.text: And the priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears lower than the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.

And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day a second time; and, behold, if the lesion is faint, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, for it is a mark; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the mark has shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy.
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there is a white scar in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is some sound living flesh in the scar,
it is longstanding leprosy on the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and isolate him, for he is unclean.
But if the leprosy breaks out abundantly in the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the lesion from head to foot, throughout the whole view of the priest,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the leprosy has covered all the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean as to the lesion, because it has all turned white; it is clean.
And on whatever day living skin appears on him, he shall be defiled.
And the priest shall examine the sound skin, and the sound skin shall make him unclean, because it is unclean; it is leprosy.
But if the sound skin is restored and turns white, he shall come unto the priest,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the lesion clean; he is clean.

And the priest shall examine it; and, behold, if its appearance is lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin of the body, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy that has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the ulcer; the priest shall declare him clean.

the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the hair in the shining spot has turned white, and its appearance is lower than the skin, it is leprosy which has blossomed in the burn; and the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in the shining spot, and it is not lower than the skin, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day; but if it has indeed spread in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the shining spot stays in its place, has not spread in the skin, and is faint, it is the scar of the burn. The priest shall declare him clean, for it is the mark of the burn.

the priest shall examine the lesion; and, behold, if its appearance is more hollow than the skin, and there is fine yellowish hair in it, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a broken patch, leprosy of the head or leprosy of the beard.

And the priest shall examine the broken patch on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread in the skin after he was shaved, and its appearance is not hollow below the skin, the priest shall declare him clean; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
But if the broken patch has indeed spread in the skin after he has been cleansed,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the broken patch has spread in the skin, the priest shall not inspect for yellow hair, for he is unclean.
But if before him the broken patch has remained in place and black hair has grown in it, the broken patch has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
And if a man or woman has shining, whitish patches on the skin of the body,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there are shining, whitish patches on the skin of his body, it is a white eruption; he is clean. It blossoms in the skin of his body; he is clean.
If anyone loses the hair of his head, he is bald; he is clean.
If he loses the hair at the front of his head, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
But if there is a white or fiery-red lesion on his bald head or bald forehead, it is leprosy on his bald head or bald forehead.
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the appearance of the lesion on his bald head or his bald forehead is white tinged with red, like the appearance of leprosy on the skin of his body,
he is a man with leprosy; the priest shall surely declare him unclean; his lesion is upon his head.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread, and there is no yellowish hair in it, and the appearance of the broken patch is not hollow below the skin,
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

verses.text: And an earthenware vessel touched by the man with a seminal discharge shall be shattered, and a wooden vessel shall be washed with water and be clean.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

paragraphs: Original Scripture: Leviticus 15:31 · Numbers 5:3

Transformed: Hebrews distinguishes the first covenant’s outward washings from cleansing of conscience and access to God through Christ. This entry is classified as a ritual requirement in that covenant setting; ordinary hygiene and protection from illness remain separate practical questions.

verses.text: And you shall make the sons of Israel wary of their uncleannesses, so that they do not die because of their uncleanness in defiling My tent which is among them.
From male unto female, send them outside the camp, and they shall in no wise defile their camps, wherein I dwell among them.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

verses.text: He shall not eat an animal found dead or torn by beasts, becoming unclean through them. I am the Lord.

You shall not eat anything that dies of itself; it shall be given unto the resident alien within your cities, and he shall eat it, or you may sell it unto a foreigner; for you are a holy people unto the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk.
He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods.
He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person.
For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”
Welcome the one who is weak in faith, but not to dispute over opinions.
One believes he may eat all things, but the weak person eats vegetables.
Do not let the one who eats despise the one who does not eat; and do not let the one who does not eat judge the one who eats, for God welcomed him.
Who are you to judge another’s household slave? To his own master he stands or falls; and he will be made to stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
For one judges one day above another, but another judges every day alike. Let each be fully assured in his own mind.
The one who regards the day regards it for the Lord. And the one who eats eats for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat refrains for the Lord and gives thanks to God.
who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
For everything created by God is good, and nothing is to be rejected when received with thanksgiving,
for it is sanctified through the word of God and intercession.

For since ancient times, people in every city have proclaimed Moses, and he is read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”

Then the apostles and elders, with the whole Church, decided to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers.
They wrote by their hand: “The apostles and elders, your brothers, to the brothers from the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings.
Since we have heard that some who went out from among us troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, although we gave them no instruction,
we have decided with one accord to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
men who have given over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves report the same things by word of mouth.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things:
to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”
But flesh with its lifeblood you shall not eat.
It is an everlasting statute throughout your generations, in every dwelling place of yours: you shall eat neither any fat nor any blood.
You shall eat no blood in any dwelling place of yours, whether of birds or of livestock.
Every soul that eats blood, that soul shall perish from among his people.
And any man of the sons of Israel, or of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who eats any blood: I will set My face against the soul that eats the blood, and destroy him from among his people.
For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it unto you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives; for its blood shall make atonement in place of the life.
Therefore I have said unto the sons of Israel: No soul among you shall eat blood; and the resident foreigner attached unto you shall not eat blood.
For the life of all flesh is its blood; and I said unto the sons of Israel: You shall eat no blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whosoever eats it shall be destroyed.
Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.
Take diligent heed that you do not eat blood; for its blood is life, and the life shall not be eaten with the flesh.
You shall not eat it; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.
You shall not eat it, that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, if you do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.

and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
But you have dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into courts?
Do they not blaspheme the good name called over you?
If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
But if you show favoritism, you commit sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
I charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels that you keep these things without prejudgment, doing nothing from partiality.
You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not favour the person of the poor, neither shall you admire the person of the mighty; you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness.

And you shall distinguish them, between the clean livestock and the unclean livestock, and between the clean birds and the unclean; and you shall not make your souls abominable through livestock, or birds, or any creeping things of the earth which I have set apart unto you as unclean.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from the Gentiles who are turning to God,
but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, sexual immorality, what is strangled, and blood.
For since ancient times, people in every city have proclaimed Moses, and he is read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”

Then the apostles and elders, with the whole Church, decided to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers.
They wrote by their hand: “The apostles and elders, your brothers, to the brothers from the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings.
Since we have heard that some who went out from among us troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, although we gave them no instruction,
we have decided with one accord to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
men who have given over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves report the same things by word of mouth.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to place no further burden upon you except these necessary things:
to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.”
Therefore let no one judge you in eating and drinking, or in the matter of a festival or new moon or Sabbaths,
which are a shadow of the things to come, but the body belongs to Christ.
Let no one disqualify you, delighting in humility and worship of angels, dwelling on what he has seen, puffed up without cause by the mind of his flesh,
and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, supplied and knit together through joints and ligaments, grows with the growth of God.
If you died with Christ to the elements of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit to decrees:
“Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch,”
which all concern things that perish with use, according to human commandments and teachings?
These indeed have a reputation of wisdom in self-chosen worship and humility and severe treatment of the body, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.

research.title: The clothing distinction in Deuteronomy 22:5
paragraphs: Study 144: The clothing distinction in Deuteronomy 22:5
Related indexed requirements: C1125, C1126. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: The cited apostolic passages provide guidance about love and conduct; they do not directly resolve the clothing vocabulary or every modern application.
Christian response today: Study the wording and context carefully and retain dignity and love toward people amid interpretive disagreement.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 22:5 Christ and the apostles: Romans 13:9–10 · Colossians 3:12–14
Text and setting: Israelite distinction
Torah: Deuteronomy 22:5

The verse prohibits a woman using what belongs to a man and a man wearing a woman’s clothing. The scope of the first expression and contemporary applications are debated; the text supplies no universal list of modern garments. Interpretations should be identified as such, and Christian application must retain dignity and love of neighbor.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Romans 13:9–10 · Colossians 3:12–14

Connection and evidence: Christian interpretation of the cited passages. The cited apostolic passages provide guidance about love and conduct; they do not directly resolve the clothing vocabulary or every modern application.
This is an editorial Christian application of the cited passages. The New Testament does not separately state that every detail of this particular rule has been fulfilled or universally reimposed.

Where interpretations differ: The original vocabulary and present application of this clothing distinction. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 23:18 (KJV 23:17) Christ and the apostles: 1 Corinthians 6:15–20
Text and setting: Sexual ethics
Torah: Deuteronomy 23:18 (KJV 23:17)

The Hebrew terms in this verse are often rendered as male and female cult prostitutes; translations differ in how explicitly they express the cultic setting. The New Testament independently warns against intercourse with a prostitute. The moral duty concerns sexual faithfulness and freedom from exploitation, not contempt toward vulnerable people.
Read with Christ and the apostles: 1 Corinthians 6:15–20

By coincidence a certain priest was going down that road. He saw him and passed by on the opposite side.
Likewise a Levite also came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the opposite side.
But a certain Samaritan, traveling, came upon him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
He approached and bound his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
On the next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Care for him, and whatever more you spend I will repay you when I return.’
Which of these three seems to you to have become a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”

And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Love does no evil to the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.

Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, inflicted blows, and went away, leaving him half dead.
By coincidence a certain priest was going down that road. He saw him and passed by on the opposite side.
Likewise a Levite also came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the opposite side.
But a certain Samaritan, traveling, came upon him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
He approached and bound his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
On the next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Care for him, and whatever more you spend I will repay you when I return.’

And the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven concerning any of all the things which he has done and wherein he has offended Him.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,
If a soul sins, and utterly disregards the commandments of the Lord, and deals falsely with his neighbour concerning a deposit, or a partnership, or robbery, or any wrong which he has done unto his neighbour,
or finds a lost thing and deals falsely concerning it, and swears unjustly concerning any of all the things which a man may do so as to sin therein,
then it shall be, when he has sinned and incurred guilt, that he shall return the plunder which he seized, or that which he obtained by wrong, or the deposit which was entrusted unto him, or the lost thing which he found,
concerning every matter about which he swore unjustly. And he shall repay the principal, and add a fifth part unto it; he shall repay it unto the one to whom it belongs, on the day when he is convicted.
And for his offence he shall bring unto the Lord an unblemished ram from the flock, of a value corresponding to the offence which he has committed against Him.
And the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven concerning any of all the things which he has done and wherein he has offended Him.

paragraphs: Study 60: Restoring property obtained dishonestly
Related indexed requirements: C0425, C0426. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: The fulfillment mark concerns the offering within the former sacrificial order, not the erasure of responsibility for stolen property.
Christian response today: Stop the dishonesty and make amends; distinguish restitution from attempting to add another atoning sacrifice.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 5:20–26 (KJV 6:1–7) Christ and the apostles: Ephesians 4:28 · Luke 19:8–10 · Hebrews 10:1–18
Text and setting: Restitution and offering law
Torah: Leviticus 5:20–26 (KJV 6:1–7)

The passage requires the return of stolen, extorted, withheld or falsely denied property, with an additional fifth and a guilt offering. Restoring what was taken is part of repentance. The Israelite compensation formula and sanctuary offering should be distinguished from the Christian moral duty to make amends and abandon theft.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Ephesians 4:28 · Luke 19:8–10

Connection and evidence: Christian interpretation of the cited passages. The fulfillment mark concerns the offering within the former sacrificial order, not the erasure of responsibility for stolen property.
This is an editorial Christian application of the cited passages. The New Testament does not separately state that every detail of this particular rule has been fulfilled or universally reimposed.
Additional biblical support: Hebrews 10:1–18

And the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven concerning any of all the things which he has done and wherein he has offended Him.
Let the one who steals steal no longer, but rather let him labor, doing what is good with his own hands, so that he may have something to share with the one in need.
But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, I give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have extorted anything from anyone, I repay it fourfold.”
Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost.”
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.text: You shall not speak evil of the deaf, neither shall you put a stumbling block before the blind; and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.

He also said to the one who had invited Him, “When you give a midday meal or a supper, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and you receive repayment.
But when you give a reception, invite the poor, the disabled, the lame, and the blind.
And you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
But you have dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into courts?
Do they not blaspheme the good name called over you?
If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
But if you show favoritism, you commit sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
You shall not speak evil of the deaf, neither shall you put a stumbling block before the blind; and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.

Leviticus joins a prohibition on slander with a prohibition concerning a neighbor’s blood or life. Christian speech and action should preserve life and dignity, including practical help when someone is in need.

verses.text: You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.

Do not speak against one another, brothers. The one who speaks against a brother or judges his brother speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
By this we have come to know love: He laid down His life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
But whoever has this world’s goods and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him?
Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.

By this we have come to know love: He laid down His life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
But whoever has this world’s goods and sees his brother in need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God abide in him?
Little children, let us not love in word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.

If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
If therefore you offer your gift upon the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,

My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?

verses.text: You shall keep far away from every unrighteous charge; the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, neither shall you justify the ungodly for gifts.
You have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not murder’; and ‘whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.’

But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
If therefore you offer your gift upon the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
Love does no evil to the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.

verses.text:
Instruct the sons of Israel to give the Levites towns to live in from their allotted possessions. They shall also give the Levites the outlying lands around the towns.
And the towns shall be theirs to live in, and their designated lands shall be for their livestock and all their four-footed animals.
And the lands adjoining the towns that you shall give the Levites shall extend two thousand cubits outward from the town wall all around.
And you shall measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the eastern side, and two thousand cubits on the southwestern side, and two thousand cubits on the seaward side, and two thousand cubits on the northern side; and the town shall be in the midst thereof for you, together with the adjoining lands of the towns.
And you shall give the Levites the six cities of refuge that you shall provide for the person who has killed someone to flee to, and in addition to these, forty-two towns.
All the towns you shall give the Levites shall be forty-eight towns, together with their outlying lands.
And for the towns that you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel, take many from those with much and fewer from those with less. Each shall give towns to the Levites according to the inheritance he receives.

verses.text:
And if a man strikes another, and he dies, the one who struck him shall surely be put to death.
But if he did not act willingly, and God delivered him into his hands, I will give you a place where the slayer shall flee.
But if a man attacks his neighbour to kill him by deceit, and flees for refuge, you shall take him from My altar to put him to death.
He who strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
He who reviles his father or his mother shall surely die.
And if a man steals one of the sons of Israel, and overpowers him and sells him, and he is found with him, he shall surely die.
And if two men quarrel, and one strikes his neighbour with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die, but lies on his bed,
if the man rises and walks outside with a staff, the one who struck him shall be guiltless; only he shall pay for his lost labour and his healing.
And if a man strikes his male slave or his female slave with a rod, and the slave dies under his hands, he shall surely be avenged by judgment.
But if the slave survives a day or two, he shall not be avenged; for he is his silver.
And if two men fight and strike a woman with child, and her child comes out not fully formed, he shall surely be fined; as the woman’s husband shall impose on him, he shall pay according to an assessment.
But if it was fully formed, he shall give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
And if a man strikes the eye of his household slave or of his female slave, and blinds it, he shall set them free for their eye.
And if he knocks out the tooth of his household slave or of his female slave, he shall set them free for their tooth.
And if a bull gores a man or a woman, and the person dies, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall be guiltless.
But if the bull was in the habit of goring before, and its owner has been warned, and he does not remove it, and it kills a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner also shall die.
But if a ransom is imposed on him, he shall give for the ransom of his life all that they impose on him.
Whether it gores a son or a daughter, they shall deal with him according to this ordinance.
And if the bull gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.
And if a man opens a pit, or hews out a pit, and does not cover it, and a calf or donkey falls in it,
the owner of the pit shall make restitution. He shall give silver to the animal’s owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
And if a man’s bull gores his neighbour’s bull, and it dies, they shall sell the living bull and divide its silver; and they shall also divide the dead bull.
But if the bull is known to have been in the habit of goring before, and its owner has been warned, and he does not remove it, he shall repay bull for bull; and the dead bull shall be his.

Connection to Christ: Paul cites the ruler clause in Acts; the apostles also teach obedience to God above conflicting human commands.
Christian response today: Speak responsibly about leaders while retaining honest criticism and obedience to God.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 22:27 (KJV 22:28) Christ and the apostles: Acts 23:5 · 1 Peter 2:17 · Acts 5:29
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Exodus 22:27 (KJV 22:28)

The ruler clause forbids cursing the people’s ruler and is cited by Paul in Acts. The preceding Hebrew term is variously translated as God, gods or judges; that textual question should not be hidden. Respect for authority does not remove the duty to obey God when human commands conflict with Him. Respectful conduct and truthful criticism should not be confused with unquestioning approval of every ruler.

The passage forbids spreading a false report and joining a wicked person as a malicious witness. It concerns both communication and judicial integrity. Let every soul submit to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been appointed by God.
Therefore the one who sets himself against authority has resisted God’s ordering, and those who resist will receive judgment upon themselves.
For rulers are not a terror to good work, but to evil. Do you want to be free from fear of the authority? Do the good, and you will have praise from it;

for it is God’s servant to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for it does not bear the sword without purpose. For it is God’s servant, an avenger who brings wrath on the one who practices evil.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
But you have dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into courts?
Do they not blaspheme the good name called over you?

A single witness is insufficient for conviction under these provisions; the law requires two or three witnesses. Jesus and Paul use related safeguards in community discipline. The requirement does not mean an initial allegation should be ignored or that several people repeating the same rumor become independent witnesses. Investigation and fair process remain essential.

One witness shall not suffice to testify against a man concerning any injustice, or any trespass, or any sin which he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, and at the mouth of three witnesses, shall every matter be established.
If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother.
But if he does not hear, take one or two more with you, so that every matter may be established upon the mouth of two or three witnesses.
If he refuses to hear them, tell the Church. And if he refuses to hear even the Church, let him be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.

Connection to Christ: New Testament warnings against unjust judgment and private vengeance guide reflection on this formal judicial procedure.

Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 19:16–21 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 7:1–5 · Romans 12:19
Text and setting: Civil law
Torah: Deuteronomy 19:16–21

Judges must investigate a disputed accusation carefully; a malicious witness faces the consequence intended for the accused. This is a formal judicial procedure, not permission for an offended person to retaliate. Christian readers should preserve the concern for evidence and fairness while distinguishing public justice from personal revenge.

Connection to Christ: Romans teaches personal accountability before God; the connection to Israel’s judicial safeguard is thematic.
Christian response today: Do not punish relatives for another person’s offense or confuse personal accountability with collective blame.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 24:16 Christ and the apostles: Romans 14:10–12
Text and setting: Civil safeguard
Torah: Deuteronomy 24:16

The text forbids executing parents for their children’s offense or children for their parents’ offense. It limits human judicial punishment; it does not command execution for every kind of sin. Paul likewise speaks of each person giving an account to God, which should not be confused with authorization for collective punishment by human authorities.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Romans 14:10–12

verses.text: These are the words which Moses spoke unto all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness toward the west, near the Red Sea, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Aulon, and Katachrysea.
It is a journey of eleven days from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir unto Kadesh-barnea.

And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spoke unto all the sons of Israel, according to all that the Lord had commanded him concerning them.
After he had smitten Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who dwelt in Ashtaroth and in Edrei,
beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to make this law plain, saying:
The Lord our God spoke unto us in Horeb, saying: Let it suffice you to have dwelt in this mountain.

Turn and set forth, and enter the hill country of the Amorites and all the neighbouring places of Arabah, the hill country and the plain, the southwest and the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites and Anti-Lebanon, as far as the great river Euphrates.
Behold, I have delivered the land before you. Enter and inherit the land which I sware unto your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give unto them and unto their seed after them.
And I spoke unto you at that time, saying: I shall not be able to bear you alone.
The Lord your God has multiplied you, and behold, you are this day as the stars of heaven in multitude.
The Lord, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you, as He has spoken unto you.
How shall I alone be able to bear your trouble, and your resistance, and your disputes?
Choose for yourselves wise men, men of knowledge and understanding, for your tribes, and I will appoint them to rule over you.
And you answered me and said: The thing which you have spoken is good to do.

And I took from among you wise men, men of knowledge and understanding, and appointed them to rule over you, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens, and recording officers for your judges.
And I commanded your judges at that time, saying: Hear the matters between your brethren, and judge justly between a man and his brother and the sojourner with him.

You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall judge the small and the great alike. You shall not shrink before the face of man, for judgment belongs unto God. And you shall bring unto me the matter which is too hard for you, and I will hear it.
And I commanded you at that time all the things which you should do.

And we departed from Horeb, and went through all that great and fearful wilderness which you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorite, as the Lord our God commanded us; and we came unto Kadesh-barnea.
And I said unto you: You have come unto the hill country of the Amorite, which the Lord our God gives you.
Behold, the Lord your God has delivered the land before you. Go up and inherit it, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has spoken unto you; fear not, neither be dismayed.

And you all came unto me, and said: Let us send men before us, and let them search out the land for us, and bring us word of the way by which we shall go up, and of the cities into which we shall enter.
And the saying pleased me; and I took twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
And they turned and went up into the hill country, and came unto the Valley of the Cluster, and searched it out.
And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down unto us, and said: The land which the Lord our God gives us is good.
And you would not go up, but disobeyed the word of the Lord your God.
And you murmured in your tents, and said: Because the Lord hates us, He brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites, to destroy us.

Whither do we go up? Your brethren have made your heart fail, saying: The nation is great and numerous and mightier than we; and the cities are great and walled up to heaven. Moreover, we have seen sons of giants there.
And I said unto you: Neither cower nor fear them.
The Lord your God, who goes before you, shall Himself fight against them with you, according to all that He did for you in the land of Egypt,
and in this wilderness which you saw, how the Lord your God nurtured you as a man nurtures his son, in all the way which you went, until you came unto this place.
And in this matter you did not trust the Lord your God,
who goes before you in the way to choose a place for you, guiding you in fire by night, to show you the way wherein you should go, and in a cloud by day.
And the Lord heard the voice of your words, and, being provoked to anger, sware, saying:
Surely none of these men shall see this good land which I sware unto their fathers,
save Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and I will give unto him and unto his sons the land whereon he trod, because he cleaved unto the things of the Lord.
And the Lord was angry with me also for your sakes, saying: You shall not enter there either.
Joshua son of Nun, who stands beside you, he shall enter there. Strengthen him, for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.
And every young child who this day knows neither good nor evil shall enter there; and I will give it unto them, and they shall inherit it.
But you, turn and encamp in the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.

And you answered me and said: We have sinned before the Lord our God. We will go up and fight, according to all that the Lord our God commanded us. And you took up, every man, his weapons of war, and gathered yourselves together, and went up into the hill country.
And the Lord said unto me: Say unto them, You shall not go up, neither shall you fight, for I am not with you; and you shall not be crushed before your enemies.
And I spoke unto you, but you did not hearken unto me; and you transgressed the word of the Lord, and forced your way up into the hill country.
And the Amorites who dwelt in that hill country came out to meet you, and pursued you as bees do, and wounded you from Seir unto Hormah.
And you sat down and wept before the Lord; but the Lord did not hearken unto your voice, neither gave He heed unto you.
And you dwelt in Kadesh many days, as many days as you dwelt there.

as when a man goes with his neighbour into the forest to gather wood, and his hand is jolted with the axe as he cuts the wood, and the iron slips from the wood and strikes his neighbour, so that he dies, he shall flee unto one of these cities and live;

But if the bull was in the habit of goring before, and its owner has been warned, and he does not remove it, and it kills a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner also shall die.
But if a ransom is imposed on him, he shall give for the ransom of his life all that they impose on him.
Whether it gores a son or a daughter, they shall deal with him according to this ordinance.
And if the bull gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.
And if a man opens a pit, or hews out a pit, and does not cover it, and a calf or donkey falls in it,

And if a bull gores a man or a woman, and the person dies, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall be guiltless.
But if the bull was in the habit of goring before, and its owner has been warned, and he does not remove it, and it kills a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner also shall die.
But if a ransom is imposed on him, he shall give for the ransom of his life all that they impose on him.
Whether it gores a son or a daughter, they shall deal with him according to this ordinance.
And if the bull gores a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.

the owner of the pit shall make restitution. He shall give silver to the animal’s owner, and the dead animal shall be his.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Command the sons of Israel to bring Me pure beaten olive oil for light, to burn a lamp continually.
Outside the veil, in the Tent of Testimony, Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening to morning before the Lord continually. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations.
You shall burn the lamps upon the pure lampstand before the Lord until morning.
And you shall take fine flour and make twelve loaves from it. Each loaf shall contain two tenths.
And you shall place them in two arrangements, six in each arrangement, on the pure table before the Lord.
And you shall put pure frankincense and salt upon the arrangement. They shall be set before the Lord as a memorial for the loaves.
On the Sabbath day he shall set it before the Lord continually, before the sons of Israel as an everlasting covenant.
And it shall belong unto Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat these things in a holy place, for this is most holy for him from the things sacrificed unto the Lord, an everlasting ordinance.
And the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the sons of Israel. The Israelite woman’s son and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
And the Israelite woman’s son pronounced the Name and cursed, and they brought him unto Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
And they placed him in custody, to judge him by the Lord’s command.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Bring the one who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him shall lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation shall stone him.
And speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: A man who curses God shall bear sin.

Let one who names the Lord’s name surely be put to death. Let the whole congregation of Israel stone him with stones. Whether resident foreigner or native-born, when he names the Lord’s name, let him die.
And if a man strikes a human being and the person dies, he shall surely be put to death.
And one who strikes an animal and it dies shall repay life for life.
And if anyone causes an injury unto his neighbour, as he has done unto him, so shall it be done unto him in return:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he has caused an injury unto a man, so shall it be inflicted upon him.
One who strikes a human being and the person dies shall surely be put to death.
There shall be one judgment for the resident foreigner and the local inhabitant, for I am the Lord your God.
And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel. They brought the one who cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. The sons of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses on the western side of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
Instruct the sons of Israel to give the Levites towns to live in from their allotted possessions. They shall also give the Levites the outlying lands around the towns.
And the towns shall be theirs to live in, and their designated lands shall be for their livestock and all their four-footed animals.

And you shall measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the eastern side, and two thousand cubits on the southwestern side, and two thousand cubits on the seaward side, and two thousand cubits on the northern side; and the town shall be in the midst thereof for you, together with the adjoining lands of the towns.
And you shall give the Levites the six cities of refuge that you shall provide for the person who has killed someone to flee to, and in addition to these, forty-two towns.
All the towns you shall give the Levites shall be forty-eight towns, together with their outlying lands.

And for the towns that you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel, take many from those with much and fewer from those with less. Each shall give towns to the Levites according to the inheritance he receives.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
and you shall set apart towns for yourselves. They shall be refuges for the killer to flee there, anyone who has struck a person unintentionally.
And the towns shall be refuges for you from the kinsman who avenges blood, so that the killer shall in no wise die before standing before the congregation for judgment.
And the towns you shall provide, the six towns, shall be refuges for you.
You shall provide three towns across the Jordan, and you shall provide three towns in the land of Canaan.

There shall be a refuge for the sons of Israel; for the sojourner and the resident stranger among you, these towns shall also be refuges, so that anyone who strikes a person unintentionally may flee there.
But if he strikes someone with an iron object and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
If he strikes someone with a stone from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
If he strikes someone with a wooden object from his hand capable of causing death and that person dies, he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death.
The kinsman who avenges blood shall himself kill the murderer. When he encounters him, he shall kill him.
If he pushes someone out of enmity and throws an object at him from ambush and that person dies,

or strikes him with his hand out of wrath and he dies, let the one who struck him surely be put to death; he is a murderer. Let the murderer surely be put to death. The kinsman who avenges blood shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
But if he suddenly pushes someone without enmity, or throws any object at him without ambush,
or, without his knowing, a stone capable of causing death falls upon him and he dies, though he was not his enemy and was not seeking to harm him,
And then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck him and the kinsman who avenges blood according to these judgments.

And the congregation shall rescue the killer from the kinsman who avenges blood and restore him to the city of refuge to which he fled. He shall live there until the high priest dies, whom they anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer goes outside the boundaries of the city to which he fled,
and the kinsman who avenges blood finds him outside the boundaries of his city of refuge and kills the killer, the avenger is not liable.
For he must live in the city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the death of the high priest, the killer may return to the land of his possession.
And these shall be an ordinance of judgment for you throughout your generations in all your settlements.
In every case of a person being struck down, you shall put the killer to death through witnesses. A single witness shall not testify against a person so as to cause his death.
And you shall not accept a ransom for a life from the killer who is guilty and liable to be killed; he shall surely be put to death.
You shall not accept a ransom concerning flight to a city of refuge, allowing him to live in the land again before the high priest dies.

And you shall in no wise stain with murder the land wherein you dwell; for this blood stains the land with murder, and atonement shall not be made for the land for the blood shed upon it, except by the blood of him who shed it.
And you shall not defile the land in which you dwell, in which I will dwell among you, for I am the Lord, dwelling among the sons of Israel.

Jesus takes up the eye-for-eye formulation and teaches disciples nonretaliation. Paul likewise forbids personal vengeance. This concerns the disciple’s response; it is not a claim that Jesus abolished civil courts or responsibility for injury.

title: Do not establish a charge by a single witness
audience_note: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
paragraphs: Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
Classification: Unchanged · Torah requirement
Topic: Justice, testimony, government and war

The requirement for corroborated testimony is explicitly reused in church correction and accusations against elders. Its continued use is tied to those proceedings; it does not import Israel’s capital penalties.
Full research entry

verses.text: One witness shall not suffice to testify against a man concerning any injustice, or any trespass, or any sin which he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, and at the mouth of three witnesses, shall every matter be established.

verses.text: One witness shall not suffice to testify against a man concerning any injustice, or any trespass, or any sin which he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, and at the mouth of three witnesses, shall every matter be established.
If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother.
But if he does not hear, take one or two more with you, so that every matter may be established upon the mouth of two or three witnesses.

verses.text: You shall have no other gods except Me.
You shall have no other gods before Me.
Then Jesus said to him, “Go away, Satan! For it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him alone shall you serve.’”
Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
I speak as to wise people; judge for yourselves what I say.
The cup of blessing that we bless—is it not participation in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break—is it not participation in the body of Christ?
Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.
Consider Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?
What, then, am I saying? That food offered to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
Rather, that what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. And I do not want you to become participants with demons.
You cannot drink the Lord’s cup and the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the Lord’s table and the table of demons.
Little children, guard yourselves from idols.
You shall have no other gods except Me.

paragraphs: Study 20: Rejecting images as objects of worship
Related indexed requirements: C0147, C0148, C0149, C0256, C0258, C0259. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Acts and First John reject idolatry; Christian traditions distinguish images and their religious use differently.
Christian response today: Reject worship of created substitutes for God and examine the distinction between art, veneration and worship.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 20:4–6 · Exodus 25:18–22 Christ and the apostles: Acts 17:29 · 1 John 5:21
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Exodus 20:4–6 · Exodus 25:18–22

The prohibition joins making images with bowing to and serving them. The same Torah also commands cherubim in the sanctuary, so the passages require more care than a blanket ban on every work of art. Christian traditions differ over religious images; all must reckon with the rejection of idolatry and created substitutes for God.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Acts 17:29 · 1 John 5:21

The ban on the names of other gods stands in a context of covenant loyalty and worship. The Torah prohibits divination and related practices that seek guidance or power apart from the Lord. Acts describes converts abandoning magical practices, and Galatians includes sorcery among works of the flesh.
