verses.text: And these are the ordinances and judgments which the Lord commanded the sons of Israel in the wilderness, when they came forth out of the land of Egypt: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength.
One of the scribes approached, having heard them disputing and seen that He had answered them well. He asked Him, “Which commandment is first of all?”
Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.’
The second is this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe said to Him, “Well said, Teacher! Thou hast truly said that He is one, and there is no other besides Him.
To love Him with the whole heart, with the whole understanding, and with the whole strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
Seeing that he answered thoughtfully, Jesus said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” No one dared to question Him any further.
He said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
This is the great and first commandment.
A second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets.”

And these are the ordinances and judgments which the Lord commanded the sons of Israel in the wilderness, when they came forth out of the land of Egypt: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.

verse_units.text: Take heed unto yourself, lest you forget the Lord your God, and fail to keep His commandments, and His judgments, and His ordinances which I command you this day;
lest, when you have eaten and are filled, and have built good houses and dwelt in them,
and your herds and your flocks are multiplied, and your silver and your gold are multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied,
you become lifted up in heart, and forget the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;

who led you through that great and fearful wilderness, wherein were biting serpents, and scorpions, and thirst, where there was no water; who brought forth for you a spring of water out of the sheer rock;
who fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and to test you, and to do you good in your latter days.
Do not say in your heart: My strength and the might of my hand have gotten me this great wealth.
And you shall remember the Lord your God, for He gives you strength to gain wealth, that He may establish His covenant which the Lord sware unto your fathers, as at this day.

beyond the Jordan, in the ravine near the house of Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel smote when they came forth out of the land of Egypt.
And they inherited his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two Amorite kings beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise,
from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon torrent as far as Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,
all the Arabah beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, below Asedoth, the hewn height.

And now, O Israel, hear the ordinances and the judgments which I teach you this day to do, that you may live and be multiplied, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord, the God of your fathers, gives you.
You shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it; you shall keep the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day.
Your eyes have seen all that the Lord our God did unto Baal-peor; for every man who went after Baal-peor, the Lord your God blotted him out from among you.
But you who cleave unto the Lord your God are all alive this day.
Behold, I have shown you ordinances and judgments, as the Lord commanded me, that you should do so in the land whither you go to inherit it.

And you shall keep and do them; for this is your wisdom and understanding before all the nations, who shall hear all these ordinances and say: Behold, this great nation is a wise and understanding people.
For what great nation is there whose god draws near unto them, as the Lord our God in all things wherein we call upon Him?
And what great nation is there that has ordinances and judgments as righteous as all this law which I set before you this day?

Take heed unto yourself, and guard your soul diligently, lest you forget all the things which your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. And you shall teach your sons and your sons’ sons

the day when you stood before the Lord your God in Horeb, in the day of the assembly, when the Lord said unto me: Assemble the people unto Me, and let them hear My words, that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live upon the earth, and may teach their sons.
And you drew near and stood beneath the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire unto heaven, with darkness, gloom, tempest, and a great sound.
And the Lord spoke unto you out of the midst of the fire; you heard the sound of words, but saw no likeness, only a voice.
And He declared unto you His covenant, which He commanded you to do, even the ten words; and He wrote them upon two tablets of stone.
And the Lord commanded me at that time to teach you ordinances and judgments, that you should do them in the land whither you go to inherit it.
And you shall guard your souls diligently; for you saw no likeness in the day when the Lord spoke unto you in Horeb, on the mountain, out of the midst of the fire,
lest you act lawlessly and make for yourselves a graven likeness, any image, the likeness of male or female,

the likeness of any creeping thing that creeps upon the earth, the likeness of any fish that is in the waters beneath the earth.

And if you beget sons and sons’ sons, and you have remained long upon the land, and act lawlessly, and make a graven likeness of anything, and do evil before the Lord your God, to provoke Him to anger,

And there you shall serve other gods, the works of men’s hands, wood and stone, which shall neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
And there you shall seek the Lord your God, and shall find Him, when you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul, in your distress.
And all these things shall find you in the latter days, and you shall return unto the Lord your God, and hearken unto His voice.
For the Lord your God is a merciful God; He will not forsake you, neither will He destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which He sware unto them.

Ask now of the former days that were before you, from the day when God created man upon the earth, and from one end of heaven unto the other: has there been anything like this great matter, or has such a thing been heard?
Has a nation heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?

Or has God attempted to go and take unto Himself a nation from the midst of a nation, by trial, and by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by an uplifted arm, and by great visions, according to all that the Lord our God did in Egypt before your eyes?

verses.text: At that time the Lord said unto me: Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like unto the first, and come up unto Me into the mountain; and you shall make for yourself an ark of wood.

And I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets into the ark which I had made; and they were there, as the Lord commanded me.
And the sons of Israel set out from Beeroth of the sons of Iakim to Misadai. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
From there they set out to Gadgad, and from Gadgad to Jotbathah, a land of flowing torrents.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister, and to bless in His name, unto this day.
Therefore the Levites have no portion or inheritance among their brethren; the Lord Himself is his inheritance, as He spoke unto him.
And I abode in the mountain forty days and forty nights; and the Lord hearkened unto me at that time also, and the Lord would not destroy you.
And the Lord said unto me: Go, set forth before this people, and let them enter and inherit the land which I sware unto their fathers to give them.

And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and His ordinances which I command you this day, that it may be well with you?
Behold, unto the Lord your God belong heaven and the heaven of heaven, the earth and all that is therein.
Yet the Lord preferred your fathers, to love them, and chose their seed after them, even you, above all the nations, as at this day.
And you shall circumcise your hardness of heart, and shall stiffen your neck no more.
For the Lord your God, He is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and fearful God, who shows no partiality, neither takes a bribe;
who executes judgment for the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow, and loves the sojourner, to give him bread and clothing.
And you shall love the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve Him, and you shall cleave unto Him, and you shall swear by His name.
He is your boast, and He is your God, who has done among you these great and glorious things which your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy souls; but now the Lord your God has made you as the stars of heaven in multitude.

verses.text: And you shall love the Lord your God, and keep His charge, and His ordinances, and His judgments, all your days.
And know this day that I speak unto you, not unto your children, who have neither known nor seen the chastening of the Lord your God, and His mighty deeds, and His mighty hand, and His uplifted arm,
and His signs and His wonders which He did in the midst of Egypt unto Pharaoh king of Egypt and unto all his land,

and what He did unto the host of the Egyptians, unto their chariots and their horsemen, when He caused the water of the Red Sea to overflow them as they pursued you, and the Lord destroyed them unto this day,
and what He did unto you in the wilderness, until you came unto this place,

and what He did unto Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them, and their houses, and their tents, and all their substance that was with them, in the midst of all Israel.
For your eyes have seen all the great works of the Lord, which He has done unto you this day.
And you shall keep all His commandments which I command you this day, that you may live and multiply, and enter and inherit the land whither you pass over the Jordan to inherit it,
that you may prolong your days upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give unto them and unto their seed after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land whither you go to inherit it is not as the land of Egypt, whence you came forth, where they sow seed and water it with their feet, as a garden of herbs.
But the land whither you go to inherit it is a land of hills and plains; it shall drink water of the rain of heaven,
a land which the Lord your God cares for; the eyes of the Lord your God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year.
And if you diligently hearken unto all His commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
He shall give the rain unto your land in its season, the early and the latter rain; and you shall gather in your grain, and your wine, and your oil.
And He shall give grass in your fields for your cattle; and when you have eaten and are filled,
take heed unto yourself, lest your heart be enlarged, and you transgress, and serve other gods, and bow down unto them,

and the Lord be kindled to wrath against you, and shut up heaven, so that there is no rain, and the land does not yield her fruit, and you perish speedily from the good land which the Lord has given you.
And you shall lay these words in your heart and in your soul, and bind them for a sign upon your hand, and it shall be immovable before your eyes.
And you shall teach them unto your children, to speak of them when you sit in the house, and when you walk in the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your houses and of your gates,
that your days and the days of your sons may be prolonged upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.
And it shall be, if you diligently hearken unto all these commandments which I command you this day to do, to love the Lord our God, and to walk in all His ways, and to cleave unto Him,
that the Lord shall cast out all these nations from before you, and you shall inherit nations great and mightier than you.

Every place whereon the sole of your foot shall tread shall be yours. From the wilderness and Anti-Lebanon, and from the great river, the river Euphrates, even unto the western sea, shall be your borders.
None shall stand before you; the Lord your God shall lay the dread of you and the fear of you upon all the land whereon you shall tread, as the Lord has spoken unto you.
Behold, I set before you this day a blessing and a curse:
the blessing, if you hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day;

and the curses, if you do not hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you this day, and wander from the way which I commanded you, going to serve other gods which you have not known.
And it shall be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land whither you pass over to inherit it, that you shall set the blessing upon Mount Gerizim, and the curse upon Mount Ebal.
Behold, are they not beyond the Jordan, behind the way of the setting sun, in the land of Canaan that lies toward the west, adjoining Gilgal, near the lofty oak?
For you pass over the Jordan, to enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession for ever; and you shall inherit it, and dwell therein.
And you shall take heed to do all His ordinances and these judgments, which I set before you this day.
And you shall love the Lord your God, and keep His charge, and His ordinances, and His judgments, all your days.

Deuteronomy 28:1 — And it shall be, when you pass over the Jordan into the land which the Lord your God gives you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that the Lord your God shall set you above all the nations of the earth.
Deuteronomy 28:2 — And all these blessings shall come upon you, and find you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 28:3 — Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field.
Deuteronomy 28:4 — Blessed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Deuteronomy 28:5 — Blessed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Deuteronomy 28:6 — Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.
Deuteronomy 28:7 — The Lord your God deliver your enemies who rise against you, crushed before your face. By one way shall they come out against you, and by seven ways shall they flee before you.
Deuteronomy 28:8 — The Lord send His blessing upon you in your storerooms, and in all that you put your hand unto, upon the land which the Lord your God gives you.
Deuteronomy 28:9 — The Lord your God establish you unto Himself a holy people, as He sware unto your fathers, if you hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, and walk in His ways.
Deuteronomy 28:10 — And all the nations of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you.

Deuteronomy 28:11 — And the Lord your God shall multiply you in good things, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle, upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give you.

Deuteronomy 28:12 — The Lord open unto you His good treasure, heaven, to give rain unto your land in its season, and to bless all the works of your hands. And you shall lend unto many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.

Deuteronomy 28:13 — The Lord your God make you the head, and not the tail; and you shall be above, and not beneath, if you hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day to keep and do.
Deuteronomy 28:14 — You shall not turn aside from any of the words which I command you this day, to the right hand or to the left, to go after other gods and serve them.

Deuteronomy 28:15 — And it shall be, if you do not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that all these curses shall come upon you, and overtake you.
Deuteronomy 28:16 — Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.
Deuteronomy 28:17 — Cursed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Deuteronomy 28:18 — Cursed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Deuteronomy 28:19 — Cursed are you when you go out, and cursed are you when you come in.

Deuteronomy 28:20 — The Lord send upon you want, and famine, and wasting, in all that you put your hand unto, whatsoever you do, until He destroys you, and causes you to perish speedily, because of your evil practices, because you have forsaken Me.
Deuteronomy 28:21 — The Lord make death cleave unto you, until He consumes you from the land whither you go to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 28:22 — The Lord smite you with destitution, and fever, and chills, and inflammation, and slaughter, and wind blight, and pallor; and they shall pursue you until they destroy you.
Deuteronomy 28:23 — And the heaven above your head shall be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
Deuteronomy 28:24 — The Lord give dust for the rain of your land; and earth shall descend upon you from heaven, until He wears you away, and until He destroys you.

Deuteronomy 28:25 — The Lord give you over to slaughter before your enemies. You shall go forth by one way against them, and you shall flee by seven ways before them; and you shall be scattered among all the kingdoms of the earth.
Deuteronomy 28:26 — And your dead shall be food for the birds of heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and there shall be none to drive them away.
Deuteronomy 28:27 — The Lord smite you with the Egyptian ulcer upon the buttocks, and with grievous scab, and with itching, so that you cannot be healed.
Deuteronomy 28:28 — The Lord smite you with madness, and with blindness, and with bewilderment of mind.

Deuteronomy 28:29 — And you shall grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and He shall not prosper your ways; and you shall be wronged and plundered all your days, and there shall be none to help you.
Deuteronomy 28:30 — You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and shall not dwell therein; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather its fruit.

Deuteronomy 28:31 — Your calf shall be slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat thereof; your donkey shall be seized from you, and shall not be restored unto you; your sheep shall be given unto your enemies, and there shall be none to help you.
Deuteronomy 28:32 — Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another nation, and your eyes shall look upon them and waste away; and your hand shall have no strength.
Deuteronomy 28:33 — A nation which you do not know shall consume the yield of your land and all your labours; and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days.
Deuteronomy 28:34 — And you shall be driven mad by the sights which your eyes shall see.
Deuteronomy 28:35 — The Lord smite you upon the knees and upon the legs with a grievous ulcer, so that you cannot be healed, from the soles of your feet unto the crown of your head.

verses.text: And it shall be, when you pass over the Jordan into the land which the Lord your God gives you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that the Lord your God shall set you above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings shall come upon you, and find you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.
Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field.
Blessed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Blessed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.
The Lord your God deliver your enemies who rise against you, crushed before your face. By one way shall they come out against you, and by seven ways shall they flee before you.
The Lord send His blessing upon you in your storerooms, and in all that you put your hand unto, upon the land which the Lord your God gives you.
The Lord your God establish you unto Himself a holy people, as He sware unto your fathers, if you hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, and walk in His ways.
And all the nations of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you.

And the Lord your God shall multiply you in good things, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle, upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give you.

The Lord open unto you His good treasure, heaven, to give rain unto your land in its season, and to bless all the works of your hands. And you shall lend unto many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.
The Lord your God make you the head, and not the tail; and you shall be above, and not beneath, if you hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day to keep and do.
You shall not turn aside from any of the words which I command you this day, to the right hand or to the left, to go after other gods and serve them.

And it shall be, if you do not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that all these curses shall come upon you, and overtake you.
Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.
Cursed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Cursed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Cursed are you when you go out, and cursed are you when you come in.

The Lord send upon you want, and famine, and wasting, in all that you put your hand unto, whatsoever you do, until He destroys you, and causes you to perish speedily, because of your evil practices, because you have forsaken Me.
The Lord make death cleave unto you, until He consumes you from the land whither you go to inherit it.
The Lord smite you with destitution, and fever, and chills, and inflammation, and slaughter, and wind blight, and pallor; and they shall pursue you until they destroy you.
And the heaven above your head shall be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
The Lord give dust for the rain of your land; and earth shall descend upon you from heaven, until He wears you away, and until He destroys you.

The Lord give you over to slaughter before your enemies. You shall go forth by one way against them, and you shall flee by seven ways before them; and you shall be scattered among all the kingdoms of the earth.
And your dead shall be food for the birds of heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and there shall be none to drive them away.
The Lord smite you with the Egyptian ulcer upon the buttocks, and with grievous scab, and with itching, so that you cannot be healed.
The Lord smite you with madness, and with blindness, and with bewilderment of mind.
And you shall grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and He shall not prosper your ways; and you shall be wronged and plundered all your days, and there shall be none to help you.
You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and shall not dwell therein; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather its fruit.

Your calf shall be slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat thereof; your donkey shall be seized from you, and shall not be restored unto you; your sheep shall be given unto your enemies, and there shall be none to help you.
Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another nation, and your eyes shall look upon them and waste away; and your hand shall have no strength.
A nation which you do not know shall consume the yield of your land and all your labours; and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days.
And you shall be driven mad by the sights which your eyes shall see.
The Lord smite you upon the knees and upon the legs with a grievous ulcer, so that you cannot be healed, from the soles of your feet unto the crown of your head.

You shall beget sons and daughters, but they shall not be yours; for they shall go into captivity.
Blight shall consume all your trees and the produce of your land.

Genesis 17:1 — And when Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am your God; be pleasing before Me, and be blameless.
Genesis 17:2 — And I will set My covenant between Me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly.”
Genesis 17:3 — And Abram fell upon his face; and God spoke to him, saying,
Genesis 17:4 — “As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you, and you shall be a father of a multitude of nations.
Genesis 17:5 — And your name shall no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you a father of many nations.
Genesis 17:6 — And I will increase you exceedingly, exceedingly, and will make nations of you; and kings shall come from you.
Genesis 17:7 — And I will establish My covenant between Me and you and your seed after you throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, to be your God and the God of your seed after you.
Genesis 17:8 — And I will give to you, and to your seed after you, the land where you live as a stranger, all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.”
Genesis 17:9 — And God said to Abraham, “And you shall keep My covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the congregation of the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God.
Each shall revere his father and his mother, and you shall keep My Sabbaths. I am the Lord your God.
You shall not follow idols, neither shall you make cast gods for yourselves; I am the Lord your God.
And if you sacrifice a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, you shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable for you.
It shall be eaten on the day when you sacrifice it and on the morrow; and if any remains until the third day, it shall be burned with fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is unfit for sacrifice; it shall not be accepted.
But he that eats it shall bear sin, for he has profaned the holy things of the Lord; and the souls that eat shall be destroyed from among their people.
And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the harvest of your field; and you shall not gather what falls from your harvest,
neither shall you glean your vineyard again, nor gather the grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the resident foreigner; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not steal. You shall not lie. No one shall defraud his neighbour.
And you shall not swear by My name for an unjust cause, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord your God.
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
You shall not speak evil of the deaf, neither shall you put a stumbling block before the blind; and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not favour the person of the poor, neither shall you admire the person of the mighty; you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness.
You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not hate your brother in your mind; you shall surely reprove your neighbour, and you shall not bear sin because of him.
And your hand shall not take vengeance, neither shall you remain angry with the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbour as yourself; I am the Lord.

You shall keep My law; you shall not mate your livestock with a different stock, neither shall you sow your vineyard with a different kind, nor put upon yourself a spurious garment woven of two materials.

And if anyone lies with a woman with an emission of semen, and she is a household slave reserved for a man but has not been ransomed or given freedom, there shall be an inquiry concerning them. They shall not die, because she has not been freed.
And he shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord beside the door of the Tent of Testimony, a ram for a guilt offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for the sin he has committed, and the sin he has committed shall be forgiven him.

But when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives unto you, and plant any tree for food, you shall purge its uncleanness; its fruit shall be unpurged unto you three years; it shall not be eaten.
And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, praiseworthy unto the Lord.
But in the fifth year you shall eat the fruit; its produce shall be an increase unto you; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not eat on the mountains. You shall not divine by omens or observe birds for divination.
You shall not make a sisoe from the hair of your head or spoil the appearance of your beards.
And you shall make no incisions in your body for a dead person, neither shall you put tattooed letters upon yourselves; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land prostitute itself and the land be filled with lawlessness.
You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.
You shall not follow spirit mediums, neither shall you attach yourselves unto enchanters, to be defiled by them; I am the Lord your God.
You shall rise before the face of the grey-haired, and honour the person of an elder, and fear your God; I am the Lord your God.
If a resident foreigner comes to you in your land, you shall not oppress him.
The resident foreigner who approaches you shall be as the native among you; and you shall love him as yourself, for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.
You shall do no injustice in judgment, in measures, weights, or scales.
You shall have just scales, just weights, and a just chous. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
And you shall keep all My law and all My ordinances, and do them; I am the Lord your God.

And upon those who remain of you I will bring cowardice into their heart in the land of their enemies; and the sound of a leaf borne along shall pursue them; and they shall flee as those fleeing from war, and fall when none pursues;
and brother shall disregard brother as in war, though no one runs after them. You shall not be able to withstand your enemies.
And you shall perish among the nations, and your enemies’ land shall devour you.
And those who remain of you shall be ruined because of your sins; they shall waste away in the land of their enemies.
And they shall confess their sins and their fathers’ sins, because they transgressed and disregarded Me, and because they walked crookedly before Me.
And I too walked with them in contrary anger, and I will destroy them in their enemies’ land. Then their uncircumcised heart will feel shame, and then they will accept their sins.
And I will remember the covenant of Jacob and the covenant of Isaac, and the covenant of Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.

And the land shall be abandoned by them. Then the land shall receive its Sabbaths when it is desolated because of them, and they shall accept their lawless deeds, because they disregarded My judgments and were indignant at My ordinances in their soul.
And yet even so, while they were in their enemies’ land, I did not disregard them or become indignant with them so as to consume them and dissolve My covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.
And I will remember for them the former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery, before the nations to be their God. I am the Lord.

You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.
If you walk in My ordinances, keep My commandments, and do them,
then I will give you rain in its season. The land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.

And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you in slaughter.
And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue tens of thousands; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
And I will look upon you, increase you, multiply you, and establish My covenant with you.
And you shall eat old stores and old stores of old stores, and clear out the old before the new.

And behold, an expert in the law stood up to test Him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole strength and with your whole mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”
He said to him, “You answered correctly. Do this and you will live.”
But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, inflicted blows, and went away, leaving him half dead.
By coincidence a certain priest was going down that road. He saw him and passed by on the opposite side.
Likewise a Levite also came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the opposite side.
But a certain Samaritan, traveling, came upon him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
He approached and bound his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
On the next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Care for him, and whatever more you spend I will repay you when I return.’
Which of these three seems to you to have become a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”
You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you,
that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.

And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

and one of you says to them, “Go in peace; be warmed and filled,” but you do not give them what the body needs, what good is it?
So also faith, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.

verses.text: And the priest shall take the basket out of your hands, and set it before the altar of the Lord your God.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.text:
Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You are entering the land of Canaan; this shall be your inheritance, the land of Canaan with its boundaries.
And your southwestern side shall run from the wilderness of Sin to the territory adjoining Edom. Your southwestern boundary shall begin from the part of the Salt Sea toward the east.
And the boundary shall turn around you from the southwest toward the Ascent of Akrabin and pass through Senna. Its endpoint shall be southwest of Kadesh-barnea; it shall extend to the settlement of Arad and pass through Azmon.
And the boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and its endpoint shall be the sea.
And for your sea boundary, the Great Sea shall mark the limit. This shall be your sea boundary.
And this shall be your boundary toward the north: from the Great Sea you shall measure out for yourselves beside the mountain, the mountain;
and from the mountain, the mountain, you shall measure out for them toward the entrance into Hamath; and its endpoint shall be the boundaries of Sarada.
And the boundary shall extend to Dephrona, and its endpoint shall be Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
And you shall measure out for yourselves the eastern boundary from Hazar-enan unto Shepham.
And the boundary shall descend from Shepham to Arbela, from the east toward the springs. The boundary shall descend to Bela, along the eastern ridge of the Sea of Chennara.
And the boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land and its surrounding boundaries.

verse_units.text: These are the names of the men who shall obtain the land as an inheritance for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
And you shall take one ruler from each tribe to allot the land unto you.
And these are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Simeon, Salamiel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon;
from the tribe of Dan, the ruler Bakchir son of Egli;
from the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, the ruler Hanniel son of Ouphi;
from the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, the ruler Kemuel son of Sabatha;
from the tribe of Zebulun, the ruler Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the ruler Paltiel son of Oza;
from the tribe of the sons of Asher, the ruler Achior son of Shelomi;
from the tribe of Naphtali, the ruler Pedahel son of Benammihud.

and throughout all the land of your possession, you shall provide redemption for the land.
But if your brother who is with you becomes poor, and sells some of his possession, and his nearest kinsman comes, he shall redeem that which his brother sold.
If someone has no kinsman but prospers by his hand and enough is found for his redemption,
then he shall calculate the years of his sale and repay the excess to the man to whom he sold himself; then he shall depart to his possession.
If his hand does not prosper enough to repay him, the sale shall remain with the one who acquired it until the sixth year of release. It shall go out at the release, and he shall depart to his possession.

Connection to Christ: Jesus’ account of the Samaritan challenges narrow limits on neighborly mercy; Hebrews commends hospitality.
Christian response today: Welcome and assist people without making nationality or social standing a condition of compassion.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 23:9 · Leviticus 19:33–34 Christ and the apostles: Luke 10:25–37 · Hebrews 13:2
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Exodus 23:9 · Leviticus 19:33–34

Israel must not oppress foreigners and is told to love the resident foreigner as oneself. The command appeals to remembered experience in Egypt. Jesus’ account of the merciful Samaritan challenges narrow definitions of neighbor, while Hebrews commends hospitality. Neither ethnic origin nor social vulnerability cancels a person’s claim to humane treatment.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Luke 10:25–37 · Hebrews 13:2

If a resident foreigner comes to you in your land, you shall not oppress him.
The resident foreigner who approaches you shall be as the native among you; and you shall love him as yourself, for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.
And behold, an expert in the law stood up to test Him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole strength and with your whole mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”
He said to him, “You answered correctly. Do this and you will live.”
But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, inflicted blows, and went away, leaving him half dead.
By coincidence a certain priest was going down that road. He saw him and passed by on the opposite side.
Likewise a Levite also came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the opposite side.
But a certain Samaritan, traveling, came upon him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
He approached and bound his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
On the next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Care for him, and whatever more you spend I will repay you when I return.’
Which of these three seems to you to have become a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”

verses.text: For six years you shall sow your land, and gather its produce;

but in the seventh you shall grant it release, and leave it; and the poor of your nation shall eat, and what they leave the wild beasts shall eat. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, the land which I give unto you shall rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord.
For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vine and gather its fruit.
But in the seventh year the land shall have a Sabbath, a rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord. You shall not sow your field or prune your vine.
And you shall not reap the things growing of themselves in your field or gather the grapes of your consecration. It shall be a year of rest for the land.
And the land’s Sabbath produce shall be food for you, your male slave, your female slave, your hired worker, and the lodger attached to you.
And all its produce shall also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
And He said to them, “See to it that you guard against every kind of greed, because a person’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
Then He told them a parable: “The land of a certain rich man yielded abundantly.
And he reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather my crops?’
And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will pull down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather all the grain and my goods there.
And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, be glad!”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool, this very night they demand your soul from you; and the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God.
For the one who entered His rest also rested from his own works, just as God did from His own.
Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.

And He said to them, “See to it that you guard against every kind of greed, because a person’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
Then He told them a parable: “The land of a certain rich man yielded abundantly.
And he reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather my crops?’
And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will pull down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather all the grain and my goods there.
And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, be glad!”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool, this very night they demand your soul from you; and the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God.
For the one who entered His rest also rested from his own works, just as God did from His own.
Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same pattern of disobedience.
For six years you shall sow your land, and gather its produce;

but in the seventh you shall grant it release, and leave it; and the poor of your nation shall eat, and what they leave the wild beasts shall eat. You shall do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, the land which I give unto you shall rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord.
For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vine and gather its fruit.
But in the seventh year the land shall have a Sabbath, a rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord. You shall not sow your field or prune your vine.
And you shall not reap the things growing of themselves in your field or gather the grapes of your consecration. It shall be a year of rest for the land.
And the land’s Sabbath produce shall be food for you, your male slave, your female slave, your hired worker, and the lodger attached to you.
And all its produce shall also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.

Connection to Christ: Jesus announces release through Isaiah in Luke 4; connecting this with Jubilee is a Christian interpretation, not a statement that he enacted every land provision.
Christian response today: Practice generosity and concern for freedom without promising automatic cancellation of every modern debt or property claim.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 25:8–17 · Leviticus 25:23–28 · Leviticus 25:39–43 Christ and the apostles: Luke 4:16–21
Text and setting: Land covenant
Torah: Leviticus 25:8–17 · Leviticus 25:23–28 · Leviticus 25:39–43

Jubilee regulates release and the return of ancestral land in Israel, grounding the provisions in God’s ownership. It is not a simple rule that all property everywhere changes hands every fifty years. Jesus announces good news and release through Isaiah’s language; that connection should be distinguished from claiming He enacted every detail of Leviticus 25 as civil policy.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Luke 4:16–21

verses.text:
You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed, the yield of your field, year by year.
And you shall eat it before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there. You shall bring the tithes of your grain, and of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and of your sheep, that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.
And if the way is too long for you, so that you cannot carry them, because the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there is far from you, when the Lord your God has blessed you,
then you shall sell them for silver, and take the silver in your hands, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose.
And you shall spend the silver for whatsoever your soul desires, for cattle, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever your soul desires; and you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice, you and your house,
and the Levite within your cities; for he has neither portion nor inheritance with you.
After three years you shall bring forth all the tithe of your produce; in that year you shall lay it up within your cities.
And the Levite, for he has neither portion nor inheritance with you, and the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow within your cities shall come, and eat, and be filled; that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works which you do.

The passage concerns agricultural produce, eating before the Lord and provision for Levites, foreigners, orphans and widows, including a third-year arrangement. It should not be reduced without explanation to a flat rule about every modern salary. Jesus prioritizes justice, mercy and faithfulness; Paul teaches willing, generous giving.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 23:23 · 2 Corinthians 9:6–8

Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Jesus addresses tithing together with justice and mercy, while Paul teaches willing generosity; applying a fixed percentage to every Christian is disputed.

Where interpretations differ: Whether a fixed tithe is obligatory for every Christian. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

verses.text:
And if there is among you one of your brethren in need, within any of your cities in the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not withhold the affection of your heart, neither shall you close your hand against your needy brother.
You shall freely open your hands unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs, according to his want.
Take heed unto yourself, lest there be a hidden, lawless thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye be evil toward your needy brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be great sin upon you.
You shall freely give unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs; and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him. For because of this the Lord your God shall bless you in all your works, and in all that you put your hand unto.
For the needy shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command you to do this thing, saying: You shall freely open your hands unto your poor brother and unto the needy in your land.

Connection to Christ: First John and Second Corinthians call for practical, willing generosity toward those in need.
Christian response today: Respond to need with concrete help rather than finding religious or financial excuses to close your hand.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 15:7–11 Christ and the apostles: 1 John 3:17–18 · 2 Corinthians 9:7
Text and setting: Moral teaching
Torah: Deuteronomy 15:7–11

Israel must not harden the heart or withhold assistance because the debt-release year is approaching. The passage exposes calculations that use the law as a reason to evade generosity. First John likewise asks how God’s love can remain in someone who sees a brother or sister’s need and refuses help.

Connection to Christ: Jesus speaks of God’s care for sparrows; the connection with this nest rule is thematic rather than a direct restatement.
Christian response today: Treat creatures with care and do not turn permission to take into a duty to take everything available.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 22:6–7 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 10:29–31
Text and setting: Care within land law
Torah: Deuteronomy 22:6–7

If a nest is encountered, the mother must be released when the young are taken. Permission to take the young is not an obligation to take every nest found. The instruction limits taking rather than encouraging indiscriminate collection. Jesus’ reference to the Father’s care for sparrows supplies a related reflection on God’s attention to creatures.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 10:29–31

Connection to Christ: Paul and James teach practical generosity, supporting the concern behind leaving produce for others.
Christian response today: Provide concrete help for vulnerable people in ways suited to your actual resources.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 24:19–22 Christ and the apostles: 2 Corinthians 9:6–9 · James 2:15–17
Text and setting: Economic law

A forgotten sheaf, remaining olives and leftover grapes are to be left for foreigners, orphans and widows. Israel’s memory of slavery grounds the instruction. The Christian connection is concrete generosity toward people in need; the law’s original agricultural form should remain visible while its concern informs other forms of provision.

Deuteronomy 26:1 — And it shall be, when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, and inherit it, and dwell therein,

Deuteronomy 26:2 — that you shall take of the firstfruits of the produce of your land which the Lord your God gives you, and put it in a basket, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.

Deuteronomy 26:3 — And you shall come unto the priest who shall be in those days, and say unto him: I declare this day unto the Lord my God, that I have come into the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers to give us.
Deuteronomy 26:4 — And the priest shall take the basket out of your hands, and set it before the altar of the Lord your God.

Deuteronomy 26:5 — And you shall answer and say before the Lord your God: My father forsook Syria, and went down into Egypt, and sojourned there, few in number; and there he became a great nation, and a multitude numerous and great.
Deuteronomy 26:6 — And the Egyptians afflicted us, and humbled us, and laid hard labours upon us.
Deuteronomy 26:7 — And we cried unto the Lord, the God of our fathers; and the Lord heard our voice, and saw our humiliation, and our toil, and our distress.
Deuteronomy 26:8 — And the Lord Himself brought us forth out of Egypt with great strength, and with a mighty hand, and with His uplifted arm, and with great visions, and with signs, and with wonders.
Deuteronomy 26:9 — And He brought us unto this place, and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

Deuteronomy 26:10 — And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the land which Thou hast given me, O Lord, a land flowing with milk and honey. And you shall set them before the Lord your God, and bow down there before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 26:11 — And you shall rejoice in all the good things which the Lord your God has given unto you and unto your house, you, and the Levite, and the sojourner among you.

Deuteronomy 26:12 — And when you have finished tithing all the tithe of the produce of your land in the third year, you shall give the second tithe unto the Levite, and unto the sojourner, and unto the orphan, and unto the widow; and they shall eat within your cities and be filled.

Deuteronomy 26:13 — And you shall say before the Lord your God: I have cleared the holy things out of my house, and have given them unto the Levite, and unto the sojourner, and unto the orphan, and unto the widow, according to all Thy commandments which Thou hast commanded me. I have not transgressed Thy commandment, neither have I forgotten it.

Deuteronomy 26:14 — And I have not eaten thereof in my mourning, neither have I offered thereof for an unclean use, nor given thereof unto the dead. I have hearkened unto the voice of the Lord my God; I have done according to all that Thou hast commanded me.

Deuteronomy 26:15 — Look down from Thy holy house, from heaven, and bless Thy people Israel, and the land which Thou hast given them, as Thou didst swear unto our fathers to give us a land flowing with milk and honey.
Deuteronomy 26:16 — This day the Lord your God has commanded you to do all these ordinances and judgments; and you shall keep and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Deuteronomy 26:17 — You have chosen God this day to be your God, and to walk in His ways, and to keep His ordinances and His judgments, and to hearken unto His voice.
Deuteronomy 26:18 — And the Lord has chosen you this day to be unto Him a people for His own possession, as He has spoken unto you, to keep all His commandments,
Deuteronomy 26:19 — and to be above all the nations, as He has made you renowned, and a boast, and glorious, that you should be a holy people unto the Lord your God, as He has spoken.

verses.text: And it shall be, when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, and inherit it, and dwell therein,

that you shall take of the firstfruits of the produce of your land which the Lord your God gives you, and put it in a basket, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.

And you shall come unto the priest who shall be in those days, and say unto him: I declare this day unto the Lord my God, that I have come into the land which the Lord sware unto our fathers to give us.
And the priest shall take the basket out of your hands, and set it before the altar of the Lord your God.

And you shall answer and say before the Lord your God: My father forsook Syria, and went down into Egypt, and sojourned there, few in number; and there he became a great nation, and a multitude numerous and great.
And the Egyptians afflicted us, and humbled us, and laid hard labours upon us.
And we cried unto the Lord, the God of our fathers; and the Lord heard our voice, and saw our humiliation, and our toil, and our distress.
And the Lord Himself brought us forth out of Egypt with great strength, and with a mighty hand, and with His uplifted arm, and with great visions, and with signs, and with wonders.
And He brought us unto this place, and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the produce of the land which Thou hast given me, O Lord, a land flowing with milk and honey. And you shall set them before the Lord your God, and bow down there before the Lord your God.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:

For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vine and gather its fruit.
But in the seventh year the land shall have a Sabbath, a rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord. You shall not sow your field or prune your vine.
And you shall not reap the things growing of themselves in your field or gather the grapes of your consecration. It shall be a year of rest for the land.
And the land’s Sabbath produce shall be food for you, your male slave, your female slave, your hired worker, and the lodger attached to you.
And all its produce shall also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
And you shall count unto yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and the seven weeks of years shall be unto you forty-nine years.

And you shall make proclamation with a trumpet sound throughout your land in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall make proclamation with a trumpet throughout your land.

And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim release throughout the land unto all who dwell therein; this shall be a year of release, a signal unto you; and each one shall depart unto his possession, and each of you shall depart unto his ancestral homeland.
This is a signal of release: the fiftieth year shall be a year for you. You shall not sow, reap what grows of itself, or gather its consecrated produce.
For it is a signal of release; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce from the fields.
In the year of release, at its signal, each shall return to his possession.
But if one sells property unto your neighbour, or you acquire it from your neighbour, let no man oppress his neighbour.
According to the number of years after the signal you shall acquire from your neighbour; according to the number of harvest years he shall sell to you.
As the years increase, you shall increase its purchase price; as the years decrease, you shall decrease its purchase price, for he is selling you a number of harvests.
Let no man oppress his neighbour, and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
And you shall do all My statutes and all My judgments, keep them, and do them; then you shall dwell confidently on the land.
And the land shall yield its produce, and you shall eat to fullness and dwell confidently upon it.
But if you say, “What shall we eat in this seventh year, if we neither sow nor gather our produce?”
then I will send My blessing to you in the sixth year, and it shall produce its harvest for the three years.
And you shall sow in the eighth year and eat old produce. Until the ninth year, until its produce comes in, you shall eat old stores from the old.
And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; for you are resident foreigners and lodgers before Me;
and throughout all the land of your possession, you shall provide redemption for the land.
But if your brother who is with you becomes poor, and sells some of his possession, and his nearest kinsman comes, he shall redeem that which his brother sold.
If someone has no kinsman but prospers by his hand and enough is found for his redemption,
then he shall calculate the years of his sale and repay the excess to the man to whom he sold himself; then he shall depart to his possession.

If his hand does not prosper enough to repay him, the sale shall remain with the one who acquired it until the sixth year of release. It shall go out at the release, and he shall depart to his possession.
But if anyone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, its redemption shall be possible until a year of days is fulfilled; that shall be its redemption period.

If it is not redeemed before its whole year is complete, the house in the city that has a wall shall be confirmed permanently to its buyer throughout his generations. It shall not go out at the release.
But houses in settlements that have no surrounding wall shall be reckoned with the field of the land. They shall always be redeemable and shall go out at the release.
And the cities of the Levites—the houses in their cities of possession—shall always be redeemable by the Levites.

And whosoever redeems from the Levites, the sale of their houses in the city of their possession shall go out at the release; for the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the sons of Israel.
And the fields set apart for their cities shall not be sold, for this is their everlasting possession.
If your brother becomes poor and grows weak in his hands beside you, you shall support him as a resident foreigner and a lodger, and your brother shall live with you.
You shall take no interest or increase from him, and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord; and your brother shall live with you.
You shall not give him your silver at interest or give your food for an increase.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother is brought low beside you and is sold to you, he shall not serve you with the service of a household slave.
He shall be with you as a hired worker or a lodger; he shall work beside you until the year of release.
And he shall go out at the release, and his children with him. He shall depart to his kin and return to his ancestral possession.
For these are My household slaves, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; one shall not be sold with the sale of a household slave.
You shall not wear him down with toil, but you shall fear the Lord your God.
And your male slave and your female slave, as many as you have from the nations which are round about you: from them you may acquire a male slave and a female slave.
And you may also acquire from the sons of the lodgers among you and from their relatives who come to be in your land; they shall become your possession.
And you shall distribute them to your children after you, and they shall be held by you permanently. But among your brethren, the sons of Israel, no one shall wear down his brother with toils.

after he is sold to him, he shall have a right of redemption. One of his brethren may redeem him,

He shall be with him as a hired worker year by year; you shall not wear him down with toil before you.
If he is not redeemed by these means, he shall go out in the year of release, he and his children with him.
For the sons of Israel are household slaves to Me; these are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

verses.text:
For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread,
and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.”
Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.”
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

verses.text:
Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law.
For “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
Love does no evil to the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.

verses.text: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.
The one who says that he is in the light and hates his brother is still in the darkness.
The one who loves his brother abides in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.
But the one who hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and he does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.

verses.text: Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse.

verse_units.text: Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse.

verses.text:
Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is honorable before all people.
If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.
Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but make room for wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.

verses.text:
But why do you judge your brother? Or you also, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat,
for it is written, “As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bend to Me, and every tongue will confess to God.”
So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
Therefore let us no longer judge one another; but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or a snare for a brother.

doing nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility considering one another above yourselves,

For if your brother is grieved because of food, you no longer walk according to love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.

verses.text:
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?

who have borne witness to your love before the Church. You will do well to send them onward in a manner worthy of God,

verses.text:

For we brought nothing into the world, because neither can we carry anything out.
But having food and coverings, with these we will be content.
But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge people into ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all evils, and some, reaching for it, wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.

verses.text:
Come now, you rich people: weep and howl over the miseries coming upon you.
Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a testimony against you and will devour your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.
Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.
You lived luxuriously on the earth and indulged yourselves; you fattened your hearts on a day of slaughter.

verses.text:
Now concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anything to be written to you.
For you yourselves know exactly that the day of the Lord comes in this way, like a thief in the night.
When they say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction comes upon them, as labor pain upon a pregnant woman, and they will certainly not escape.
But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief.
For you are all sons of light and sons of day. We are not of night or darkness.
So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us keep watch and be sober.

But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a rushing roar, and the elements will be dissolved by burning heat, and the earth and the works in it will not be found.
Since all these things are being dissolved in this way, what sort of people ought you to be in holy acts of conduct and godliness,
waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved by fire and the elements melt in burning heat?

verses.text:
Be patient, therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Look, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until he receives the early and late rain.
You too be patient; strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Look, the Judge stands before the doors.

verses.text:
He answered, “Have you not read that the Creator from the beginning made them male and female,
and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has yoked together, let no human being separate.”

He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery.”

He said to them, “You set aside God’s commandment very well indeed, so that you may establish your tradition!
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Let whoever speaks evil of father or mother surely die.’
But you say, ‘If a person says to his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban”—that is, a gift—’
you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother,
making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. You do many similar things.”
Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
“Honor your father and mother”—which is the first commandment with a promise—
“so that it may be well with you and you may live long upon the earth.”

And you shall teach them to your sons, and speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk in the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.

Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.
And the priest shall take the sacrifice of jealousy from the woman’s hand, place the sacrifice before the Lord, and bring it near the altar.
And the priest shall take a handful from the sacrifice as its memorial portion and offer it up on the altar. Afterward he shall make the woman drink the water.

And if a man takes a wife and dwells with her as husband, and she finds no favour in his sight, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house,
and she departs and becomes another man’s wife,
and the latter husband hates her, and writes her a certificate of divorce, and gives it into her hands, and sends her forth out of his house, or if the latter husband who took her to be his wife dies,
her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after she has been defiled; for it is an abomination before the Lord your God. And you shall not defile the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.
