Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body.
Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? And you are not your own,
for you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.
For perhaps he was separated from you for a little while for this reason: that you might have him back forever,
no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
So if you regard me as a partner, welcome him as you would me.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

And if anyone lies with a woman with an emission of semen, and she is a household slave reserved for a man but has not been ransomed or given freedom, there shall be an inquiry concerning them. They shall not die, because she has not been freed.
And he shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord beside the door of the Tent of Testimony, a ram for a guilt offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for the sin he has committed, and the sin he has committed shall be forgiven him.
Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body.
Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? And you are not your own,
for you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.
For perhaps he was separated from you for a little while for this reason: that you might have him back forever,
no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
So if you regard me as a partner, welcome him as you would me.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

And if anyone lies with a woman with an emission of semen, and she is a household slave reserved for a man but has not been ransomed or given freedom, there shall be an inquiry concerning them. They shall not die, because she has not been freed.
And he shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord beside the door of the Tent of Testimony, a ram for a guilt offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for the sin he has committed, and the sin he has committed shall be forgiven him.

Related indexed requirements: C1166. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus expressly distinguishes the Mosaic divorce concession from the creation ideal; Paul addresses further circumstances.
Christian response today: Take fidelity and Jesus’ teaching seriously, and seek careful pastoral guidance where Christian applications differ.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 24:1–4 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 19:3–9 · Mark 10:2–12 · 1 Corinthians 7:10–16
Text and setting: Family law
Torah: Deuteronomy 24:1–4

Deuteronomy regulates a case involving divorce, remarriage and return to the first husband; it is not a command to divorce. Jesus explicitly distinguishes Mosaic concession from the creation ideal. Paul addresses further pastoral circumstances. Christian traditions differ over some applications, so the study should present these texts together rather than manufacture one unrestricted rule.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Matthew 19:3–9 · Mark 10:2–12 · 1 Corinthians 7:10–16
Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Jesus expressly distinguishes the Mosaic divorce concession from the creation ideal; Paul addresses further circumstances.

Where interpretations differ: Divorce, remarriage and the application of the stated New Testament circumstances. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

He answered, “Have you not read that the Creator from the beginning made them male and female,
and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has yoked together, let no human being separate.”
They said to Him, “Why then did Moses command giving a certificate of divorce and divorcing her?”
He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery.”
Pharisees came to Him and asked whether it was lawful for a man to divorce his wife, testing Him.
He answered them, “What did Moses command you?”
They said, “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and dismiss her.”
Jesus said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote you this commandment.
But from the beginning of creation, ‘He made them male and female.’
‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,
and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore, what God has yoked together, let no human separate.”
In the house, the disciples asked Him about this again.
He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
And if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”
To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband—
but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.
To the rest I say—I, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she agrees to live with him, let him not dismiss her.
And if any woman has an unbelieving husband and he agrees to live with her, let her not dismiss her husband.

But if the unbelieving spouse separates, let that one separate. The brother or sister is not enslaved in such cases; God has called you in peace.
For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

verses.text:
And if brethren dwell together, and one of them dies, and has no seed, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside unto a man who is not near of kin. Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her unto himself for a wife, and dwell with her as husband.
And it shall be, that the child whom she bears shall be established in the name of the dead, and his name shall not be blotted out of Israel.
And if the man will not take his brother’s wife, the woman shall go up unto the gate, unto the elders, and say: My husband’s brother will not raise up his brother’s name in Israel; my husband’s brother has refused.
And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak unto him; and if he stands and says: I will not take her,

Related indexed requirements: C1184, C1185, C1186, C1187, C1188, C1189, C1190, C1191, C1192. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus discusses levirate marriage in a resurrection dispute, while Paul speaks of a widow’s freedom to marry in the Lord.
Christian response today: Respect widows and do not impose this ancient household arrangement as a universal marriage obligation.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 25:5–10 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 22:23–33 · 1 Corinthians 7:39
Text and setting: Family and inheritance law
Torah: Deuteronomy 25:5–10

The law concerns brothers dwelling together when one dies without descendants (KJV: “child”; some translations: “son”), providing marriage and a named refusal procedure to preserve the deceased brother’s line. It is not a universal command that every man must marry a deceased brother’s widow. Jesus discusses the institution in a resurrection dispute; Paul gives Christian widows freedom to marry in the Lord.

And if you come upon a bird’s nest before you in the way, in any tree or upon the ground, with young birds or eggs, and the mother sitting upon the young or upon the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young.
You shall surely let the mother go, but the young you may take unto yourself, that it may be well with you, and that your days may be long.
And when you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, that you do not cause bloodshed in your house, if anyone falls from it.
You shall not sow your vineyard with a different crop, lest the produce and the seed which you sow, together with the produce of your vineyard, become consecrated.
You shall not plough with a calf and a donkey together.
You shall not wear a mingled fabric, wool and linen together.
You shall make twisted tassels upon the four edges of your outer garments wherewith you cover yourself.
And if a man takes a wife, and dwells with her as husband, and hates her,
and brings charges against her as a pretext, and gives her an evil name, and says: I took this woman, and when I came unto her, I did not find the tokens of her virginity,
then the father of the young woman and her mother shall take and bring forth the tokens of her virginity unto the elders at the gate.
And the father of the young woman shall say unto the elders: I gave this my daughter unto this man for a wife, and he has hated her;

and behold, he brings charges against her as a pretext, saying: I did not find the tokens of your daughter’s virginity. Yet these are the tokens of my daughter’s virginity. And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.
And the elders of that city shall take that man and chasten him.

And they shall fine him a hundred shekels, and give them unto the father of the young woman, because he has brought an evil name upon a virgin of Israel; and she shall be his wife, and he may not put her away all his days.
But if this matter is true, and the tokens of the young woman’s virginity are not found,

then they shall bring forth the young woman unto the doors of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die; for she has wrought folly among the sons of Israel, bringing harlotry into her father’s house. And you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.
And if a man is found lying with a woman married unto a husband, you shall put both of them to death, the man who lay with the woman, and the woman; and you shall remove the evil one from Israel.
And if a young woman, a virgin, is betrothed unto a man, and a man finds her in the city and lies with her,

you shall bring both of them forth unto the gate of their city, and they shall be stoned with stones and shall die: the young woman, because she did not cry out in the city, and the man, because he violated his neighbour’s wife. And you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.
But if a man finds the betrothed young woman in the field, and forces her and lies with her, you shall put to death only the man who lay with her.
And unto the young woman you shall do nothing; there is in her no sin deserving death. For as when a man rises against his neighbour and slays him, so is this matter.
For he found her in the field; the betrothed young woman cried out, and there was none to help her.
And if a man finds a young woman, a virgin who is not betrothed, and forces her and lies with her, and he is found out,
the man who lay with her shall give unto the father of the young woman fifty silver didrachmas, and she shall be his wife, because he violated her; he may not put her away all his days.

Leviticus 18:1 — And the Lord said unto Moses, saying,
Leviticus 18:2 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: I am the Lord your God.

Leviticus 18:3 — You shall not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you dwelt; and you shall not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; neither shall you walk in their statutes.
Leviticus 18:4 — You shall do My judgments, and keep My ordinances, to walk in them; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 18:5 — And you shall keep all My ordinances and all My judgments, and do them; the man who does them shall live by them; I am the Lord your God.
Leviticus 18:6 — No person shall approach any relative of his flesh to uncover nakedness. I am the Lord.
Leviticus 18:7 — You shall not uncover your father’s nakedness or your mother’s nakedness. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
Leviticus 18:8 — You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; it is your father’s nakedness.
Leviticus 18:9 — The nakedness of your sister, from your father or from your mother, born at home or born outside: you shall not uncover her nakedness.
Leviticus 18:10 — The nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, you shall not uncover their nakedness, for it is your nakedness.
Leviticus 18:11 — You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter. She is your sister by the same father; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
Leviticus 18:12 — You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.
Leviticus 18:13 — You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister; she is your mother’s close relative.
Leviticus 18:14 — You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother, and you shall not go in to his wife. She is your relative.
Leviticus 18:15 — You shall not uncover your daughter-in-law’s nakedness. She is your son’s wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
Leviticus 18:16 — You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife; it is your brother’s nakedness.

Leviticus 18:17 — You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover their nakedness; they are your relatives. It is an act of impiety.
Leviticus 18:18 — You shall not take a woman in addition to her sister as a rival, to uncover her nakedness alongside her while she is alive.
Leviticus 18:19 — And you shall not approach a woman in separation for her uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
Leviticus 18:20 — And you shall not lie with your neighbour’s wife to emit semen and become defiled through her.
Leviticus 18:21 — And you shall not give any of your seed to serve a ruler, neither shall you profane the holy name; I am the Lord.
Leviticus 18:22 — And you shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination.

Leviticus 18:23 — And you shall not lie with any four-footed animal for insemination and become defiled through it. A woman shall not stand before any four-footed animal to be mounted; it is detestable.
Leviticus 18:24 — Do not defile yourselves in any of these things; for in all these things the nations whom I drive out before your face were defiled,
Leviticus 18:25 — and the land became defiled, and I repaid them for wrongdoing because of it, and the land became indignant with those settled upon it.
Leviticus 18:26 — And you shall keep all My statutes and all My commands, and do none of these abominations, neither the native nor the resident foreigner who has joined himself among you—
Leviticus 18:27 — for the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land became defiled—
Leviticus 18:28 — so that the land is not indignant with you when you defile it, as it was indignant with the nations before you.
Leviticus 18:29 — For whosoever does any of all these abominations, the souls that do them shall be destroyed from among their people.
Leviticus 18:30 — And you shall keep My ordinances, that you do none of all the abominable practices which were before you; and you shall not be defiled in them, for I am the Lord your God.

verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: I am the Lord your God.

You shall not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you dwelt; and you shall not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; neither shall you walk in their statutes.
You shall do My judgments, and keep My ordinances, to walk in them; I am the Lord your God.
And you shall keep all My ordinances and all My judgments, and do them; the man who does them shall live by them; I am the Lord your God.
No person shall approach any relative of his flesh to uncover nakedness. I am the Lord.
You shall not uncover your father’s nakedness or your mother’s nakedness. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; it is your father’s nakedness.
The nakedness of your sister, from your father or from your mother, born at home or born outside: you shall not uncover her nakedness.
The nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, you shall not uncover their nakedness, for it is your nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter. She is your sister by the same father; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister; she is your mother’s close relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother, and you shall not go in to his wife. She is your relative.
You shall not uncover your daughter-in-law’s nakedness. She is your son’s wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife; it is your brother’s nakedness.

You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover their nakedness; they are your relatives. It is an act of impiety.
You shall not take a woman in addition to her sister as a rival, to uncover her nakedness alongside her while she is alive.
And you shall not approach a woman in separation for her uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
And you shall not lie with your neighbour’s wife to emit semen and become defiled through her.
And you shall not give any of your seed to serve a ruler, neither shall you profane the holy name; I am the Lord.
And you shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination.
And you shall not lie with any four-footed animal for insemination and become defiled through it. A woman shall not stand before any four-footed animal to be mounted; it is detestable.
Do not defile yourselves in any of these things; for in all these things the nations whom I drive out before your face were defiled,
and the land became defiled, and I repaid them for wrongdoing because of it, and the land became indignant with those settled upon it.
And you shall keep all My statutes and all My commands, and do none of these abominations, neither the native nor the resident foreigner who has joined himself among you—
for the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land became defiled—
so that the land is not indignant with you when you defile it, as it was indignant with the nations before you.
For whosoever does any of all these abominations, the souls that do them shall be destroyed from among their people.
And you shall keep My ordinances, that you do none of all the abominable practices which were before you; and you shall not be defiled in them, for I am the Lord your God.

Numbers 5:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Numbers 5:2 — Command the sons of Israel to send out of the camp everyone with leprosy, everyone with a seminal discharge, and everyone unclean through a dead person.
Numbers 5:3 — From male unto female, send them outside the camp, and they shall in no wise defile their camps, wherein I dwell among them.
Numbers 5:4 — And the sons of Israel did so and sent them outside the camp. As the Lord spoke unto Moses, so the sons of Israel did.
Numbers 5:5 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Numbers 5:6 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a man or woman commits any of the sins of men, and acts with utter disregard, and that soul incurs guilt,
Numbers 5:7 — that person shall confess the sin committed, and repay the principal of the offence, and add a fifth part thereto, and give it unto the one who was wronged.

Numbers 5:8 — But if the man has no next of kin to receive repayment for the offence, the repayment made unto the Lord shall be the priest’s, besides the ram of atonement, wherewith he shall make atonement for him.
Numbers 5:9 — And every first portion from all the things consecrated among the sons of Israel that they bring unto the Lord, unto the priest, shall belong to him.
Numbers 5:10 — And each man’s consecrated things shall be his; whatsoever a man gives unto the priest shall be his.
Numbers 5:11 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Numbers 5:12 — Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If any man’s wife transgresses and utterly disregards him,

Numbers 5:13 — and anyone lies with her with an emission of semen, and it escapes the eyes of her husband, and she conceals it, though she is defiled, and there is no witness concerning her, and she is not caught,

Numbers 5:14 — and a spirit of jealousy comes upon him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she is defiled; or a spirit of jealousy comes upon him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she is not defiled:

Numbers 5:15 — then the man shall bring his wife unto the priest, and shall present the gift on her behalf, a tenth of an oiphi of barley flour. He shall pour no oil upon it, neither shall he put frankincense upon it; for it is a sacrifice of jealousy, a memorial sacrifice bringing sin to remembrance.
Numbers 5:16 — And the priest shall bring her near and stand her before the Lord.
Numbers 5:17 — And the priest shall take clean, living water in an earthenware vessel. He shall take some earth from the floor of the Tent of Testimony and put it into the water.

Numbers 5:18 — And the priest shall stand the woman before the Lord, uncover her head, and put the memorial sacrifice—the sacrifice of jealousy—on her hands. In the priest’s hand shall be this curse-bringing water of testing.

Numbers 5:19 — And the priest shall put her under oath, and say unto the woman: If no one has lain with you, and you have not transgressed into defilement while under your own husband, be unharmed by this curse-bringing water of testing.
Numbers 5:20 — But if you have transgressed while under a husband, or have become defiled, and someone other than your husband has lain with you:

Numbers 5:21 — then the priest shall put the woman under the oaths of this curse, and the priest shall say unto the woman: The Lord make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the Lord makes your thigh collapse and your belly swell;
Numbers 5:22 — and this curse-bringing water shall enter your belly, to make your belly swell and your thigh collapse. And the woman shall say: So be it, so be it.
Numbers 5:23 — And the priest shall write these curses in a scroll and wipe them off into the curse-bringing water of testing.
Numbers 5:24 — And he shall make the woman drink the curse-bringing water of testing, and the curse-bringing water of testing shall enter her.
Numbers 5:25 — And the priest shall take the sacrifice of jealousy from the woman’s hand, place the sacrifice before the Lord, and bring it near the altar.
Numbers 5:26 — And the priest shall take a handful from the sacrifice as its memorial portion and offer it up on the altar. Afterward he shall make the woman drink the water.

Numbers 5:27 — And it shall be, if she is defiled and has concealed it from her husband, that the curse-bringing water of testing shall enter her, and her belly shall swell, and her thigh shall collapse, and the woman shall become a curse among her people.
Numbers 5:28 — But if the woman is not defiled, and is clean, she shall be unharmed, and shall bring forth seed.
Numbers 5:29 — This is the law of jealousy, when a wife transgresses while under a husband and becomes defiled,
Numbers 5:30 — or when a spirit of jealousy comes upon a man and he is jealous of his wife. He shall set his wife before the Lord, and the priest shall perform all this law for her.
Numbers 5:31 — And the man shall be free from sin, and that woman shall bear her sin.

verses.text: And if he takes another wife to himself, he shall not deprive her of her necessities, her clothing, or her conjugal companionship.
Let the husband fulfill his obligation to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.
The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does; likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does.

verses.text:
By faith Abel offered God a greater sacrifice than Cain, through which he received testimony that he was righteous, God testifying concerning his gifts; and through it, though he died, he still speaks.
By faith Enoch was taken away so as not to see death, and he was not found, because God took him away. For before his taking away he had received testimony that he had pleased God.
And without faith it is impossible to please Him, for the one approaching God must believe that He is and that He becomes a rewarder of those who seek Him.
By faith Noah, instructed concerning things not yet seen, acted with reverent fear and prepared an ark for the salvation of his household. Through this he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness according to faith.

For just as the body without spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who disobeyed, having received the spies in peace.

Joshua son of Nun sent two young men from Shittim to spy, saying, “Go up and look at the land and Jericho.” The two young men went into Jericho, entered the house of a harlot named Rahab, and lodged there.
The king of Jericho was informed, “Men from the sons of Israel have entered here to spy out the land.”
The king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying, “Bring out the men who entered your house by night, for they have come to spy out the land.”
The woman took the men and hid them, and said to the messengers, “The men came to me.
As the gate was closing in the darkness, the men went out. I do not know where they have gone. Pursue them, to see whether you can overtake them.”
But she had brought them up to the roof and hidden them among the flax stalks she had piled on the roof.
And likewise was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works, when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way?
For just as the body without spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.

Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Thesbon in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain these years except through the utterance of my word.”
Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of the rain’s footsteps.”
Ahab went up to eat and drink. Elijah went up onto Carmel, bent down to the ground, and put his face between his knees.

He said to his young attendant, “Go up and look toward the sea.” The young attendant looked and said, “There is nothing.” Elijah said, “Go back seven times.” The young attendant went back seven times.
At the seventh time, behold, a little cloud like a man’s footprint was bringing up water. He said, “Go up, tell Ahab, ‘Harness your chariot and go down, so the rain does not overtake you.’”
Meanwhile the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a heavy rain. Ahab wept and went to Jezreel.

And just as we bore the image of the one made of dust, we will also bear the image of the heavenly One.

verses.text:
Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, “And to seeds,” as concerning many, but as concerning one, “And to your seed,” who is Christ.
What I mean is this: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise.
For if the inheritance is from law, it is no longer from promise. But God has graciously given it to Abraham through promise.
Why, then, the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made, and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.

Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, “And to seeds,” as concerning many, but as concerning one, “And to your seed,” who is Christ.
What I mean is this: the law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God, so as to nullify the promise.
For if the inheritance is from law, it is no longer from promise. But God has graciously given it to Abraham through promise.
Why, then, the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made, and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
So the law became our guardian until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.

verses.text:
For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become accountable for all of it.
For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and so act as those who are going to be judged through a law of freedom.

verses.text:
For, finding fault with them, He says, “Look, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will conclude a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,
not according to the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.
For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws into their mind, I will also inscribe them upon their hearts, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.
And they shall certainly not teach, each his fellow citizen and each his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because all will know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.
For I will be merciful toward their wrongdoings, and I will certainly remember their sins no more.”

who also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant, not of letter but of Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

verses.text:
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
and all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were strewn over the wilderness.
Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired.
Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, just as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose to play.”
Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
Nor let us put Christ to the test, as some of them tested Him and were being destroyed by the serpents.
Nor grumble, just as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer.
These things happened to them as examples, and were written to admonish us, upon whom the ends of the ages have arrived.

He rose early the next day, offered whole burnt offerings, and brought a sacrifice of deliverance. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.
And Israel lodged at Shittim, and the people profaned themselves by engaging in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab.
And they invited them to the sacrifices of their idols. The people ate from their sacrifices and bowed down to their idols.
And Israel was initiated into the worship of Baal of Peor, and the Lord became angry with Israel.
And the Lord said unto Moses: Take all the leaders of the people and make a public example of them before the Lord in the sunlight, and the Lord's fierce anger will turn away from Israel.
And Moses said to Israel's tribes: Each of you shall kill his own kinsman who was initiated into the worship of Baal of Peor.

And an Israelite man came and brought his brother to the Midianite woman before Moses and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, while they were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, rose from among the congregation, and took a lance in his hand.
He went after the Israelite man into the chamber and stabbed both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her womb. The plague against the sons of Israel stopped.
And those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
And the people spoke against God and against Moses: Why have you brought us out of Egypt to kill us in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and our soul is disgusted with this empty bread.
And the Lord sent deadly serpents among the people. They bit the people, and many of the sons of Israel died.
And the next day the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the Lord’s people!
And when the congregation banded together against Moses and Aaron, they rushed toward the Tent of Testimony. The cloud covered it, and the Lord’s glory appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came into the area before the Tent of Testimony.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Withdraw from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them all at once. They fell on their faces.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Take the fire pan, put fire from the altar on it, and place incense on it. Carry it quickly into the camp and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from before the Lord; it has begun to strike the people.
And Aaron took it just as Moses had told him and ran into the congregation. The outbreak had already begun among the people. He placed the incense and made atonement for the people,
and stood between the dead and the living, and the outbreak subsided.
And those who died in the outbreak numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, apart from those who died because of Korah.

And Aaron took it just as Moses had told him and ran into the congregation. The outbreak had already begun among the people. He placed the incense and made atonement for the people,
and stood between the dead and the living, and the outbreak subsided.
And those who died in the outbreak numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, apart from those who died because of Korah.
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
and all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were strewn over the wilderness.
Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired.
Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, just as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose to play.”
Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
Nor let us put Christ to the test, as some of them tested Him and were being destroyed by the serpents.
Nor grumble, just as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer.
These things happened to them as examples, and were written to admonish us, upon whom the ends of the ages have arrived.

Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear His voice,
do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested Me with a trial and saw My works
for forty years. Therefore I was indignant with this generation and said, ‘They always wander in their heart, and they did not know My ways,’
as I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall certainly not enter My rest.’”
Watch out, brothers, so that none of you has an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
But encourage one another each day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin.

verses.text:
Pursue peace with everyone, and sanctification, without which no one will see the Lord.
Watch lest anyone fall short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness grow up and cause trouble, and through it many be defiled,
lest anyone be sexually immoral or profane like Esau, who sold his own birthright for a single meal.
For you know that even afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, although he sought it with tears.

Woe to them! For they have gone in the way of Cain, have poured themselves into Balaam’s error for pay, and have perished in Korah’s rebellion.
Leaving the straight way, they wandered off, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing,
but received a rebuke for his own transgression: a speechless beast of burden spoke with a human voice and restrained the prophet’s madness.
And God opened the donkey's mouth, and she says to Balaam: What have I done unto you that you have struck me this third time?
And Balaam said to the donkey: Because you have mocked me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would have stabbed you already.
And the donkey says to Balaam: Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden from your youth until this day? Have I acted like this toward you out of deliberate disregard? He said: No.
God uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he sees the Lord's angel opposing him in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He bent down and prostrated himself on his face.
And God's angel said to him: Why have you struck your donkey this third time? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is not fitting before me.
And the donkey saw me and turned away from me this third time. If she had not turned away, I would now have killed you and preserved her.
And Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, spoke, with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, son of Reuben.
And they rose up before Moses, with two hundred fifty men of the sons of Israel, leaders of the congregation, members summoned to the council, men of renown.
They banded together against Moses and Aaron and said: Enough for you! The whole congregation, all of them, is holy, and the Lord is among them. Why do you rise up against the Lord’s congregation?
As he finished speaking all these words, the ground beneath them split apart.
And the earth opened and swallowed them, their households, all the people who were with Korah, and their livestock.
And they and all that belonged to them went down alive to Hades; the earth covered them, and they perished from the midst of the congregation.
Woe to them! For they have gone in the way of Cain, have poured themselves into Balaam’s error for pay, and have perished in Korah’s rebellion.

verses.text:
Therefore, having such hope, we use great boldness,
and are not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel might not gaze at the end of what was being brought to an end.
But their minds were hardened. For until this very day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant, not being unveiled, because in Christ it is brought to an end.
But to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart.
But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is removed.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
And we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit.

verses.text:
Our fathers had the Tent of Testimony in the wilderness, as the One who spoke to Moses directed him to make it according to the pattern he had seen.
Our fathers in their turn received it and brought it in with Joshua when they took possession of the nations’ land, whose people God drove out before our fathers. It remained until the days of David,
who found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling for the house of Jacob.
But Solomon built Him a house.
Yet the Most High does not dwell in things made by hands, as the prophet says:
‘Heaven is My throne, and the earth the footstool of My feet. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or what place is there for My rest?
Did not My hand make all these things?’

verses.text:
Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump of dough?
Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump of dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed.
So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him.
Abraham also apportioned to him a tenth of everything. His name is interpreted first as king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace.

verses.text:
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the one to come.

The eunuch said to Philip, “I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this—about himself or about someone else?”
Philip opened his mouth and, beginning from this Scripture, proclaimed to him the good news of Jesus.

verses.text: He bears our sins, and suffers pain for us; yet we reckoned him to be in toil and affliction and distress.
But he was wounded for our iniquities, and has been weakened for our sins. The chastisement of our peace was upon him; by his bruise we were healed.
We all, like sheep, have gone astray; each person has strayed in his own way. And the Lord delivered him over to our sins.
And because he has been afflicted, he does not open his mouth. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and as a lamb is silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.
He Himself bore our sins in His body upon the tree, so that, having died to sins, we might live to righteousness. By His wound you were healed.
For you were wandering like sheep, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

verses.text:
For David says concerning Him, ‘I kept the Lord before me always, for He is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken.
Therefore my heart rejoiced and my tongue exulted; moreover, my flesh will dwell in hope,
because Thou wilt not abandon my soul to Hades, nor allow Thy Holy One to see decay.
Thou hast made known to me the paths of life; Thou wilt fill me with gladness in Thy presence.’
Men, brothers, I may speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day.
Since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one from the fruit of his loins upon his throne,
he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ: He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay.
God raised this Jesus, and all of us are witnesses of it.

verses.text:
and you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline, nor faint when reproved by Him.
For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and scourges every son He receives.”
Endure for discipline. God deals with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
But if you are without discipline, in which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
Furthermore, we had our fathers in the flesh to discipline us, and we respected them. But shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live?
For they disciplined us for a few days according to what seemed right to them, but He for our benefit, so that we may share in His holiness.
Now every discipline seems for the present to be a matter of sorrow, not joy, but afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained through it.

For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

Fulfilled: This requirement belongs to the sacrificial order whose repeated offerings Hebrews contrasts with Christ’s once-for-all offering. The classification concerns that order as a whole; it does not invent a separate symbolic fulfillment for each ingredient or action.
Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 10:1–18. Explicit teaching about the sacrificial system.
Source passages: Leviticus 6:1–23

verses.text: Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of whole burning. The whole burnt offering shall remain upon its burning place upon the altar all night until morning; and the fire of the altar shall burn upon it, and shall not be quenched.

And the fire upon the altar shall burn from it, and shall not be quenched; and the priest shall burn wood upon it in the morning, and pile the whole burnt offering upon it, and place upon it the fat of the offering of deliverance.
And a fire shall burn continually upon the altar; it shall not be quenched.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.text:
and you make whole burnt offerings unto the Lord, a whole offering or a sacrifice, to honour a vow, or willingly, or at your feasts, to make a sweet savour unto the Lord, whether from the cattle or from the sheep,
And the one presenting a gift unto the Lord shall bring a sacrifice of one tenth of an oiphi of fine flour mixed with one quarter of a hin of oil.
And you shall prepare wine for a drink offering, a fourth of a hin, with the whole burning or with the sacrifice; you shall prepare this much for each lamb, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
And for a ram, when you prepare it for a whole burnt offering or for a sacrifice, you shall prepare a sacrifice of two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, a third of a hin.
And you shall present wine for a drink offering, a third of a hin, for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
But if you prepare an animal from the cattle for a whole burnt offering or for a sacrifice to honour a vow, or for a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord,
he shall present with the calf a sacrifice of three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, half a hin,
and half a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
Thus you shall do for each calf, or each ram, or each lamb from the sheep or from the goats.
According to the number that you prepare, thus you shall do for each one according to their number.

And he shall present alive before the Lord the male young goat on which the lot of the one sent away fell, to make atonement over it, so as to send it away for removal. He shall release it into the wilderness.
And he shall finish making atonement for the holy place, the Tent of Testimony, and the altar, and perform cleansing for the priests. He shall present the living male young goat.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Consecrate to Me every firstborn, the first offspring opening every womb among the sons of Israel, both human and animal. It is Mine.”
And when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, as He swore to your fathers, and gives it to you,

you shall set apart to the Lord all that opens the womb, the males; every male that opens the womb among the herds or among your livestock, whatever shall be born to you, you shall consecrate to the Lord.
Every donkey that opens the womb you shall exchange for a sheep; and if you do not exchange it, you shall redeem it. Every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem.
And if your son asks you later, saying, ‘What is this?’ you shall say to him, ‘With a mighty hand the Lord brought us out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, He killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human firstborn and firstborn of the livestock. Therefore I sacrifice to the Lord every male that opens the womb, and every firstborn of my sons I will redeem.’
And it shall be a sign upon your hand, and a fixed reminder before your eyes; for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out of Egypt.”

The verse specifically prohibits bringing a prostitute’s earnings or the price of a dog into the Lord’s house for a vow; the meaning of “dog” in this setting is disputed. A broad label such as “dirty money” needs that explanation. A religious donation does not erase an obligation to stop wrongdoing and make restitution.

Leviticus 6:1 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Leviticus 6:2 — Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of whole burning. The whole burnt offering shall remain upon its burning place upon the altar all night until morning; and the fire of the altar shall burn upon it, and shall not be quenched.

Leviticus 6:3 — And the priest shall put on a linen tunic, and he shall put linen undergarments about his body; and he shall remove from the altar the burnt remains of the whole burning which the fire has consumed, and place them beside the altar.
Leviticus 6:4 — And he shall take off his robe, and put on another robe, and carry the burnt remains outside the camp unto a clean place.

Leviticus 6:5 — And the fire upon the altar shall burn from it, and shall not be quenched; and the priest shall burn wood upon it in the morning, and pile the whole burnt offering upon it, and place upon it the fat of the offering of deliverance.
Leviticus 6:6 — And a fire shall burn continually upon the altar; it shall not be quenched.
Leviticus 6:7 — This is the law of the sacrifice which the sons of Aaron shall bring before the Lord, opposite the altar.

Leviticus 6:8 — And he shall take a handful from the fine flour of the sacrifice, with its oil and the frankincense upon the sacrifice, and offer it up upon the altar as an offering: a sweet savour, its memorial portion unto the Lord.
Leviticus 6:9 — But Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains of it. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Testimony.
Leviticus 6:10 — It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it unto them as a portion from the offerings of the Lord; it is most holy, as the offering for sin and the guilt offering.
Leviticus 6:11 — Every male among the priests shall eat it; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations, from the offerings of the Lord. Whosoever touches them shall be sanctified.
Leviticus 6:12 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Leviticus 6:13 — This is the gift of Aaron and his sons which they shall bring unto the Lord on the day when you anoint him: a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour as a continual sacrifice, half in the morning and half in the evening.
Leviticus 6:14 — It shall be made upon a griddle with oil; he shall bring it mixed, in rolled pieces, a sacrifice of fragments, a sacrifice for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
Leviticus 6:15 — The priest from among his sons who is anointed in his stead shall prepare it. It is an everlasting law; it shall all be fully performed.
Leviticus 6:16 — And every sacrifice of a priest shall be wholly burned, and shall not be eaten.
Leviticus 6:17 — And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Leviticus 6:18 — Speak unto Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the offerings for sin before the Lord; they are most holy.
Leviticus 6:19 — The priest who offers it up shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Testimony.
Leviticus 6:20 — Whosoever touches its flesh shall be sanctified; and if any of its blood is sprinkled upon a garment, what it was sprinkled upon shall be washed in a holy place.
Leviticus 6:21 — And the earthenware vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it and rinse it with water.
Leviticus 6:22 — Every male among the priests shall eat them; they are most holy unto the Lord.
Leviticus 6:23 — And none of the offerings for sin whose blood is brought into the Tent of Testimony to make atonement in the holy place shall be eaten; they shall be burned with fire.

verses.text: And this is the law of the ram for the guilt offering; it is most holy.
In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord; and he shall pour the blood round about upon the base of the altar.
And he shall bring all its fat from it: the loin, and all the fat which covers the inward parts, and all the fat upon the inward parts,
and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver; these he shall remove with the kidneys.
And the priest shall offer them up upon the altar as an offering unto the Lord. It is for guilt.
Every male among the priests shall eat them; they shall eat them in a holy place. They are most holy.
As the offering for sin, so also the guilt offering: one law is theirs. It shall belong unto the priest who makes atonement with it.
And the priest who brings a man’s whole burnt offering shall have the hide of the whole burnt offering which he brings.
And every sacrifice made in an oven, and every sacrifice made upon a hearth or upon a griddle, shall belong unto the priest who brings it.
And every sacrifice prepared with oil, or not so prepared, shall belong unto all the sons of Aaron, unto each an equal share.
This is the law of the sacrifice of deliverance which they shall bring unto the Lord.
If he brings it for praise, he shall bring with the sacrifice of praise loaves of fine flour prepared with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour mixed with oil.
He shall bring his gifts with leavened loaves, with a sacrifice of praise and deliverance.
And he shall bring one of all his gifts as a portion set apart unto the Lord; it shall belong unto the priest who pours the blood of the offering of deliverance.
And the flesh of the sacrifice of praise and deliverance shall be his, and shall be eaten on the day when it is given; they shall leave none of it until morning.
And if he sacrifices his gift as a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day when he brings his sacrifice, and on the morrow.
And what remains of the flesh of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned with fire.

But if he eats any of the flesh on the third day, it shall not be accepted for him who brings it, neither shall it be reckoned unto him; it is a defilement. And the soul that eats of it shall bear the sin.
And flesh which touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. Whosoever is clean shall eat flesh.
But the soul that eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of deliverance which is the Lord’s, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall perish from among his people.

And if a soul touches any unclean thing, human uncleanness, or unclean four-footed beasts, or any unclean abomination, and eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of deliverance which is the Lord’s, that soul shall perish from among his people.

You shall eat no blood in any dwelling place of yours, whether of birds or of livestock.
Every soul that eats blood, that soul shall perish from among his people.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

He among the sons of Aaron who brings the blood of the offering of deliverance and the fat shall have the right foreleg as his portion.

and he shall make atonement for the Holy of Holies, and for the Tent of Testimony and the altar shall he make atonement; and for the priests and for the whole congregation shall he make atonement.

as the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord gave command to you and onward throughout your generations,

And if it happened unintentionally, out of the congregation’s sight, the whole congregation shall prepare one unblemished calf from the cattle as a whole burnt offering of sweet savour unto the Lord, with its sacrifice and drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat for sin.

And the priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, and they shall be forgiven, because it was unintentional. They have brought their gift, an offering unto the Lord for their sin, before the Lord for their unintentional acts.
And forgiveness shall extend throughout the whole congregation of the sons of Israel and to the sojourner attached to you, because it was unintentional for the whole people.
But if one soul sins unintentionally, he shall present one year-old female goat for sin.
And the priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who acted unintentionally and sinned unintentionally, making atonement for that person.
For the native among the sons of Israel, and for the sojourner joined unto them, they shall have one law for whosoever acts unintentionally.
And the soul that acts with a presumptuous hand, whether of the natives or of the sojourners, provokes God; that soul shall be destroyed from his people,
because he treated the word of the Lord as worthless, and scattered His commandments. That soul shall surely be wiped out; his sin is upon him.
And while the sons of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
And those who found him gathering wood on the Sabbath day brought him unto Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
And they placed him in custody, because they had not determined what they should do to him.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying: The man must certainly be put to death. Stone him with stones, all the congregation.
And the whole congregation brought him outside the camp, and the whole congregation stoned him with stones outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord said unto Moses, saying:

Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Let them make for themselves fringes upon the corners of their garments throughout their generations; and you shall put a blue thread upon the fringes of the corners.

And it shall be among your fringes; and you shall see them, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them; and you shall not turn aside after your thoughts and after your eyes, after which you go a whoring,
that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy unto your God.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.

And behold, an expert in the law stood up to test Him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole strength and with your whole mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”
He said to him, “You answered correctly. Do this and you will live.”
But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, inflicted blows, and went away, leaving him half dead.
By coincidence a certain priest was going down that road. He saw him and passed by on the opposite side.
Likewise a Levite also came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the opposite side.
But a certain Samaritan, traveling, came upon him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
He approached and bound his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
On the next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Care for him, and whatever more you spend I will repay you when I return.’
Which of these three seems to you to have become a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”
You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you,
that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Love does no evil to the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
But if one sells property unto your neighbour, or you acquire it from your neighbour, let no man oppress his neighbour.

And behold, an expert in the law stood up to test Him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole strength and with your whole mind, and your neighbor as yourself.”
He said to him, “You answered correctly. Do this and you will live.”
But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
Jesus replied, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, inflicted blows, and went away, leaving him half dead.
By coincidence a certain priest was going down that road. He saw him and passed by on the opposite side.
Likewise a Levite also came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the opposite side.
But a certain Samaritan, traveling, came upon him. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
He approached and bound his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He placed him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.
On the next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Care for him, and whatever more you spend I will repay you when I return.’
Which of these three seems to you to have become a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go, and you do likewise.”
You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you,
that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Love does no evil to the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
But if one sells property unto your neighbour, or you acquire it from your neighbour, let no man oppress his neighbour.
Let no man oppress his neighbour, and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.

verses.text: For when I cast out nations before you, and enlarge your borders, you shall not sacrifice the blood of My offering with leaven, neither shall the fat of My feast remain until morning.
You shall not offer the blood of My offerings with leaven, nor shall the sacrifices of the Passover feast remain until morning.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.text: You shall do no laborious work, and you shall bring a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
And you shall present whole burnt offerings as a sweet savour unto the Lord: one calf from the cattle, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the calf and two tenths for the ram,
and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
And also offer one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you,

besides the whole burnt offerings of the new moon, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, and the continual whole burnt offerings, their sacrifices and their drink offerings, according to their prescription, as a sweet savour unto the Lord.

Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”

He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
