Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

verses.text:
By the command of the Lord the sons of Israel shall camp, and by the command of the Lord they shall set out; all the days in which the cloud overshadows the Tent, the sons of Israel shall camp.
And when the cloud remains over the Tent for many days, the sons of Israel shall keep the charge of God, and shall in no wise set out.
And it shall be, when the cloud covers the Tent for a number of days, that by the voice of the Lord they shall camp, and by the command of the Lord they shall set out.
And it shall be, when the cloud remains from evening until morning, and the cloud rises in the morning, that they shall set out by day or by night.
For the days of a month, while the cloud continues overshadowing it, the sons of Israel shall camp, and shall in no wise set out.
For by the command of the Lord they shall set out. They kept the Lord’s charge, by the command of the Lord through Moses.

verses.text:
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
“This month shall be the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of the year for you.
Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month, each shall take a sheep for the ancestral households, one sheep for each household.
If those in the house are too few to be sufficient for a sheep, he shall join with his nearest neighbour. According to the number of persons, each person’s sufficient portion shall be reckoned for the sheep.
Your sheep shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.
And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; and the whole multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
They shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat them.
They shall eat the meat that night, roasted over fire, and eat unleavened bread with bitter herbs.
You shall eat none of it raw, nor boiled in water, but roasted with fire, its head together with its feet and inward parts.
You shall leave none of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it. Whatever remains until morning you shall burn with fire.
And this is how you shall eat it: your loins girded, your sandals upon your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to the Lord.
I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as a perpetual statute.

Transformed — Passover remembrance in Christ
Connection to Christ: Paul explicitly identifies Christ as our Passover sacrifice; this mark concerns that identification, not the cancellation of every festival custom.
Christian response today: Remember Christ in the Lord’s Supper and live in sincerity and truth, with gratitude for the deliverance the exodus recounts.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 12:1–14 · Exodus 12:43–49 Christ and the apostles: Luke 22:14–20 · 1 Corinthians 5:7–8
Ancient covenant practice: Israel keeps Passover in remembrance of deliverance from Egypt, with its prescribed sacrifice and meal.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Paul identifies Christ as the Passover sacrifice. At the Passover meal Jesus gives the bread and cup in relation to his body, blood and the new covenant; Paul transmits remembrance of the Lord and proclamation of his death.
Saints Translation support: Luke 22:14–20 · 1 Corinthians 5:7–8 · 1 Corinthians 11:23–26
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament identification and institution; festival and sacramental applications differ.

Read carefully: The Fulfilled mark concerns the sacrifice; Transformed concerns Christian remembrance and participation. This does not declare every Passover custom forbidden or erase differences in Eucharistic understanding.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Passover commemorates Israel’s deliverance from Egypt and includes specific household, meal and covenant requirements. Jesus gives the bread and cup their significance in relation to His death; Paul calls Christ our Passover. Christian traditions differ in festival observance. The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the law of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it.
And every man’s household slave, or one bought with silver, you shall circumcise; and then he shall eat of it.
A sojourner or a hired worker shall not eat of it.
It shall be eaten in one house. You shall not take any of the meat outside the house, and you shall not break a bone of it.
The whole congregation of the sons of Israel shall observe it.

But if a resident foreigner comes to you to keep the Passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male belonging to him; and then he shall draw near to keep it, and shall be as the native of the land. No uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
There shall be one law for the native, and for the resident foreigner who has come among you.”
When the hour came, He reclined at table, and the apostles with Him.
And He said to them, “With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
For I tell you that I will certainly not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
And He received a cup, gave thanks, and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
For I tell you, from now on I will certainly not drink from the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”
And He took bread, and having given thanks, He broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
And likewise the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, poured out for you.
Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump of dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed.
So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread,
and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.”
Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.”
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.

And He received a cup, gave thanks, and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
For I tell you, from now on I will certainly not drink from the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”
And He took bread, and having given thanks, He broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
And likewise the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, poured out for you.
Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump of dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed.
So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when He was being handed over, took bread,
and after giving thanks He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.”
Likewise He also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of Me.”
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
“This month shall be the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of the year for you.
Speak to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month, each shall take a sheep for the ancestral households, one sheep for each household.

If those in the house are too few to be sufficient for a sheep, he shall join with his nearest neighbour. According to the number of persons, each person’s sufficient portion shall be reckoned for the sheep.
Your sheep shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.
And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; and the whole multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
They shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat them.
They shall eat the meat that night, roasted over fire, and eat unleavened bread with bitter herbs.
You shall eat none of it raw, nor boiled in water, but roasted with fire, its head together with its feet and inward parts.
You shall leave none of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it. Whatever remains until morning you shall burn with fire.
And this is how you shall eat it: your loins girded, your sandals upon your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to the Lord.
I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as a perpetual statute.

The seventh-day Sabbath is commanded to Israel, with rest extending to workers, animals and resident foreigners. Jesus teaches its human benefit and the lawfulness of doing good. Christians differ about seventh-day observance, Sunday and the continuity of this command. Romans and Colossians must be included when discussing that application.

And He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
Moving on from there, He entered their synagogue.
And behold, a man had a withered hand. They asked Him, “Is it lawful to heal on Sabbaths?” so that they might accuse Him.
He said to them, “Who among you, if he has one sheep and it falls into a pit on a Sabbath, will not grasp it and lift it out?
How much more valuable, then, is a human being than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on Sabbaths.”
For one judges one day above another, but another judges every day alike. Let each be fully assured in his own mind.
The one who regards the day regards it for the Lord. And the one who eats eats for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat refrains for the Lord and gives thanks to God.
Therefore let no one judge you in eating and drinking, or in the matter of a festival or new moon or Sabbaths,
which are a shadow of the things to come, but the body belongs to Christ.

What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Israel is instructed to observe a solemn annual day of rest and self-affliction, with atonement performed by the priest. Hebrews interprets the sanctuary rites through Christ’s once-for-all offering. Christian traditions may commemorate the day differently, but no recurring ritual should be presented as completing an insufficiency in Christ’s sacrifice.

And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement; it shall be a holy convocation unto you, and you shall humble your souls and bring a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
You shall do no work on that very day, for this is a Day of Atonement for you, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
Every soul that shall not be humbled on that very day shall be destroyed from among his people.
And every soul that does work on that very day, that soul shall perish from among his people.
You shall do no work. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
It shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths unto you, and you shall humble your souls; from the ninth day of the month, from evening unto evening, you shall keep your Sabbath.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
For Christ did not enter holy places made by hands, counterparts of the true ones, but heaven itself, now to appear before the face of God on our behalf.
Nor did He enter to offer Himself many times, as the high priest enters the holy places year by year with another’s blood,
for then He would have had to suffer many times since the foundation of the world. But now, once at the end of the ages, He has appeared to set aside sin through His sacrifice.
And just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after this judgment,
so also Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, apart from sin, to those eagerly awaiting Him, for salvation.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.
Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for the One who promised is faithful.
And let us consider one another, to stir up love and good works,
not abandoning our own gathering together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the day drawing near.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Say unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, and reap its harvest, you shall bring a sheaf as the first portion of your harvest unto the priest;
and he shall offer up the sheaf before the Lord, acceptable for you; the priest shall offer it up on the morrow after the first day.
And on the day you bring the sheaf, you shall offer an unblemished year-old sheep as a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
And its sacrifice shall be two tenths of fine flour kneaded with oil, a sacrifice unto the Lord, a sweet savour unto the Lord. Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.
And you shall eat neither bread nor roasted fresh grain until that very day, until you bring the gifts to your God. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.
And you shall count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the presentation, seven complete weeks.
Until the day after the last week you shall count fifty days, and then present a new sacrifice unto the Lord.
From your dwelling you shall bring bread as a presentation, two loaves. They shall be made from two tenths of fine flour and baked leavened, as firstfruits unto the Lord.
And with the loaves you shall bring seven unblemished year-old lambs, one calf from the herd, and two unblemished rams. They shall be a whole burnt offering unto the Lord, with their sacrifices and drink offerings, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And they shall offer one male young goat from the goats for sin and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of deliverance with the firstfruits loaves.
And the priest shall present them with the firstfruits loaves as a presentation before the Lord, with the two lambs. They shall be holy unto the Lord; they shall belong unto the priest who presents them.
And you shall proclaim this day a convocation; it shall be holy for you. You shall do no laborious work on it. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.
And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish the remainder of the harvest of your field when you reap; neither shall you gather what falls from your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and for the resident foreigner; I am the Lord your God.

Connection to Christ: Paul explicitly calls the risen Christ the firstfruits; Acts records the Spirit’s coming at Pentecost. This does not declare every festival detail completed.
Christian response today: Live in resurrection hope and respond to the Spirit; keep firstfruits, the count and Weeks distinct in the Torah calendar.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 23:9–22 Christ and the apostles: Acts 2:1–4 · 1 Corinthians 15:20–23
Text and setting: Israel’s worship
Torah: Leviticus 23:9–22

Leviticus distinguishes the first sheaf, the counting of days and the later Festival of Weeks. Calling them one event erases that sequence. Acts places the Spirit’s coming at Pentecost, and Paul calls the risen Christ the firstfruits. These connections should accompany, rather than replace, the Torah’s actual calendar instructions.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Acts 2:1–4 · 1 Corinthians 15:20–23

Connection and evidence: Explicit New Testament treatment. Paul explicitly calls the risen Christ the firstfruits; Acts records the Spirit’s coming at Pentecost. This does not declare every festival detail completed.

Where interpretations differ: Festival observance; the firstfruits identification itself is explicit in Paul. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in the same place.

Transformed — festival observance in relation to Christ
Connection to Christ: Colossians relates festivals to Christ, but the New Testament does not explicitly identify this date with a completed trumpet event.
Christian response today: Let sacred-day observance lead to worship and gratitude in Christ, with humility toward believers who observe differently.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 23:23–25 · Numbers 29:1 Christ and the apostles: Colossians 2:16–17
Ancient covenant practice: The first day of the seventh month is marked by rest, assembly and trumpet blasts or acclamation.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Colossians warns against judgment over a festival, new moon or Sabbaths and directs attention to Christ. This informs Christian calendar practice without naming a specific event that fulfills this date.
Saints Translation support: Colossians 2:16–17 · Romans 14:5–6
Basis and scope: Christian application of Colossians’ general festival teaching, not an identified fulfillment of this date.
Read carefully: This mark makes no prediction about the date of Christ’s return and does not resolve the separate debate about the weekly Sabbath.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

The Torah calls for a sacred assembly, rest and a memorial of trumpet blasts or acclamation on this date. It does not in these verses name a New Testament event that must occur on the same calendar day. Christian festival practice and prophetic interpretations should be identified as interpretations, not added to the command.

verses.text:
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Tents unto the Lord for seven days.
And on the first day there shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work.
For seven days you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. The eighth day shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. It is a closing observance; you shall do no laborious work.
These are the feasts for the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to present offerings unto the Lord: whole burnt offerings and their sacrifices and their drink offerings, each day’s requirement on its day,
besides the Lord’s Sabbaths, besides your gifts, besides all your vows, and besides your freewill offerings that you give unto the Lord.

of the year. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations; you shall celebrate it in the seventh month.
You shall dwell in tents seven days; every native in Israel shall dwell in tents,
so that your generations may see that I made the sons of Israel dwell in tents when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 23:33–43 Christ and the apostles: John 7:2 · John 7:37–39 · Colossians 2:16–17
Ancient covenant practice: Israel dwells in booths in remembrance of wilderness life and keeps the concluding assembly.

Saints Translation support: John 7:2 · John 7:37–39 · Colossians 2:16–17
Basis and scope: Direct Gospel festival setting and apostolic festival teaching; present observance remains an interpretive question.
Read carefully: John’s connection does not assign a separate completed prophecy to every booth, day or ritual detail. Christians differ in continuing festival practice.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Israel celebrates seven days, dwells in booths in remembrance of the wilderness, and observes an eighth-day assembly. John places Jesus’ teaching about living water at the festival. Christians differ about observance; keep the historical memorial, the eighth-day distinction and the Gospel connection clear.

Connection to Christ: John 4 addresses the place of worship, and Hebrews invites believers to draw near through Christ and continue meeting together.
Christian response today: Gather, worship, encourage one another and give generously; Christian access to God does not depend on making the three ancient sanctuary journeys.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 16:16–17 Christ and the apostles: John 4:21–24 · Hebrews 10:19–25
Ancient covenant practice: Israelite males appear at the chosen sanctuary for the three festivals with gifts according to the blessing received.
Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus teaches worship of the Father in spirit and truth; Hebrews calls believers to draw near through Christ and not neglect assembling together.
Saints Translation support: John 4:21–24 · Hebrews 10:19–25 · 2 Corinthians 9:7
Basis and scope: Direct teaching on access to God and worship location, applied to this pilgrimage law.
Read carefully: Voluntary pilgrimage may still serve devotion. The mark concerns a universal requirement to make these journeys, not a ban on travel or festivals.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Israelite males are instructed to appear at the chosen sanctuary for Unleavened Bread, Weeks and Booths, bringing gifts according to blessing received. This is a sanctuary pilgrimage law. Jesus’ teaching about worship and Hebrews’ invitation to approach God through Christ must be included before describing any Christian obligation to travel to a particular place.

verses.text: Three times in the year shall every male among you appear before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose: in the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and in the Feast of Weeks, and in the Feast of the Pitching of Tents. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty,
but every man according to the ability of your hands, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which He has given you.
Jesus said to her, “Believe Me, woman, an hour is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.
You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.
But an hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father seeks such people to worship Him.
God is spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth.”
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.
Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for the One who promised is faithful.
And let us consider one another, to stir up love and good works,
not abandoning our own gathering together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the day drawing near.
Let each give as he has decided in his heart, not out of sorrow or compulsion; for God loves a cheerful giver.

You shall not plant for yourself a sacred grove, any tree, beside the altar of the Lord your God which you shall make for yourself.

You shall eat no leaven with it; you shall eat unleavened bread with it for seven days, the bread of affliction, for you came forth out of Egypt in haste; that you may remember the day of your departure out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.

and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—

verses.text:
You shall make a lampstand of pure gold, of worked metal. Its stem, branches, bowls, knobs, and lilies shall be made from it.
Six branches shall extend from its sides, three from one side of the lampstand and three from the other.
There shall be three bowls shaped like little nuts, with a knob and lily on one branch. So it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.

There shall be a knob under the two branches extending from it, and a knob under the four branches extending from it; so it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Its knobs and branches shall be made from it, the whole worked from one piece of pure gold.

verses.text:
“You shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of spun fine linen, blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn. You shall make them with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains shall have the same measure.
Five curtains shall be joined to one another, and the other five joined to one another.
You shall make blue loops along the edge of one curtain at the joining side, and do the same along the edge of the outer curtain at the second joining.
You shall make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty along the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains one to another with the clasps; and the tabernacle shall be one.

verses.text:
You shall make hair curtains as a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
Each curtain shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. The eleven curtains shall have the same measure.
You shall join five hair curtains by themselves and six by themselves, and double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tabernacle.
You shall make fifty loops along the edge of the middle hair curtain at the joining, and fifty along the edge of the curtain joining the second set.
You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and fasten the clasps into the loops, and join the hair curtains; and they shall be one.
You shall tuck under the surplus in the tabernacle’s hair curtains. You shall cover over the remaining half curtain; you shall cover over the surplus of the tabernacle’s hair curtains behind the tabernacle.
A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, from the excess length of the tabernacle’s hair curtains, shall cover the tabernacle’s sides on either side.

verses.text:
You shall make posts of decay-resistant wood for the tabernacle.
You shall make each post ten cubits long, and the breadth of each post shall be a cubit and a half.
Each post shall have two tenons fitted opposite each other. You shall make all the tabernacle’s posts this way.
You shall make twenty posts for the tabernacle’s north side.
You shall make forty silver bases for the twenty posts, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the second side, to the south, there shall be twenty posts,
with their forty silver bases, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the rear of the tabernacle, toward the sea, you shall make six posts.
You shall make two posts for the corners at the rear of the tabernacle.
They shall be equal below, and likewise equal at their tops, at one joining. You shall make both this way for the two corners.
There shall be eight posts with sixteen silver bases, two for each post at its two parts, and two for each post.

Each post shall have two tenons fitted opposite each other. You shall make all the tabernacle’s posts this way.
You shall make twenty posts for the tabernacle’s north side.
You shall make forty silver bases for the twenty posts, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the second side, to the south, there shall be twenty posts,
with their forty silver bases, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the rear of the tabernacle, toward the sea, you shall make six posts.
You shall make two posts for the corners at the rear of the tabernacle.
They shall be equal below, and likewise equal at their tops, at one joining. You shall make both this way for the two corners.
There shall be eight posts with sixteen silver bases, two for each post at its two parts, and two for each post.

For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.

who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.

and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.

by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

verses.text:
You shall make a court for the tabernacle. On the side toward the southwest there shall be court hangings of spun fine linen a hundred cubits long on that side,
with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver rings and braces.
Likewise, on the side toward the east there shall be hangings a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the rings, the posts’ braces, and their bases shall be silver-plated.
On the side toward the sea, across the court’s width, there shall be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
Across the court’s width on the south side there shall be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
The hangings on one side shall be fifteen cubits high, with three posts and three bases.

verses.text:
You shall make a holy robe for Aaron your brother, for honour and glory.
Speak to everyone skilled in understanding whom I have filled with a spirit of perception. They shall make Aaron’s holy robe for the sanctuary, in which he shall serve Me as priest.
These are the robes they shall make: a breastpiece, a shoulder-piece, a full-length robe, a tasselled tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy robes for Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests.
They shall take gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
They shall make the shoulder-piece of spun fine linen, the work of a skilled weaving embroiderer.
It shall have two shoulder-pieces joined to one another, fitted at the two sides.
The woven work of the shoulder-pieces upon it shall be made as one piece with it, of the same workmanship: gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen.

verses.text:
You shall make a full-length under-robe entirely blue.
And its neck opening shall be in the midst of it, with a border around the opening, the work of a weaver, its joining woven as one with it, so that it is not torn.
Around the under-robe’s lower hem you shall make little pomegranates like those of a flowering pomegranate tree, of blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen; likewise gold pomegranates, with bells between them all around.
Beside a gold pomegranate there shall be a bell and a floral ornament around the under-robe’s hem.

Fulfilled: This belongs to the earthly sanctuary and its appointed ministry. Hebrews reads that sanctuary in relation to Christ’s priesthood and access to God through Him. Its materials, transport rules and priestly specifications are retained as original instructions, not imposed as a Christian building code.

verses.text: You shall clothe Aaron your brother and his sons with these garments, anoint them, fill their hands, and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
Clothe Aaron in the holy robes, anoint him, and sanctify him, and he shall serve Me as priest.
Anoint them as you anointed their father, and they shall serve Me as priests. They shall have an anointing for priesthood for ever, throughout their generations.”

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

verses.text: And Aaron and his sons shall wear them when they enter into the Tent of Testimony, or draw near to minister at the altar of the sanctuary; and they shall not bring sin upon themselves, lest they die. It shall be an everlasting statute for him and for his seed after him.”

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.

verses.text: “This is what you shall do for them: consecrate them to serve Me as priests. Take one calf from the herd and two rams without blemish,
unleavened loaves mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil. Make them from fine wheat flour.
Put them on one basket and present them on the basket, together with the calf and the two rams.
Take Aaron and his sons, his robes, the anointing oil, the calf for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities, can never perfect those who approach by the same sacrifices offered continually year by year.
Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore, coming into the world, He says, “Sacrifice and offering Thou didst not desire, but a body Thou didst prepare for Me.
In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst take no pleasure.
Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about Me—to do Thy will, O God.’”
After saying above, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin Thou didst not desire or take pleasure in”—which are offered according to law—
He then said, “Look, I have come to do Thy will.” He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.
But this One, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
“This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: putting My laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their mind,”
He adds, “And their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.”
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.

This is what you shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs without blemish each day continually, a continual offering.

verses.text:
You shall make an incense altar of decay-resistant wood.
It shall be square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high, with horns of one piece with it.
You shall overlay its grating, all its walls, and its horns with pure gold, and make a twisted gold rim around it.
You shall make two rings of pure gold beneath its twisted rim, on its two flanks, on the two sides, as holders for the poles used to carry it.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

verses.text: You shall not offer other incense, an offering, or a sacrifice on it; you shall not pour a libation on it.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

Fulfilled: This belongs to the earthly sanctuary and its appointed ministry. Hebrews reads that sanctuary in relation to Christ’s priesthood and access to God through Him. verses.text: “On the first day of the first month, at the new moon, you shall erect the Tent of Testimony.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
