verses.text:
Say unto Aaron: A man from your kin throughout your generations, in whom there is a blemish, shall not draw near to present the gifts of his God.
No man who has a blemish shall approach: a lame man, a blind man, one with a mutilated nose, or one with a cut-off ear;
or a man with a broken hand or a broken foot;
or a hunchback, one with a skin spot, one with diseased eyelids, a man with a severe scab or skin eruption, or one with a single testicle.
No one of the seed of Aaron the priest, in whom there is a blemish, shall draw near to present the sacrifices unto your God; because a blemish is in him, he shall not draw near to present the gifts of God.
He may eat the gifts of God, both the most holy things and portions of the holy things.
But he shall not approach the veil or come near the altar, because he has a blemish. He shall not profane the holy place of his God, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

Topic: Sanctuary, priesthood and ministry

This belongs to the earthly sanctuary and its appointed ministry. Hebrews reads that sanctuary in relation to Christ’s priesthood and access to God through Him. Its materials, transport rules and priestly specifications are retained as original instructions, not imposed as a Christian building code.
Full research entry

verses.text:
Say unto them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your seed who draws near unto the holy things which the sons of Israel consecrate unto the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be destroyed from before Me; I am the Lord your God.
And any man among the seed of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a seminal discharge shall not eat the holy things until he is cleansed. Nor shall one who touches any uncleanness of a person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,
or anyone who touches any unclean creeping creature that defiles him, or a human being who defiles him through any uncleanness of his.
The soul that touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water;
and when the sun sets, he shall be clean; afterward he may eat the holy things, for they are his bread.

verses.text:
They shall not bring anything with a blemish unto the Lord, for it will not be acceptable for you.
And if a man presents a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, specifying a vow by voluntary choice or at your feasts, from the cattle or the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.
They shall not bring unto the Lord an animal that is blind, crushed, has its tongue cut, has warts, a severe scab, or skin eruptions. You shall not place any of these on the altar as an offering unto the Lord.
And you may slaughter for yourself a calf or a sheep with a cut-off ear or a shortened tail; but for your vow it shall not be accepted.
You shall not bring unto the Lord an animal castrated by crushing, or by squeezing out, or by cutting out, or by tearing away; and in your land you shall not do this.
And you shall not present any of these as the gifts of your God from the hand of a foreigner, for there are corruptions in them; they have a blemish. These will not be accepted for you.

and the hangings of the court, the curtain at the gate of the court by the Tent, and the remaining things for all its work.

verses.text: Take the Levites from among the sons of Israel, and you shall purify them.

And you shall do thus unto them for their purification: you shall sprinkle them with water of purification, and a razor shall pass over their whole body, and they shall wash their garments and be clean.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

verses.text: And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.
And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.

Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.

verse_units.text: And the sons of Israel shall camp, each in his own formation and each according to his own command, with their army.

verses.text:
Let the sons of Israel camp, each beside his neighbour, by formation and by the signs of their ancestral houses. The sons of Israel shall camp opposite, around the Tent of Testimony.
And those camping first toward the east shall be the formation of Judah’s camp, with their army. The ruler of the sons of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
His army, those registered, numbered seventy-four thousand six hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Issachar; the ruler of the sons of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-four thousand four hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Zebulun; the ruler of the sons of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Judah, with their army, numbered one hundred eighty-six thousand four hundred. They shall set out first.
The formation of the camp of Reuben, with their army, shall be toward the southwest. The ruler of the sons of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-six thousand five hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Simeon; the ruler of the sons of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Gad; the ruler of the sons of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-five thousand six hundred fifty.
All those registered in the camp of Reuben, with their army, numbered one hundred fifty-one thousand four hundred fifty. They shall set out second.
And the Tent of Testimony and the camp of the Levites shall be raised in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so they shall set out, each beside his neighbour according to command.
The formation of the camp of Ephraim, with their army, shall be toward the sea. The ruler of the sons of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
His army, those registered, numbered forty thousand five hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Manasseh; the ruler of the sons of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His army, those registered, numbered thirty-two thousand two hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Benjamin; the ruler of the sons of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
His army, those registered, numbered thirty-five thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Ephraim, with their army, numbered one hundred eight thousand one hundred. They shall set out third.
The formation of the camp of Dan, with their army, shall be toward the north. The ruler of the sons of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His army, those registered, numbered sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Asher; the ruler of the sons of Asher is Pagiel son of Ocran.
His army, those registered, numbered forty-one thousand five hundred.
And those camping next shall be the tribe of Naphtali; the ruler of the sons of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
His army, those registered, numbered fifty-three thousand four hundred.
All those registered in the camp of Dan numbered one hundred fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They shall set out last, by their formation.

The law permits an altar of earth and specifies unworked stones when a stone altar is built. It addresses Israel’s worship arrangements, not a universal prohibition on tools or worked stone. Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.

verses.text:
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take spices: five hundred shekels of the choicest myrrh, half as much fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty, and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane,
five hundred sanctuary shekels of iris, and a hin of olive oil.
Make these into holy anointing oil, a compound prepared by a perfumer’s skill. It shall be holy anointing oil.
With it anoint the Tent of Testimony and the ark of the testimony,
the lampstand and all its utensils, and the incense altar,
the altar of whole burnt offerings and all its utensils, the table and all its utensils, and the basin and its base.
Consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Everyone who touches them shall be sanctified.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.
Tell the sons of Israel: ‘This shall be holy anointing oil for you throughout your generations.
It shall not be applied to human flesh, and you shall not make anything like it for yourselves according to this composition. It is holy and shall be a holy thing to you.
Whoever makes anything like it, or gives any of it to an outsider, shall be destroyed from among his people.’”

Connection to Christ: Hebrews supplies a broad sanctuary-to-Christ connection, while James describes anointing the sick; neither turns this recipe into a universal Christian formula.
Christian response today: Treat worship reverently and distinguish Israel’s reserved oil from other legitimate uses of oil.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 30:22–33 Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 9:1–14 · James 5:14

The prescribed oil and its formula are reserved for consecrating the sanctuary and its ministers; it must not be reproduced for common use or applied to an unauthorized person. This does not prohibit ordinary skin oils or the anointing of the sick mentioned in James. The sanctuary restriction must retain its particular object and purpose.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 9:1–14 · James 5:14

verses.text:
The Lord said to Moses, “Take to yourself spices: stacte, onycha, fragrant galbanum, and clear frankincense, in equal portions.
They shall make them into incense, a perfumer’s compound, blended, a pure and holy work.
Grind some of it fine and place it before the testimonies in the Tent of Testimony, where I will make Myself known to you. It shall be most holy to you.
You shall not make incense for yourselves according to this composition. It shall be a holy thing to you for the Lord.
Whoever makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall perish from among his people.”

verses.text: The Lord said to Moses, “Take to yourself spices: stacte, onycha, fragrant galbanum, and clear frankincense, in equal portions.
They shall make them into incense, a perfumer’s compound, blended, a pure and holy work.
Grind some of it fine and place it before the testimonies in the Tent of Testimony, where I will make Myself known to you. It shall be most holy to you.
You shall not make incense for yourselves according to this composition. It shall be a holy thing to you for the Lord.
Whoever makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall perish from among his people.”
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through an eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!

Connection to Christ: John identifies Jesus’ body as the temple, and Paul applies temple language to believers; Leviticus itself refers to Israel’s sanctuary and Sabbath.
Christian response today: Honor Christ and care for his people and your body; offer worship and a holy life through him, with reverence in the places where the church gathers.
Saints Translation — Law: Leviticus 19:30 Christ and the apostles: John 2:13–22 · 1 Corinthians 6:19–20
Ancient covenant practice: Leviticus commands reverence for God’s sanctuary within Israel’s worship.

Development in Christ and the apostles: John identifies the temple of which Jesus speaks as his body. Paul applies temple language to the community and to the believer’s body; Peter describes a spiritual house offering spiritual sacrifices through Christ.
Saints Translation support: John 2:19–22 · 1 Corinthians 3:16–17 · 1 Corinthians 6:19–20 · 1 Peter 2:4–5
Basis and scope: Direct New Testament temple imagery; application to this Torah command is interpretive.

Read carefully: The original verse means Israel’s sanctuary. Its accompanying Sabbath command is not automatically relabeled here, and the temple imagery does not make sacred places or Jewish worship contemptible.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

Leviticus commands Sabbath observance and reverence for God’s sanctuary. It does not call an individual body a temple in this verse. John and Paul provide later temple teaching, including Paul’s moral application to the body. That is a Christian connection, not a replacement of the Torah passage’s original referent.

Connection to Christ: Jesus’ teaching in John 4 addresses worship beyond the rival claims of particular mountains; this informs the chosen-sanctuary law.
Christian response today: Worship the Father in spirit and truth through Christ, obey his teaching and gather with fellow believers wherever you live.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 12:8–14 Christ and the apostles: Matthew 7:21–23 · John 4:23–24 · John 4:21–24
Ancient covenant practice: Deuteronomy directs Israel’s offerings to the place God chooses rather than to self-selected sanctuaries.

Development in Christ and the apostles: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman of worship no longer defined by the rivalry between her mountain and Jerusalem. The Father seeks worshipers in spirit and truth; Hebrews describes access through Christ.
Saints Translation support: John 4:21–24 · Hebrews 10:19–25
Basis and scope: Direct teaching of Jesus on worship, applied to the Torah’s chosen-place requirement.
Read carefully: This does not turn worship into doing whatever seems right to oneself, nor does it prohibit churches, pilgrimages or reverence for historic holy places.
What Transformed means · Browse transformed practices

The warning about doing what is right in one’s own eyes occurs here in the transition to worship at the place God chooses. It should not be detached into a prohibition on all individual judgment. Christian obedience likewise requires more than personal sincerity, while Jesus’ teaching about worship must govern the later application.

Exodus 26:1 — “You shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of spun fine linen, blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn. You shall make them with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
Exodus 26:2 — Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains shall have the same measure.
Exodus 26:3 — Five curtains shall be joined to one another, and the other five joined to one another.
Exodus 26:4 — You shall make blue loops along the edge of one curtain at the joining side, and do the same along the edge of the outer curtain at the second joining.
Exodus 26:5 — You shall make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty along the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
Exodus 26:6 — You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains one to another with the clasps; and the tabernacle shall be one.
Exodus 26:7 — You shall make hair curtains as a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
Exodus 26:8 — Each curtain shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. The eleven curtains shall have the same measure.
Exodus 26:9 — You shall join five hair curtains by themselves and six by themselves, and double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tabernacle.
Exodus 26:10 — You shall make fifty loops along the edge of the middle hair curtain at the joining, and fifty along the edge of the curtain joining the second set.
Exodus 26:11 — You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and fasten the clasps into the loops, and join the hair curtains; and they shall be one.

Exodus 26:12 — You shall tuck under the surplus in the tabernacle’s hair curtains. You shall cover over the remaining half curtain; you shall cover over the surplus of the tabernacle’s hair curtains behind the tabernacle.
Exodus 26:13 — A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, from the excess length of the tabernacle’s hair curtains, shall cover the tabernacle’s sides on either side.

verses.text: “You shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of spun fine linen, blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn. You shall make them with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains shall have the same measure.
Five curtains shall be joined to one another, and the other five joined to one another.
You shall make blue loops along the edge of one curtain at the joining side, and do the same along the edge of the outer curtain at the second joining.
You shall make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty along the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and join the curtains one to another with the clasps; and the tabernacle shall be one.
You shall make hair curtains as a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
Each curtain shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. The eleven curtains shall have the same measure.
You shall join five hair curtains by themselves and six by themselves, and double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tabernacle.
You shall make fifty loops along the edge of the middle hair curtain at the joining, and fifty along the edge of the curtain joining the second set.
You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and fasten the clasps into the loops, and join the hair curtains; and they shall be one.

You shall tuck under the surplus in the tabernacle’s hair curtains. You shall cover over the remaining half curtain; you shall cover over the surplus of the tabernacle’s hair curtains behind the tabernacle.
A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, from the excess length of the tabernacle’s hair curtains, shall cover the tabernacle’s sides on either side.
You shall make a covering for the tabernacle of rams’ skins dyed red, with coverings of blue skins above it.
You shall make posts of decay-resistant wood for the tabernacle.
You shall make each post ten cubits long, and the breadth of each post shall be a cubit and a half.
Each post shall have two tenons fitted opposite each other. You shall make all the tabernacle’s posts this way.
You shall make twenty posts for the tabernacle’s north side.
You shall make forty silver bases for the twenty posts, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the second side, to the south, there shall be twenty posts,
with their forty silver bases, two bases for one post at its two parts, and two bases for another post at its two parts.
For the rear of the tabernacle, toward the sea, you shall make six posts.
You shall make two posts for the corners at the rear of the tabernacle.
They shall be equal below, and likewise equal at their tops, at one joining. You shall make both this way for the two corners.
There shall be eight posts with sixteen silver bases, two for each post at its two parts, and two for each post.
You shall make bars of decay-resistant wood, five for the post on one side of the tabernacle,
five for the post on the second side, and five for the rear post on the side toward the sea.
The middle bar shall pass through the middle of the posts from one side to the other.
You shall overlay the posts with gold and make gold rings into which you shall insert the bars. You shall overlay the bars with gold.
You shall erect the tabernacle according to the plan shown to you on the mountain.
You shall make a veil of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
You shall place it on four posts of decay-resistant wood overlaid with gold, with gold capitals and four silver bases.
And you shall set the veil upon the posts, and bring in there, within the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall divide for you between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.
You shall screen the ark of the testimony with the veil in the Holy of Holies.
You shall place the table outside the veil and the lampstand opposite it on the tabernacle’s south side; the table shall be on the north side.
You shall make a screen of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, the work of an embroiderer.
You shall make five posts for the curtain and overlay them with gold, with gold capitals, and cast five bronze bases for them.”

You shall make a bronze grating of network for it, with four bronze rings on its four sides.
You shall place them beneath the altar’s grating, and the grating shall reach halfway up the altar.
You shall make carrying poles of decay-resistant wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.
You shall put the carrying poles through the rings, and they shall lie along the altar’s sides when it is carried.
You shall make it hollow, of boards; as it was shown to you upon the mountain, so you shall make it.
You shall make a court for the tabernacle. On the side toward the southwest there shall be court hangings of spun fine linen a hundred cubits long on that side,
with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver rings and braces.
Likewise, on the side toward the east there shall be hangings a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the rings, the posts’ braces, and their bases shall be silver-plated.
On the side toward the sea, across the court’s width, there shall be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
Across the court’s width on the south side there shall be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
The hangings on one side shall be fifteen cubits high, with three posts and three bases.
On the second side the hangings shall be fifteen cubits high, with three posts and three bases.
For the court’s gate there shall be a covering twenty cubits high, of blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn and spun fine linen, embroidered needlework, with four posts and four bases.
All the posts around the court shall be silver-plated, with silver capitals and bronze bases.
The court’s length shall be a hundred by a hundred, its width fifty by fifty, and its height five cubits, with spun fine linen and bronze bases.
All the equipment, all the tools, and the court’s pegs shall be bronze.
You shall command the sons of Israel to bring you pure beaten olive oil, free of sediment, for the light, so that a lamp may burn continually

in the Tent of Testimony, outside the veil over the covenant. Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening to morning before the Lord, a perpetual statute throughout your generations on behalf of the sons of Israel.”

Exodus 30:1 — You shall make an incense altar of decay-resistant wood.
Exodus 30:2 — It shall be square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high, with horns of one piece with it.
Exodus 30:3 — You shall overlay its grating, all its walls, and its horns with pure gold, and make a twisted gold rim around it.
Exodus 30:4 — You shall make two rings of pure gold beneath its twisted rim, on its two flanks, on the two sides, as holders for the poles used to carry it.
Exodus 30:5 — You shall make the poles of decay-resistant wood and overlay them with gold.
Exodus 30:6 — You shall put it opposite the veil over the ark of the testimonies, where I will make Myself known to you.
Exodus 30:7 — Aaron shall burn finely ground compounded incense upon it morning by morning, when he tends the lamps.

Exodus 32:28 — The sons of Levi did as Moses told them. As many as three thousand men of the people fell that day.
Exodus 32:29 — Moses said to them, “You have filled your hands today to the Lord, each at the cost of his son or brother, that a blessing may be given to you.”

Exodus 40:1 — The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
Exodus 40:2 — “On the first day of the first month, at the new moon, you shall erect the Tent of Testimony.
Exodus 40:3 — You shall place the ark of the testimony and screen the ark with the veil.
Exodus 40:4 — Bring in the table and set out its presentation. Bring in the lampstand and put its lamps on it.
Exodus 40:5 — Place the gold altar for burning incense before the ark, and put a screening veil over the doorway of the Tent of Testimony.
Exodus 40:6 — Place the altar of offerings by the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
Exodus 40:8 — Set the tent about, and sanctify everything belonging to it all around.
Exodus 40:9 — Take the anointing oil and anoint the tent and everything in it. Sanctify it and all its utensils, and it shall be holy.
Exodus 40:10 — Anoint the altar of offerings and all its utensils. Sanctify the altar, and it shall be most holy.
Exodus 40:12 — Bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the Tent of Testimony and wash them with water.
Exodus 40:13 — Clothe Aaron in the holy robes, anoint him, and sanctify him, and he shall serve Me as priest.
Exodus 40:14 — Bring his sons and clothe them in tunics.
Exodus 40:15 — Anoint them as you anointed their father, and they shall serve Me as priests. They shall have an anointing for priesthood for ever, throughout their generations.”
Exodus 40:16 — Moses did everything the Lord had commanded him; so he did.
Exodus 40:17 — In the first month of the second year after they came out of Egypt, at the new moon, the tent was erected.
Exodus 40:18 — Moses erected the tent, placed its capitals, inserted its bars, and erected its pillars.
Exodus 40:19 — He spread the curtains over the tent and placed the tent covering above it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 40:20 — He took the testimonies and put them into the ark, and placed the carrying poles beneath the ark.
Exodus 40:21 — He brought the ark into the tent, put up the screening veil, and screened the ark of the testimony, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 40:22 — He placed the table in the Tent of Testimony, on its north side, outside the tent’s veil.
Exodus 40:23 — He set the bread of the Presence upon it before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 40:24 — He placed the lampstand in the Tent of Testimony, on the south side of the tent.
Exodus 40:25 — He put its lamps in place before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 40:26 — He placed the gold altar in the Tent of Testimony opposite the veil,
Exodus 40:27 — and burned the compounded incense on it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Exodus 40:29 — He placed the altar of offerings by the doors of the tent.
Exodus 40:33 — He erected the court around the tent and the altar. Moses completed all the work.
Exodus 40:34 — The cloud covered the Tent of Testimony, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Exodus 40:35 — Moses could not enter the Tent of Testimony because the cloud overshadowed it and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.

verses.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“On the first day of the first month, at the new moon, you shall erect the Tent of Testimony.
You shall place the ark of the testimony and screen the ark with the veil.
Bring in the table and set out its presentation. Bring in the lampstand and put its lamps on it.
Place the gold altar for burning incense before the ark, and put a screening veil over the doorway of the Tent of Testimony.
Place the altar of offerings by the doors of the Tent of Testimony.
Set the tent about, and sanctify everything belonging to it all around.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the tent and everything in it. Sanctify it and all its utensils, and it shall be holy.
Anoint the altar of offerings and all its utensils. Sanctify the altar, and it shall be most holy.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the Tent of Testimony and wash them with water.
Clothe Aaron in the holy robes, anoint him, and sanctify him, and he shall serve Me as priest.
Bring his sons and clothe them in tunics.
Anoint them as you anointed their father, and they shall serve Me as priests. They shall have an anointing for priesthood for ever, throughout their generations.”
Moses did everything the Lord had commanded him; so he did.
In the first month of the second year after they came out of Egypt, at the new moon, the tent was erected.
Moses erected the tent, placed its capitals, inserted its bars, and erected its pillars.
He spread the curtains over the tent and placed the tent covering above it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He took the testimonies and put them into the ark, and placed the carrying poles beneath the ark.
He brought the ark into the tent, put up the screening veil, and screened the ark of the testimony, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the table in the Tent of Testimony, on its north side, outside the tent’s veil.
He set the bread of the Presence upon it before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the lampstand in the Tent of Testimony, on the south side of the tent.
He put its lamps in place before the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the gold altar in the Tent of Testimony opposite the veil,
and burned the compounded incense on it, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He placed the altar of offerings by the doors of the tent.
He erected the court around the tent and the altar. Moses completed all the work.
The cloud covered the Tent of Testimony, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Moses could not enter the Tent of Testimony because the cloud overshadowed it and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Whenever the cloud rose from the tent, the sons of Israel set out with their belongings.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take Aaron and his sons, his robes, the anointing oil, the calf for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
And assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses did as the Lord directed him, and he assembled the congregation at the door of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses said unto the congregation: This is the word which the Lord commanded to be done.
And Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.

And he clothed him with the tunic, girded him with the belt, clothed him with the under-robe, and put the shoulder-piece on him. He girded him according to the shoulder-piece’s workmanship and fastened him securely in it.
And he placed the oracle-piece on it and put Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece.
And he put the turban on his head and placed on its front the gold plate, the consecrated holy object, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses took some of the anointing oil,

and sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and consecrated it, and all its utensils, the basin and its stand, and consecrated them. He anointed the tent and everything in it and consecrated it.
And Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, clothed them with tunics, girded them with belts, and put turbans on them, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses brought the calf for the sin offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the calf of the sin offering.

And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and put it with his finger all around on the altar’s horns, cleansing the altar. He poured out the blood at the altar’s base and consecrated it, to make atonement upon it.
And Moses took all the fat on the inward parts, the lobe on the liver, both kidneys and the fat on them, and Moses offered them up on the altar.
And he burned up the calf, its hide, its flesh, and its dung with fire outside the camp, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses brought the ram for the whole burnt offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And Moses slaughtered the ram, and Moses poured the blood all around against the altar.
And he divided the ram limb by limb, and Moses offered up the head, the limbs, and the fat.
And he washed the belly and feet with water, and Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar: a whole burnt offering for a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And Moses brought the second ram forward, a ram of consecration, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it upon Aaron’s right earlobe, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.

And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on their right earlobes, the extremities of their right hands, and the extremities of their right feet. Moses poured the blood all around against the altar.
And he took the fat, the loin, the fat on the belly, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the right foreleg.
And from the basket of consecration before the Lord he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and the right foreleg.
And he put everything on Aaron’s hands and his sons’ hands and offered them up as a portion set apart before the Lord.
And Moses took them from their hands, and Moses offered them up on the altar upon the whole burnt offering of consecration, which is a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord.
And Moses took the breast and removed it as a presentation before the Lord from the ram of consecration. It became Moses’ portion, as the Lord commanded Moses.

And Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him. He consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.

And Moses said unto Aaron and his sons: Boil the flesh in the court of the Tent of Testimony, in a holy place, and there you shall eat it, and the loaves in the basket of consecration, as I have been directed, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them.
And what remains of the flesh and loaves shall be burned up with fire.
And you shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Testimony for seven days, until the day is fulfilled, the day of your consecration; for he shall consecrate your hands for seven days.
As he has done this day, the Lord commanded it to be done, to make atonement for you.
And you shall remain at the door of the Tent of Testimony seven days, day and night; you shall keep the charges of the Lord, so that you do not die, for thus the Lord God commanded me.
And Aaron and his sons did all the things the Lord directed Moses.

And they brought what Moses commanded opposite the Tent of Testimony, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the Lord.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Draw near unto the altar, and prepare your offering for sin and your whole burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and your house; and prepare the gifts of the people, and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded Moses.

And he presented the sacrifice, filled his hands with some of it, and placed it on the altar, apart from the morning whole burnt offering.

And if a man eats holy things in ignorance, he shall add a fifth to it and give the holy thing unto the priest.
And they shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel that they set aside for the Lord,
and so bring upon themselves the lawlessness of an offence by eating their holy things, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the congregation of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto them in Israel, who presents his gifts according to any of their pledges or any of their freewill offerings, which they present unto God for a whole burnt offering,
to be acceptable for you, they shall be males without blemish, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
They shall not bring anything with a blemish unto the Lord, for it will not be acceptable for you.

And if a man presents a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, specifying a vow by voluntary choice or at your feasts, from the cattle or the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.

They shall not bring unto the Lord an animal that is blind, crushed, has its tongue cut, has warts, a severe scab, or skin eruptions. You shall not place any of these on the altar as an offering unto the Lord.
And you may slaughter for yourself a calf or a sheep with a cut-off ear or a shortened tail; but for your vow it shall not be accepted.
You shall not bring unto the Lord an animal castrated by crushing, or by squeezing out, or by cutting out, or by tearing away; and in your land you shall not do this.
And you shall not present any of these as the gifts of your God from the hand of a foreigner, for there are corruptions in them; they have a blemish. These will not be accepted for you.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
When a calf, sheep, or goat is born, it shall remain under its mother for seven days. On the eighth day and afterward it may be accepted among the gifts, as an offering unto the Lord.
And you shall not slaughter a cow or a sheep together with her young on one day.
But if you sacrifice a sacrifice, a vow of rejoicing, unto the Lord, you shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable for you.
It shall be eaten that same day. You shall leave none of the flesh until morning. I am the Lord.
And you shall keep My commandments, and do them.
And you shall not profane the name of the Holy One, and I will be sanctified among the sons of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.

And I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the sons of Israel, a gift given unto the Lord, to perform the ministries of the Tent of Testimony.

And you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood in every matter of the altar and within the veil; and you shall perform the ministries, a gift of your priesthood; and the outsider who approaches shall die.

And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance.

And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.
You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.
Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.
All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.
Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.

And everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present unto the Lord, from man unto livestock, shall be yours; but the firstborn of men shall surely be redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock.
And its redemption shall be from one month old; the valuation is five shekels by the holy shekel, which is twenty obols.

But you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves, and the firstborn of sheep, and the firstborn of goats; they are holy. And you shall pour their blood against the altar, and you shall offer up the fat as an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

Every portion of the holy things which the sons of Israel set apart unto the Lord I have given unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance; it is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord for you and for your seed after you.
And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: You shall not inherit in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.
And to the sons of Levi, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an allotment in return for their ministries, the service they perform in the Tent of Testimony.
And the sons of Israel shall no longer approach the Tent of Testimony, incurring a death-bringing sin.

And the Levite himself shall perform the ministry of the Tent of Testimony, and they shall bear their offences. It is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations. Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no inheritance.

For the tithes of the sons of Israel that they set apart for the Lord as a portion set apart I have given to the Levites as an allotment. Therefore I have said to them: Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no allotment.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And you shall speak unto the Levites, and shall say unto them: When you receive from the sons of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for an allotment, you shall take from it a portion set apart unto the Lord, a tithe of the tithe.
And your portions set apart shall be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as a portion set apart from the winepress.

Thus you shall also take of the portions set apart unto the Lord, from all your tithes which you receive from the sons of Israel; and from them you shall give a portion set apart unto the Lord unto Aaron the priest.
From all your gifts you shall take a portion set apart unto the Lord, or from all the firstfruits the consecrated portion thereof.
And you shall say unto them: When you take the firstfruits from it, it shall be reckoned unto the Levites as produce from the threshing floor and as produce from the winepress.
And you shall eat it in every place, you and your households, for it is your wage in return for your ministries in the Tent of Testimony.
And you shall incur no sin through it, when you take the firstfruits from it; and you shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, lest you die.

Its materials, transport rules and priestly specifications are retained as original instructions, not imposed as a Christian building code.
Christ and the apostles: Hebrews 7:11–28 · Hebrews 9:1–12 · Hebrews 10:19–22. Explicit teaching about priesthood and sanctuary; application to its component rules.
Source passages: Leviticus 9:1–24

verses.text: And Moses said unto Aaron: Take unto yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and present them before the Lord.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence for entry into the holy places in the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.

For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily takes place as well.
For the One concerning whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord has sprung from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified, “Thou art a priest for the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For there is a setting aside of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law perfected nothing; and there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And insofar as this was not without an oath—for those became priests without an oath,
but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, “The Lord swore and will not change His mind: Thou art a priest for the age”—
to that extent Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And there were many of those priests, because death prevented them from continuing,
but He, because He remains for the age, has a permanent priesthood.
Therefore He is also able to save completely those who approach God through Him, since He always lives to intercede on their behalf.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens.
He has no daily need, as the high priests do, to offer sacrifices first for His own sins and then for those of the people; for He did this once for all when He offered Himself.
For the law appoints people subject to weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son, perfected for the age.
Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; it is called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

having a golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant, covered on every side with gold. In it were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that had sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now speak of these things in detail.
With these things so arranged, the priests enter the first tent continually, carrying out the acts of worship.
But into the second only the high priest enters, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people’s sins of ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places has not yet been disclosed while the first tent still has its standing.
This is a figure for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience.
They concern only foods, drinks, and various washings: regulations for the flesh, imposed until a time of setting things right.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands—that is, not of this creation—
and entered the holy places once for all, not through the blood of goats and calves but through His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.

by the new and living way He inaugurated for us through the curtain—that is, His flesh—

research.title: Lending without exploiting the needy
paragraphs: Study 36: Lending without exploiting the needy
Related indexed requirements: C0205, C0206. These links indicate overlapping passages; they do not assert that every requirement is identical to the study’s subject.
Connection to Christ: Jesus teaches generous lending; applying Israel’s interest provisions to modern banking requires further interpretation.
Christian response today: Lend mercifully and refuse to profit by exploiting another person’s desperation.
Saints Translation — Law: Exodus 22:24 (KJV 22:25) · Deuteronomy 23:20–21 (KJV 23:19–20) Christ and the apostles: Luke 6:34–35
Text and setting: Economic law
Torah: Exodus 22:24 (KJV 22:25) · Deuteronomy 23:20–21 (KJV 23:19–20)

Exodus prohibits charging interest to the poor among God’s people; Deuteronomy distinguishes lending to an Israelite brother and to a foreigner. Those distinctions should be stated rather than omitted. Jesus teaches generosity in lending. Christian judgments about modern banking vary; the text clearly opposes exploiting need for personal advantage.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Luke 6:34–35
Connection and evidence: Related New Testament teaching. Jesus teaches generous lending; applying Israel’s interest provisions to modern banking requires further interpretation.
These passages support a related teaching or moral application. The connection is not presented as a direct quotation of this exact Torah rule.

Where interpretations differ: Interest, usury and applications to modern banking. Read the biblical passages together and distinguish a tradition’s conclusion from the wording of the text. Compare interpretive approaches.

Topic: Wages, lending, pledges and inheritance
Original scope: Text and setting: Civil and land law

Connection to Christ: Galatians speaks of shared inheritance in Christ; this theological connection is not a replacement civil inheritance code. Christian response today: Treat family members fairly and distinguish spiritual inheritance from the details of lawful estate arrangements.
Full research entry
wording_notes: This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

citations.role: Read with Christ and the apostles

verses.text:
And the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, of the clan of Manasseh among the sons of Joseph, came forward. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
And they stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the rulers, and the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony, saying:
Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the congregation that rose against the Lord in Korah's congregation; he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
Let our father's name not be erased from his clan because he has no son. Give us a possession among our father's brothers.
And Moses brought their case before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among their father’s brethren, and shall assign their father’s allotment unto them.
And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a man dies, and has no son, you shall assign his inheritance unto his daughter.
But if he has no daughter, you shall give the inheritance to his brother.
But if he has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brother.
But if his father has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his nearest relative from his tribe, and he shall inherit his property. This shall be a rule of judgment for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.

Saints Translation — Law: Numbers 27:1–11 · Numbers 36:6–9 Christ and the apostles: Galatians 3:28–29
Text and setting: Civil and land law

The daughters of Zelophehad bring a claim, and the law supplies an inheritance order when a man has no son, alongside tribal land provisions. This is a particular Israelite legal system, not a complete modern estate-planning code. Galatians’ language of shared inheritance in Christ is a theological development, not a repeal of every civil inheritance arrangement.
Read with Christ and the apostles: Galatians 3:28–29

title: Seventh-year release and provision for freed servants
audience_note: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
original_scope: Text and setting: Economic and civil law
paragraphs: Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.
Classification: Study context · Topical study
Topic: Wages, lending, pledges and inheritance
Original scope: Text and setting: Economic and civil law

Connection to Christ: Jesus teaches generous lending, and Philemon calls for receiving Onesimus as a beloved brother; these guide Christian reflection on release and dignity. Christian response today: Show mercy in debt and labor relationships without treating the ancient regulation of servitude as permission to own people.
Full research entry
wording_notes: This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

citations.role: Read with Christ and the apostles
Read with Christ and the apostles

verses.text:
At the end of seven years you shall make a release.
And this is the ordinance of the release: you shall release every debt of yours which your neighbour owes you; and you shall not exact it of your brother, for a release unto the Lord your God has been proclaimed.
Of a foreigner you may exact whatsoever he owes you; but you shall release your brother’s debt unto you.
For there shall be none in need among you; for the Lord your God shall surely bless you in the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession, to inherit it,
if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all these commandments which I command you this day.
For the Lord your God has blessed you, as He has spoken unto you; and you shall lend unto many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.
And if there is among you one of your brethren in need, within any of your cities in the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not withhold the affection of your heart, neither shall you close your hand against your needy brother.
You shall freely open your hands unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs, according to his want.
Take heed unto yourself, lest there be a hidden, lawless thought in your heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, draws near; and your eye be evil toward your needy brother, and you give him nothing, and he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be great sin upon you.
You shall freely give unto him, and shall surely lend him as much as he needs; and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him. For because of this the Lord your God shall bless you in all your works, and in all that you put your hand unto.
For the needy shall never cease out of the land; therefore I command you to do this thing, saying: You shall freely open your hands unto your poor brother and unto the needy in your land.
And if your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold unto you, he shall serve you six years; and in the seventh year you shall send him forth free from you.
And when you send him forth free from you, you shall not send him away empty.
You shall furnish him generously out of your sheep, and out of your grain, and out of your winepress; as the Lord your God has blessed you, you shall give unto him.

Connection to Christ: Jesus teaches generous lending, and Philemon calls for receiving Onesimus as a beloved brother; these guide Christian reflection on release and dignity.
Christian response today: Show mercy in debt and labor relationships without treating the ancient regulation of servitude as permission to own people.
Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 15:1–18 Christ and the apostles: Luke 6:34–36 · Philemon 1:15–17
Text and setting: Economic and civil law

Deuteronomy regulates release of debts among fellow Israelites and the release and furnishing of Hebrew servants, with stated exceptions and procedures. It is not an undifferentiated cancellation of every debt worldwide. Christian application should attend to mercy, freedom and dignity, without treating the ancient regulation of servitude as a command to own people.

My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with acts of favoritism.
For if a man with gold rings and splendid clothing enters your gathering, and a poor person in filthy clothing also enters,
and you pay attention to the one wearing splendid clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” but say to the poor person, “You stand, or sit there beneath my footstool,”
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
But you have dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into courts?
Do they not blaspheme the good name called over you?
If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.

Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
But you have dishonored the poor person. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into courts?
Do they not blaspheme the good name called over you?
If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
But if you show favoritism, you commit sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
And if a man has two wives, one loved and one hated, and both the loved and the hated bear him children, and the firstborn son is hers that is hated,
then it shall be, in the day when he gives his sons an inheritance of his possessions, that he may not make the son of the loved wife the firstborn, overlooking the firstborn son of the hated wife.

But he shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the hated wife, by giving him a double portion of all that he has; for he is the beginning of his children, and the right of the firstborn belongs unto him.

Connection to Christ: Paul explicitly quotes the unmuzzled-ox command to support material provision for gospel workers.

Saints Translation — Law: Deuteronomy 25:4 Christ and the apostles: 1 Corinthians 9:8–14 · 1 Timothy 5:17–18

verses.text: You shall not muzzle an ox when it treads out the grain.
Am I saying these things merely in a human way, or does not the law also say them?
For in the law of Moses it is written, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it threshes.” Is it oxen that concern God,
or does He surely say it for our sake? For it was written for our sake, because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher in hope of sharing.
If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap your material things?
If others share in this right over you, do we not all the more? But we did not use this right; instead, we bear everything so that we may put no hindrance in the way of the good news of Christ.
Do you not know that those who perform the sacred duties eat what comes from the temple, and those who attend the altar share with the altar?
In the same way, the Lord directed those who proclaim the good news to live from the good news.
Let the elders who lead well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in word and teaching.
For Scripture says, “You shall not muzzle an ox that threshes,” and, “The worker is worthy of his wage.”

“When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not recline in the foremost place. Someone more honored than you may have been invited by him,
and the one who invited you both will come and say to you, ‘Give this man your place.’ Then you will begin, with shame, to occupy the last place.

But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have honor before all who recline at table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

You will give the Levitical priests who are of Zadok’s offspring and draw near to Me to minister to Me, says the Lord God, a calf from the cattle as an offering for sin.
They will take some of its blood and put it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of the place of atonement, and on the base all around. They will make atonement for it.
They will take the calf for the sin offering, and it will be burned in the separated area of the house, outside the holy places.
On the second day they will take two unblemished goat kids for sin, and they will make atonement for the altar as they made atonement with the calf.
After you have completed the atonement, they will bring an unblemished calf from the cattle and an unblemished ram from the sheep.
You all will bring them before the Lord, and the priests will throw salt upon them and offer them as burnt offerings to the Lord.
For seven days you will prepare a kid for sin each day, and a calf from the cattle and a ram from the sheep. They will prepare unblemished animals—
—for seven days. They will make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and they will fill their hands.
From the eighth day onward, the priests will offer your burnt offerings and your offerings for well-being on the altar. I will accept you, says the Lord.”

verses.text:
You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall not commit adultery.’
But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna.

Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall fulfil your oaths to the Lord.’
But I tell you: do not swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God,
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of His feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let your word be ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever is beyond these is of evil.

verses.text:
You have heard that it was said: ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
But I tell you: do not resist the evildoer; but whoever strikes you upon your right cheek, turn the other to him also.
And if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak also.
And whoever compels you to go one Roman mile, go with him two.
Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who would borrow from you.

verses.text:
You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you,
that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
